s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_count.tableComment: County-level death counts and rates for drug overdose, suicide, homicide, and firearm injury, from CDC's Mapping Injury, Overdose, and Violence (MIOV) tool. Both yearly and trailing-twelve-month periods. Currently updated. Complements cdc_county_overdose_deaths with suicide/homicide/firearm categories. Counts of 1-9 are suppressed for privacy (see count_sup); for those counties CDC publishes a Bayesian small-area model estimate in rate instead of a crude rate, flagged by rate_m=true with its credible interval in rate_m_ci. rate is therefore a crude rate where rate_m is false and a model estimate where rate_m is true, so a population-weighted rate over many counties blends the two. rate is NULL only where CDC publishes no estimate at all. year is the observation year: the calendar year for a Yearly row (2019 onward), and for a trailing-twelve-months row the year in which the window ends (ttm_date_range, e.g. June 2025 to May 2026 is 2026), so filter period to the four-digit rows for like-for-like annual comparisons.

Maps table-specific line codes (key) to their descriptions (desc) for the 56 tracked BEA Regional tables (SAINC*, SQINC*, CAINC*, SAGDP*, SQGDP*, CAGDP* series). s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/ces_revisio.tableComment: BLS's own CES revision-vintage product (cesvinall.zip: "as originally published" vintages for every monthly Employment Situation release since May 2003) — the revision/vintage history that employment_statistics does not carry (each row there is only the CURRENT, most-revised value; this table lets a caller see what a series looked like as first published vs. after subsequent revisions). One row per (series, release, reference_period): release_year/release_month identify which monthly Employment Situation release this vintage snapshot is from; reference_year/ reference_month identify which data month the value describes; value is that release's published estimate for that data month (thousands of employees, CES convention). Comparing rows with the same series_id + reference_period across different release_period values shows the revision path for that data month — including the annual February benchmark revision, which is simply a jump in value for prior-year reference months between the January and February releases; no second QCEW source is needed to see it. PARTIAL/SCOPED BUILD BY DESIGN, in two ways: (1) series scope — the source ZIP carries 113 CES industry codes (226 SA/NSA files); only 4 are loaded — total nonfarm (CES/CEU0000000001), total private (CES/CEU0500000001), goods-producing (CES/CEU0600000001), and service-providing (CES/CEU0700000001) — not the 58+ deeper industry-detail series. (2) reference- period window — BLS's own file melts to the FULL 1939-present history in every release row (1000+ columns), but reference months more than a few years old are permanently frozen (never revised again) by the time they age out of BLS's own benchmark-revision reach, so repeating them in every subsequent vintage is pure duplication with zero revision signal; each release here keeps only its most recent 73 reference months (~6 years) — see CesRevisionVintagesTransformer javadoc for the exact windowing logic. Widening either scope later only requires editing that transformer's target-code set / window size, not re-deriving the source. series_id is reconstructed from the ZIP's filename industry_code (see column comment) since the file itself never spells out the full BLS series ID.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/phmsa_.tableComment: PHMSA gas transmission & gathering operators' annual report (Form PHMSA F 7100.2-1), Part A-D fields, one row per (report_year, operator, commodity) — the per-mile normalization denominator for phmsa_gas_transmission_incidents (join on operator_id + report_year). Same data.transportation.gov bulk-file route as phmsa_hazardous_liquid_mileage (catalog resource aemm-7pyq, the same multi-commodity "href" pointer; this fetches the Gas Transmission & Gathering file attachment). The source ZIP splits each year's annual report into ~12-14 "Part" CSVs (Part A-D, F-G, H, I, ... T); only the Part A-D file is ingested here, since it alone carries total_miles (Part D) and the HCA mileage summary (Part B) — the fields this warehouse needs. Confirmed identical column layout (154 cols) across 2017-2024. Unlike the gas distribution and hazardous-liquid annual reports, this form has no Part E installation-decade mileage breakdown at all (confirmed: no PARTE-prefixed columns anywhere in the 2024 zip), so miles_installed_* columns are not carried here. total_miles (PARTDTOTALMILES) is the sum of separately-reported transmission-only and gathering-only mileage (PARTDTTOTAL + PARTDGTOTAL, confirmed live), both also captured here since the two pipeline types differ operationally and are usually analyzed separately. Confirmed live: comma-only padding lines exist here too (1-16 per year, fewer than the other annual reports but the same defect), requiring the same OPERATOR_ID rowFilter. An operator can file more than one commodity row per year (Natural Gas, Landfill Gas, Hydrogen Gas, and assorted "Other Gas-*" industrial gases), so report_number is the unique key, not operator_id + report_year. 2010-2016 exist only as whole-workbook XLSX files (one per year, sheet "GT AR Part A to D") rather than separate per-year Part-CSVs; a PhmsaGasTransmissionMileageHistoricalTransformer responseTransformer parses those years via POI and appends them to the 2017+ CSV text extractPattern already produces, so this table now covers 2010-present. Confirmed live: the 2010-2011 workbooks carry only 116 columns (vs. 154 for 2012+), but every target field this table ingests is present for the whole 2010-2016 span — the narrower layout only drops columns this table never used anyway.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/research/nih_pub.tableComment:
Long-format (appl_id, pmid) publication links from RePORTER's POST /v2/publications/search API — one row per funded-project/publication pair per fiscal year, joinable back to nih_award_projects.appl_id. Closes the funding-to-output gap: nih_award_projects, nsf_federal_rd_obligations, and nsf_herd_by_institution all carry funding totals or award-level funding size, but none carries an output measure to compute a genuine agency-funding-volatility-vs-research-output relationship.
RePORTER's publications endpoint takes a batch of appl_ids as its criteria rather than a year/agency filter directly, so this table's provider first re-walks /v2/projects/search for the same (year, agency_ic) slice nih_award_projects uses (fetching only appl_id, not the full award record) to get that slice's appl_id population, then batches those appl_ids (500 per call, RePORTER's own page-size convention) into /v2/publications/search calls.
**Cross-linked appl_id filtering**: the publications response's applid field is not necessarily one of the appl_ids just queried — confirmed live, a batch of FY2023/FIC appl_ids surfaced a linked FY2025/NHGRI appl_id in the same response (a renewal-year continuation of the same underlying project, credited on the same publication). Rows are kept only when applid is a member of the batch queried, so every row's fiscal_year/slice is guaranteed accurate; the cross-linked appl_id is captured correctly when its own (year, agency_ic) slice is walked instead.
**Two different years**: the /v2/publications/search response carries no year field, so fiscal_year is the *funding* fiscal year of the (year, agency_ic) slice being walked, i.e. when the underlying grant was active. The paper's own year is pub_year, looked up from NIH iCite (/api/pubs?pmids=, field year); it is null for a pmid iCite does not index. A paper appears against every fiscal_year its funding project spanned, and RePORTER credits a renewed project's whole publication history to each of its appl_ids — so counting links by fiscal_year measures accumulated portfolio output, not output produced that year. For a publication-output series count DISTINCT pmid grouped by pub_year (and by agency_ic via nih_award_projects.appl_id when institute attribution is needed).
**Scope**: NIH only. NSF's publication linkage is an inline field (`publicationResearch`) on its own Award API record rather than a separate paginated endpoint and needs its own extraction pass — tracked as follow-on work, not this table. Patent linkage (NIH-award-to-patent) has no public RePORTER/iCite endpoint at all; USPTO PatentsView plus a government-interest-clause parse would be a genuinely separate, harder build.
Scoped to a recent-years trend window (FY2022+) rather than RePORTER's full FY1985+ history — lower minYear on the year dimension to reach further back.

Complements acs_housing_tenure's median_year_built: a median only tells you 50% of units are older/newer than itself, not the share relative to an arbitrary threshold (e.g. "percent of housing stock built before 1980") — these brackets answer that directly. Verified live 2026-09-11: bracket sum matches the table's own total exactly (Bronx County NY, 2023 ACS5); pre-1939 share is far higher in an established Northeast county (Nantucket MA ~17%) than a Sun Belt boomtown (Maricopa AZ ~1%), matching known housing-stock-age geography. Tract-grain is NOT included — this codebase's declarative ACS infrastructure has no per-county tract fan-out mechanism; state and county grain only (see all_geographies).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cms_pbj_n.tableComment: CMS Payroll-Based Journal (PBJ) "Daily Nurse Staffing" (data.cms.gov catalog entry "Payroll Based Journal Daily Nurse Staffing"), one row per facility (PROVNUM — joins to cms_nursing_home.ccn) per calendar day (work_date), with hours split by nursing role (RN Director of Nursing, RN admin, staff RN, LPN admin, staff LPN, CNA, nurse-aide-in-training, medication aide) and further split employee vs. contract. Fills the gap cms_nursing_home leaves: that table carries only a current-snapshot hours-per-resident-day ratio with no history, this table is the underlying daily time series a staffing trend needs — divide any hrs_*/resident_census pair for a per-resident-day rate on any day or rolled-up period. Quarterly releases back to 2017Q1 (~37 quarters as of 2026Q1); each quarter is a separate, independently-hosted CSV with no derivable URL pattern, so this table is built by catalog discovery rather than a templated URL (see the provider class comment). Verified live 2026-09-27: 2017Q1-Q4 name the RN-director and LPN-admin total columns hrs_rn_donadmin/hrs_lpn_admin instead of the hrs_rndon/hrs_lpnadmin used from 2018Q1 on — both aliased to the same output column by the provider. The 2017Q2 file itself has a malformed header (no hrs_medaide_ctr column; a stray duplicate hrs_rn_donadmin token appears in its place) — medication_aide_hours_contract is null for that one quarter, not a defect in this pipeline. Large: ~237MB per quarter CSV, full history is a multi-GB backfill.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/wdfw_s.tableComment: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife Salmonid Population Indicators (SPI, the SCoRE / State of Our Salmon data): annual adult spawner and escapement estimates for wild and hatchery salmon, steelhead, bull trout and cutthroat stocks across Washington (Puget Sound, coast, Columbia basin), one row per stock x data series x year x data_type, 1938 to the latest completed return year. Species are Chinook, Coho, Chum, Pink, Sockeye, Steelhead, Bull Trout and Cutthroat. abundance_qty is a count of fish (or redds where data_type is 'Spawner Redds'); data_type says what is counted (Spawner Fish, Escapement Fish, Spawner Redds, or the SPI codes NOSAEJ natural-origin spawners, HOSAEJ hatchery-origin spawners, TSAEJ total spawners; IJ variants include jacks, EJ exclude them), production_type is Natural / Hatchery / Composite and calculation_type is Expanded / Unexpanded. A stock can appear under several data_types and series, so filter to one data_type (and production_type) before summing or comparing years; do not add across data_types. The state is always WA (state_abbr); this is the stock-level counterpart to dart_adult_counts (dam passage) and adfg_fish_counts (Alaska). s3://govdata-parquet-v1/housing/building.tableComment:
Census Building Permits Survey — new privately-owned residential construction authorized by building permits, at PLACE (incorporated city/town/village) grain, annual. One row per place per year with buildings/units/valuation for 1-unit, 2-unit, 3-4-unit and 5-plus-unit structures (Census's imputed totals, the canonical series). This is the grain municipal housing policy is actually made at: zoning, permitting and approval decisions are a city function, and the county-grain building_permits table sums across every jurisdiction in a county plus its unincorporated area, so it cannot separate a permissive city from a restrictive neighbour. Roughly 20,000 rows per year across the four regional files, available back to 1980.
GRAIN — one row per permit-issuing jurisdiction per county part per year. The unique key is (state_fips, place_fips, mcd_fips, county_fips, year); place_geoid alone is NOT a key. Two things break the naive one-row-per-place assumption. First, a jurisdiction straddling a county line is reported once per county it falls in. Second, and much larger: most rows nationally are NOT identified by place at all — in strong-MCD states (PA, MA, NJ, NY, ...) the permit-issuing jurisdiction is a township or town carried in the MCD field, and those rows have place_fips 00000. Chester County PA alone reports 57 townships that way. Use jurisdiction_type to tell which identity a row carries — 'place' (place_geoid set), 'mcd' (mcd_geoid set), 'unincorporated' (a county's leftover unincorporated area, the 99990 sentinel, also flagged by is_unincorporated_area), or 'county' (a county-wide permit office). place_geoid and mcd_geoid are populated ONLY where a real code backs them, never synthesised from a sentinel, so a join on either cannot silently merge distinct jurisdictions. Filter to jurisdiction_type='place' to compare municipalities; keep every type to reconcile against the county-grain building_permits table — but expect an exact match only for recent years. Census's place and county products do not fully agree on older vintages: 2023 and 2024 reconcile to the unit, while 2009-2022 and 2025 differ by up to 0.8% (2013: 625,225 place units against 620,785 county). Both tables here match their own source file to the row (verified against fresh downloads), so that gap is upstream, in how Census aggregates and imputes at each grain — not an ingestion difference. Treat the county table as authoritative for county totals and this one for within-county composition, rather than expecting either to be derivable from the other. months_reported says how many of the year's 12 months the jurisdiction actually reported — the rest is imputed, which matters more here than at county grain because one small jurisdiction's silence is not averaged away. Source: www2.census.gov/econ/bps/Place/{region}/{prefix}{year}a.txt.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: FHWA bridge-specific award-level grants from USAspending — one row per award, with recipient, dollar amount, performance period, and recipient location (county-grain via county_fips; state_abbr supports GROUP BY state totals). Covers the IIJA Bridge Formula Program (CFDA 20.263, formula funds apportioned to every state DOT for bridge replacement/rehabilitation) and the discretionary Bridge Investment Program (CFDA 20.264, competitive large -bridge awards). DQ-validated 2026-09-14: real large bridge projects (e.g. CFDA 20.263's Vincent Thomas Bridge deck replacement in Los Angeles County CA, $152.6M; CFDA 20.264's Brent Spence Bridge Corridor OH/KY, $400M). recipient_name/state_abbr/county_fips are the state DOT's registered address, not necessarily the bridge's physical location — the same convention as this table's sibling USAspending award tables (broadband_reconnect_awards, broadband_arra_awards); the award description usually names the specific bridge/corridor. Closes the program-level counterpart to usaspending_by_state (which carries only an undifferentiated per-state total with no program breakdown): filtering this table to cfda_number = '20.263' isolates Bridge Formula Program dollars per state, the gap this table was built for. A full crawl each run (not year-partitioned): the award-search endpoint has no reliable date-filter parameter that matches how award records are dated (obligation vs. performance-start vary by award), and the result set is small enough (low thousands of awards across both CFDA numbers, DQ-confirmed: 3,380 for 20.263 + 33 for 20.264) that a full refresh is cheap. The Competitive Highway Bridge Program (CFDA 20.267) and Competitive Type 3 Highway Bridge Program (20.198) exist in the CFDA catalog but had zero awarded grants as of 2026-09-14 — not included here; add them if/when they start awarding. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (program_numbers filter, award types 02/03/04/05 — grants only, no contracts/loans in either program).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fec/committee_co.tableComment: Committee-to-candidate transactions (PACs, party committees), spanning direct contributions and coordinated/independent spending via transaction_type codes (24K=direct contribution, 24C=coordinated party expenditure, 24E=independent for, 24A=independent against, 24F=communication cost for). Each row carries a candidate_id, distinguishing it from intercommittee_transactions (committee-to-committee transfers with no candidate link). Source: pas2{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header). DIRECTION: committee_id is the DONOR/filing committee (the PAC or party committee that made this expenditure — join fec.committees on committee_id + year for its name/type/connected organization); contributor_name and other_id both identify the RECIPIENT (candidate's authorized committee) — contributor_name is its name despite the field's name, other_id is its FEC committee ID (join fec.committees on other_id + year for the recipient's own details), and candidate_id is the recipient candidate. amount is signed per transaction_type — a negative value is a refund/adjustment against a prior contribution, not new money moving; net (don't just sum) amount when computing a total given/received. PERFORMANCE: always filter on the year partition — an aggregate filtered only by candidate_id (or any other non-partition column) across all years can exceed a 30s query timeout.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/patents/patent_a.tableComment:
To reach a patent assignee FROM a company rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on patents_assignee_id = assignee_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so a firm's SEC CIK and its patent assignee id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching assignee_organization as text finds the wrong entities and misses subsidiaries filing under unrelated names.
Faithful recreation of g_assignee_disambiguated.tsv — one row per patent-assignee combination (assignee_organization or first/last name, assignee_type, assignee_sequence), keyed by patent_id, no joins and no year. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row). location_id is the foreign key into patent_locations for geography.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/cps_votin.tableComment:
State-level reported voting and registration rates for the citizen voting-age population, from the Census Bureau's Current Population Survey (CPS) Voting and Registration Supplement — a biennial November survey module (even years only: congressional and presidential election years), not part of the ACS and not on the acs5 endpoint. The CPS API (api.census.gov/data/{year}/cps/voting/nov) returns person-level survey microdata (one row per respondent, with person weight PWSSWGT), not a pre-tabulated table, so this table is a weighted state-level aggregation of that microdata computed by CpsVotingSupplementTransformer: voted_rate_pct / registered_rate_pct are the population-weighted share of respondents answering "Yes" to PES1 (did you vote?) / PES2 (registered to vote?), among respondents who gave a Yes/No answer (excluding "Not in Universe", "Refused", "Don't Know"). population_reported_voted / population_reported_registered are the weighted denominators (the estimated citizen voting-age population that answered the question); sample_size_voted / sample_size_registered are the unweighted respondent counts backing each estimate, for margin-of-error context. Available biennially from 1996 (the earliest api.census.gov vintage for this dataset with PES1/PES2 variable coding stable through the most recent cycle — the November 1994 file predates api.census.gov and used different variable codes, PES3/PES4, for the same two questions, so 1994 is not in this table).
CAUTION for turnout-gap or turnout-rate comparisons across states: this table is SELF-REPORTED turnout among the citizen voting-age population, known to systematically OVER-REPORT relative to actual counted votes (social-desirability bias) — it is NOT voting-eligible population (VEP), the standard denominator the turnout literature actually uses (Cantoni & Pons; McDonald/US Elections Project). For any question comparing turnout RATES between groups of states (e.g. by a policy like voter-ID requirements), prefer pairing real certified vote totals (e.g. officials.presidential_election_results or an equivalent FEC/certified- results table) with a VEP-style population denominator instead of this table's self-reported rate — this table alone will overstate turnout by roughly 10 points and can misstate a gap's size even when the direction is right.

Currently updated. Each row is one jurisdiction x reporting month x indicator, and the period is a 12-month-ending window: a row is the count over the twelve months ending in its year and month, not that single month. Indicators are counts by ICD-10 drug class (all opioids T40.0-T40.4/T40.6, natural and semi-synthetic opioids T40.2, methadone T40.3, synthetic opioids excluding methadone T40.4 which is where illicit fentanyl sits, heroin T40.1, cocaine T40.5, psychostimulants T43.6) plus total deaths, total drug overdose deaths and the percent of deaths with a drug specified. Drug-class counts overlap because one death can involve several drugs, so do not sum them. Jurisdictions are the 50 states, DC, PR, the national total ('US') and New York City ('YC'). State of occurrence, not residence; for county residence see cdc_county_overdose_deaths, and for national counts by named drug (fentanyl, xylazine, oxycodone and others) see cdc_drug_overdose_deaths_by_drug.

Uses dimension resolver to handle NAICS version differences: - 2017: Uses NAICS2017 variable - 2022: Uses NAICS2022 variable Partitioned by year only (not geography) to reduce file count. For annual (non-quinquennial) county-level establishment counts, employment, and payroll by NAICS — no sales — see cbp_establishments. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ref/gleif_relati.tableComment: GLEIF Level 2 relationship records — the LEI-to-LEI edges that LEI-CDF (gleif_entities) does not carry. One row per directed relationship. Both endpoints are always LEIs, so the table self-joins to gleif_entities on either side and, through gleif_cik_mapping, resolves to SEC CIKs. relationship_type values (2026-07-31 publish, 482,849 rows): IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY (126,021) and IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY (132,196) are the two levels of the ownership hierarchy; IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY (148,576), IS_SUBFUND_OF (72,731), IS_FEEDER_TO (1,386) are fund structures; IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF (1,939) is branch registration. In every type start_node_id is the subordinate entity and end_node_id is the superior one — but only consolidation means ownership. A fund commonly carries a manager AND an umbrella (59,419 entities; the two are different entities in 60,266 of 60,370 cases): two distinct relations, not two parents. GLEIF flattens the ownership chain to two attested levels and never publishes the intermediate one, so IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY is largely derivable — walking the direct chain reaches the declared ultimate for 113,860 of the 118,627 entities that report both. It is kept because it is REPORTED, not computed: 13,569 entities declare an ultimate with no direct edge to walk from, and 4,765 chains break at an intermediate holding company that has no LEI. Dropping it loses those ~18k attestations. Only entities that report a relationship to GLEIF appear here — an absent edge means "not reported", which the REPEX (reporting exception) publish explains and this table does not carry. Source: GLEIF Golden Copy RR (goldencopy.gleif.org).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/fas_export_sa.tableComment: USDA FAS Export Sales Reporting (ESR) — weekly net sales, outstanding sales, shipments, and marketing-year total commitment by commodity and destination country, published every Thursday. year is the FAS marketYear (not calendar year; marketing-year start month varies by commodity — e.g. corn/soybeans start September 1, wheat starts June 1). One row per commodity x country x week_ending_date. weekly_exports is that week's physical shipments; accumulated_exports is the marketing-year-to-date shipment total; outstanding_sales is contracted-but-not-yet-shipped quantity; current_my_net_sales/current_my_total_commitment cover the active marketing year, next_my_outstanding_sales/next_my_net_sales are forward sales already booked against the following marketing year (used for early-signal detection, e.g. a large next_my_net_sales spike ahead of the current marketing year's close). country_code is FAS's own numeric code (China=5700, not an ISO code); country_iso3 carries the ISO 3166-1/GENC alpha-3 equivalent where FAS publishes one (null for FAS regional/historical groupings that are not real ISO countries) for a best-effort join to ref.countries.iso_alpha3. Detecting a purchase pause/resume: filter commodity_code + country_code and watch weekly_exports and current_my_net_sales (a net sales row can go negative on a cancellation) week over week; a sudden multi-week run of zero/near- zero weekly_exports and current_my_net_sales after a prior active run is the pause signature, a resumed positive current_my_net_sales week is the resume signature. Joins to econ.fred_indicators (commodity price context) and ag.nass_crop_production (US production side of the same commodity).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/lobbying_act.tableComment: The individual lobbyists named on each lobbying activity, one row per (activity, lobbyist). `covered_position` is any covered executive or legislative branch position the lobbyist held in the previous 20 years, as the filer wrote it (e.g. "Principal", "National President"); `is_new` is true when the lobbyist was added on this filing. `lobbyist_id` joins to the lobbyists registry. Join to lobbying_activities on (filing_uuid, activity_seq). Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fec/intercommitt.tableComment: Transactions between political committees — transfers, joint fundraising allocations, and other inter-committee financial activity — with no candidate_id column, unlike committee_contributions (which links each row to a specific candidate). Shows the flow of money between PACs, party committees, and campaign committees. Source: oth{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header). DIRECTION: committee_id is the FILING committee (whose oth-schedule report this row came from) and is constant across every row for one filer; entity_type, contributor_name, and other_id together describe the COUNTERPARTY committee/entity for that one transaction (entity_type/contributor_name vary row to row even though committee_id doesn't — join fec.committees on other_id + year for the counterparty's details). Unlike committee_contributions, whether money moved INTO or OUT OF the filing committee is NOT fixed by column position — it depends on transaction_type (see FEC Schedule L code descriptions); amount is signed (negative = refund/reversal) regardless. PERFORMANCE: always filter on the year partition first.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/govt_fina.tableComment: State & local government finance from Census's annual "Individual Unit File" — one row per government unit x finance item code x year (long/tall layout: amount_thousands is the single fact, item_code the dimension). The landing page (census.gov/data/datasets/{year}/econ/local/public-use-datasets.html) is read by GovtFinanceProvider, which discovers and streams the actual ZIP link (filename is neither year-templatable nor stable — confirmed live: 2023_Individual_Unit_Files.zip vs 2021_Individual_Unit_File.zip, singular/plural and casing both vary), then streams the fixed-width data file inside it (records are 32 chars for 2017+ and 34 for 2012-2016, whose ID field is two characters wider). item_code follows the Census government finance classification manual (2006_classification_manual.pdf); notable codes for capital-vs-operating comparisons: E12/F12 (elementary- secondary education current operations / construction), E36/F36 (hospitals current operations / construction), E61/F61 (parks & recreation current operations / construction). Local water and sewer utilities: A91 water supply utility revenue (charges billed to customers) and A80 sewerage charges, with E91/E80 the matching operating expenditure and F91/F80 construction; A81/E81 are solid waste. These give what each city, county, township or special district collects and spends on water and sewer service per year (2022: ~20k units report A91) — dollar totals, not per-customer rates or tariffs. For a per-person comparison, divide by the local population (geo/census tables via county_fips; environment.drinking_water has population_served_count per water system but shares no key with government units). For the national trend in water/sewer prices see the CPI series CUUR0000SEHG02 in econ.inflation_metrics. There is no single item code for "Total Taxes" — T01 is Property Tax specifically (the classification manual's largest single tax category, not an aggregate); a total-taxes figure for a unit or state requires summing every T-prefixed row (T01, T09-T16, T19-T29, T40, T41, T50, T51, T53, T99) grouped by (state_fips, year), or by (state_fips, gov_type_code, year) for a level breakdown — summing T01 alone understates total tax revenue by an amount that depends entirely on how heavily that state's governments rely on property tax versus sales/income/other taxes. gov_type_code: 0=state, 1=county, 2=city, 3=township, 4=special district, 5=independent school district (3rd digit of the source ID field). unit_id is that government's unique identifier within (state_fips, gov_type_code, county_fips) — not globally unique alone. county_fips is the county OR county-type area the unit is located in; for state-level rows (gov_type_code=0) this is not a valid geo.counties FIPS. county_fips is a FIPS code for every year: the 2012-2016 files' own ID county field is a Census county sequence number, not FIPS, so GovtFinanceProvider looks up the real FIPS county per unit from the Fin_GID identifier file bundled in the same ZIP. amount_thousands is in THOUSANDS of dollars and may be negative (debt retirements, etc.). This is a stratified sample survey of government units (large governments fully enumerated, smaller ones sampled) even in Census-of-Governments years (2012/2017/2022) — a raw per-state sum over the units present in this table is not guaranteed to equal that state's true total; cross-validate a state-level dollar aggregate against Census's own state-level crosstab file (NNstatetypepu.txt, bundled in each year's ZIP) before relying on it. state_fips is a FIPS code for every year: the 2012-2016 files number states with Census's own alphabetical codes (01-51, District of Columbia 09), which GovtFinanceProvider translates. Source (per year): census.gov/data/datasets/{year}/econ/local/public-use-datasets.html.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/weather/coops_ti.tableComment: Predicted high and low tide times and heights from NOAA CO-OPS harmonic prediction (product=predictions&interval=hilo), one row per predicted extreme per tidal station. Predictions are astronomical only (no weather), so water_level_m from coops_high_low minus the matching prediction isolates storm surge and other non-tidal anomaly; see the coops_daily_surge view. Heights are meters above MLLW (current tidal epoch), time in UTC. Source: api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov Data API, keyless, public domain, 365 days per call so the ETL pulls one station-year per call. Join coops_stations on station_id for state and coordinates. Currents predictions are not included.

Complements fisheries.noaa_commercial_landings (wild catch) for total seafood supply; species names are NASS wording and are not harmonized with NOAA species codes.

Header fields are the docket's own — title, when it was docketed, the court below and its case numbers and decision date, any application it is linked with, and the Questions Presented. `granted_date`, `argued_date` and `judgment_issued_date` are the dates of the docket entries "Petition GRANTED", "Argued." and "Judgment Issued." and are null where the docket has none (a summary reversal is not argued; a docket in which the Court's own entry is misspelt has no judgment date). `entry_count` and `document_count` count the docket's entries and the filings linked from them; the entries are in scotus_docket_entries. Join to scotus_slip_opinions on `docket_number` = `listing_docket`. Not included: dockets of cases decided before term 2017 (the docket pages before 2016 use an older layout that is not read), original-jurisdiction cases (their page address cannot be derived from the listing), and, for a consolidated case, the companion dockets — only the lead docket the listing names is fetched. No petitions the Court declined to hear are here.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/edu/library_outl.tableComment: IMLS Public Libraries Survey (PLS), outlet-level file — one row per physical library outlet (central, branch, or bookmobile stop) x fiscal year, the only PLS grain that carries square footage. IMLS lists every fiscal year's ZIP on one static landing page (not a per-year URL), so LibraryOutletsTransformer discovers the year's link from that page, then the "outlet" CSV inside the ZIP (which also holds a separate administrative-entity-level CSV with no square-footage column). Outlet identity is (state, fscs_key, fscs_seq) — NOT the source's own library_id field, which is not reliably unique/self-consistent in the raw data (confirmed: over a thousand library_id values collide across two different library systems in the FY2024 file). outlet_type: CE=Central, BR=Branch, BS=Bookmobile Stop, BM=Bookmobile. square_feet is null wherever the source carries an NCES missing/not-applicable/not-reported sentinel rather than a real count. county_fips is derived from the first 5 digits of the source's 11-digit Census tract FIPS (no county FIPS column is provided directly). Source: imls.gov/research-evaluation/surveys/public-libraries-survey-pls.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/geo/county_cbsa_.tableComment: County to Core Based Statistical Area (metropolitan and micropolitan area) membership from the OMB delineations as republished by the Census Bureau ("List 1" of the delineation files): one row per county per delineation vintage, with the CBSA code and title, metropolitan or micropolitan type, the metropolitan division (31 divisions in 2013 to 2020, 37 in 2023, e.g. division 35614 within CBSA 35620 New York), the combined statistical area (CSA), and whether the county is a central or an outlying county of the CBSA. Six vintages: 2013 (Feb 2013, 1,882 counties), 2015 (Jul 2015, 1,899), 2017 (Aug 2017, 1,899), 2018 (Sep 2018, 1,915), 2020 (Mar 2020, 1,916) and 2023 (Jul 2023, 1,915; Connecticut counties are replaced by its nine planning regions, 09110 to 09190). Counties that belong to no CBSA (rural counties outside every metro and micro area, about 1,200 of the ~3,140) are simply absent: a left join from a county table gives null cbsa_code for them. (vintage, county_fips) is unique: a county is in at most one CBSA per vintage. Which vintage to join: for a time-varying join pick the latest vintage in force at the observation date, i.e. the largest vintage with delineation_date on or before it (2013 for data through mid-2015, 2015 from Jul 2015, 2017 from Aug 2017, 2018 from Sep 2018, 2020 from Mar 2020, 2023 from Jul 2023); for a single current mapping use vintage 2023 (the latest), but note that its Connecticut codes are planning regions, so Connecticut county data keyed on the legacy 09001 to 09015 codes needs vintage 2020. Exact county membership as OMB defines it, unlike the ZIP-weighted approximation of geo.zip_county_crosswalk x geo.zip_cbsa_crosswalk. Boundaries are in geo.cbsa. Joins to geo.counties on county_fips and to geo.cbsa on cbsa_code = cbsa_fips. Source: Census Bureau metro-micro delineation files (www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/metro-micro/geographies/reference-files/{vintage}/ delineation-files/list1*.xls[x]). The April 2018 delineation (Bulletin 18-03) that the September 2018 one replaced is not included.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ref/gleif_cik_ma.tableComment: Bridge table mapping GLEIF LEI codes to SEC CIK numbers (lei, cik, legal_name, entity_status). Derived from the GLEIF golden copy CSV filtered where registration_authority_id = 'RA000665' (SEC EDGAR). That authority ID covers both real filer CIKs and SEC fund-series identifiers (e.g. "S000005113") registered with SEC but not themselves filers — a validator drops any non-numeric cik value, since a series ID never matches a real CIK downstream. Current snapshot only, overwritten each run — unlike gleif_entities, which keeps an append-only change history. Provides fast LEI <-> CIK lookups without scanning the full GLEIF dataset. entity_org_bridge.sec_cik (EIN-path matches) joins here on cik = sec_cik to reach the LEI — the exact bridge for that column; do not name-match its org against gleif_entities.legal_name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/research/nsf_awa.tableComment:
NSF award-level grant microdata from the NSF Award Search API (api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards.json) — one row per award, dated by the award's initial award date and assigned to the federal fiscal year (October-September) containing it. Carries funds_obligated_amt (dollars obligated to date) and estimated_total_amt (the award's full expected amount over its life), the recipient (awardee_name, awardee_uei, city, state, congressional district), the NSF directorate and division that made the award, the funding program, and transaction_type (Standard Grant, Continuing Grant, Cooperative Agreement, fellowship ...). Answers "are federal research awards getting bigger or more numerous" for NSF at award grain, where nsf_federal_rd_obligations and nsf_herd_by_institution carry only agency and institution TOTALS; nih_award_projects is the NIH counterpart at the same grain.
Both amounts are as of the latest refresh, not as of the award date: a multi-year continuing grant's funds_obligated_amt grows as later years are funded, so a recent fiscal year's obligated total is understated relative to what the same cohort will show once its increments are made; estimated_total_amt is the stable size measure for an award-size distribution. Dollars are nominal (not inflation-adjusted). Not every NSF row is a research grant: education, infrastructure, fellowships and cooperative agreements are all here, so filter on transaction_type or directorate when the question is specifically about research project grants. NSF only — other agencies' awards are not in this table.
The API truncates any query at 10,000 results, so the provider fetches one calendar month of award dates at a time (the busiest month on record is ~3,600 awards) and rejects a month that reports the cap instead of loading a truncated prefix. Coverage starts at FY2010 and follows the calendar forward; lower minYear on the year dimension to reach further back.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/banking/enforcem.tableComment: Federal Reserve enforcement actions against state member banks, bank holding companies, and individuals under Fed jurisdiction — cease-and- desist orders, written agreements, civil money penalties, prohibitions from banking, and prompt corrective action notices. Board of Governors bulk CSV, full history back to 1989, refetched and overwritten in full each cycle (the source carries no per-row last-modified field, so an incremental append could miss a later-added termination_date on an already-seen row). Covers Federal Reserve-supervised entities only: OCC-regulated national banks and FDIC-regulated state non-member banks are NOT covered here, since neither publishes a bulk enforcement feed (OCC's EASearch is a search-only web form; FDIC's BankFind Suite API has no enforcement endpoint). No natural primary key: effective_date + banking_organization is not unique (the source legitimately carries multiple concurrent actions against the same organization on the same date), and there is no cert number to join against banking.institutions — individual_affiliation/banking_organization are free-text name and location strings only. Source: federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg bulk CSV.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/adfg_f.tableComment: Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Sport Fish Division escapement and run counts of adult Chinook, Sockeye (incl. early/late run), Coho and Steelhead at ~40 weirs, towers and sonar sites (Kenai, Kasilof, Russian, Anchor, Ninilchik, Situk, Gulkana, Copper, Chena, Salcha, Karluk, Ayakulik, Buskin, Nushagak, Deshka, Little Susitna and more), one row per count site x species x year, summed from the daily counts, 1960s onward (start year varies by site). state_abbr is always AK. This is the Alaska counterpart to dart_adult_counts: the Division's own in-river counts at monitored sites, not a statewide run-size estimate (Bristol Bay, Yukon and Kuskokwim commercial-area escapement belong to the Commercial Fisheries Division and are not in this table), and a site's count is only comparable to the same site's other years. Counts for a year are only the days the site operated (days_counted, first/last_count_date); the current year is partial. Use noaa_commercial_landings for statewide harvest.

Senate only; see fd_filings for coverage.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/bts_po.tableComment: Monthly container throughput (TEUs) for the Top-10 U.S. container ports, from BTS's Port Performance Freight Statistics Program (Socrata rd72-aq8r, "Monthly TEU Data"). Melted from the source's one-row-per-month/one-column-per-port layout into one row per (port, month). This is the best freely-ingestible port-level container-volume series found — the industry-standard NRF/Hackett Global Port Tracker has no free bulk-downloadable time series, only point figures in press releases (confirmed independently by two arms in Defect Register D-109). NOT a currently-updated series: the source dataset itself stops at October 2022 (46 months from Jan 2019) and has not been refreshed since — verified live 27 Aug 2026. Real historical data for that window, not a live/current-era proxy; a national customs-value proxy (econ.trade_imports) remains the only current-era option.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/county_mi.tableComment: IRS SOI county-to-county migration derived from year-over-year address changes on returns. One row per origin->destination county for the filing year (from the OUTFLOW file: Y1 = origin, Y2 = destination). Summary/foreign buckets (state FIPS >= 57; county 000) and non-migrant same-county rows are filtered out; suppressed cells (n1 < 0) dropped. Both endpoints join to geo.counties. agi in $1000s. Years 2008 onward (2008 = the 2007-2008 file). Coverage is not uniform: IRS lists a county pair only above a disclosure threshold, 10 returns for 2008-2013 (about 78,000-91,000 pairs a year) and about 20 returns from 2014 (about 36,000-60,000 pairs a year), so pair counts and summed flows from 2014 on are not comparable with 2008-2013 and a pre/post comparison of small flows needs the threshold applied to both sides. Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/countyoutflow{YYZZ}.csv.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/bridge.tableComment: FHWA National Bridge Inventory — one row per raw NBI record per annual data-year snapshot, NOT one row per bridge: the source file commingles primary bridge records, culvert records, and border/jointly-owned-structure secondary records under one row shape (see record_type). Filter to record_type='1' to match FHWA's own published national bridge count. Deck/superstructure/substructure condition ratings (0-9, N), FHWA's own precomputed bridge_condition (Good/Fair/Poor) and lowest_rating summary fields, location, year built/reconstructed, traffic, and improvement-cost fields (bridge/roadway/total, plus year_of_imp) for federal-spending comparisons. The "delimited" national file uses a single-quote text qualifier, not RFC4180 double quote, so source.response.quoted is false: a handful of free-text columns (e.g. features_desc, facility_carried) carry literal leading/trailing single quotes that this table does not strip — harmless for the numeric/coded columns this table curates — and any stray literal " in free text (an apostrophe mistyped as one, an inch mark) is read as ordinary text instead of an RFC4180 quote, which would otherwise merge that record with the next line and desync every column in both. decimal_latitude/decimal_longitude are computed from the source's packed DDMMSS.ss / DDDMMSS.ss fields (Items 16/17) using length-relative substring extraction (minutes/seconds anchored to the end of the string, degrees to whatever remains at the front) rather than fixed character positions, so a digit-count change at the front of the field (e.g. a leading zero) doesn't shift the split; county_code is zero-padded back to 3 digits for the same leading-zero-loss reason numeric fields generally have. LAT_016/LONG_017 are also listed in source.response.rawFields to stop the generic CSV ingest from routing them through numeric inference at all — undeclared as their own column, they'd otherwise be parsed as a Long/Double and re-serialized before this expression ever runs, which can append a trailing .0 that length-relative extraction can't distinguish from real digits. The raw LAT_016/LONG_017 fields are not carried through as their own output columns. Source: fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/nbi/{year}allstatesallrecsdel.zip (see fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/nbi/ascii.cfm).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/regional_pr.tableComment: BEA Regional Price Parities (RPP): the standard federal cost-of-living / price-level index by state (search terms: cost of living, COLA, price parity, RPP) — by state and Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) relative to the national average (100.000), annual since 2008. This is the table to divide nominal wages/income by (index/100) to get real, cost-of-living-adjusted dollars comparable across states. Verified live against apps.bea.gov/api/data (dataset Regional, tables SARPP/MARPP): coverage 2008-2024 at verification time. tablename selects the geography: SARPP = state (includes a GeoFips=00000 "United States" national baseline row, always rpp_index=100.000, plus all 50 states + DC); MARPP = Metropolitan Statistical Areas only (no non-metro/rural, micropolitan, or port-area coverage — BEA's port-level PARPP table is not loaded here). line_code selects the price component: 1=All items, 2=Goods, 3=Services: Rents, 4=Services: Utilities, 5=Services: Other. An rpp_index of e.g. 88.901 means costs are 11.1% below the national average for that component/geography/year. (BEA's Regional dataset also lists SARPP/MARPP among the 63 tables regional_income iterates, but that table's line_code resolver only has reference data for SAINC/SQINC/CAINC/SAGDP/SQGDP/CAGDP series, so regional_income never actually fetches RPP rows — this table is the source of that data.)

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/rmis_r.tableComment: Hatchery and wild salmon, steelhead and trout release groups recorded in the Regional Mark Information System (RMIS, Regional Mark Processing Center / PSMFC, PSC format v5.0), one row per coded-wire-tag release group (tagged) or untagged release group, brood years 1950 onward, about 190,000 records from 17 reporting agencies (WDFW, CDFO, ADFG, ODFW, NWIFC, USFWS, CDFW, IDFG, NMFS and tribes) across Alaska, British Columbia, Washington, Idaho, Oregon and California. Gives how many fish were released (total_released, cwt_tagged_count, non-CWT mark counts), species, brood year and release dates, release stage, rearing type, broodstock origin, average weight and length, and the release / hatchery / stock location codes (join to rmis_locations for site name, basin, region and coordinates). Use it to set hatchery stocking against the adult returns in dart_adult_counts, adfg_fish_counts, cdfw_grandtab_escapement and wdfw_salmonid_escapement. Counts are as submitted by each agency: tagged groups carry both tagged and untagged-fish counts, so total_released is the group size, not the CWT count alone. Canadian (CDFO, state_abbr BC) releases are included. Mark counts are null when the agency did not report them. RMPC refreshes the files as agencies submit validated data.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/edu/fsa_pslf_dis.tableComment:
Federal Student Aid's own PSLF (Public Service Loan Forgiveness) Combined Report — studentaid.gov/data-center/student/loan-forgiveness/pslf-data, the same file FSA calls "PSLF Combined Report" (pslf-combined-report.xlsx). Sourced to close the gap #721 documents: no table in edu or fiscal covered any federal student loan discharge or forgiveness figures, leaving claims like a 2026-09-24 lawsuit's $4.6B disputed-discharge allegation with no DOE-published number to cross-check against. This table carries FSA's own cumulative PSLF/TEPSLF/Limited-Waiver discharge totals (unique borrowers processed, total and average balance discharged per program) plus PSLF application throughput and portfolio-composition counts from the same combined workbook — it does NOT cover other discharge programs (borrower defense, closed school, total-and-permanent- disability) or credit-bureau-side delinquency reporting, neither of which FSA publishes in a comparably structured public file (credit-bureau reporting in particular is very unlikely to ever be publicly available — it lives inside CRA-borrower-servicer channels the government does not operate).
Long/key-value grain: one row per (section, program, metric_name), not one row per borrower — FSA does not publish borrower-level discharge data. `section` is one of 'application_status' (application throughput, forms + borrowers), 'cumulative_portfolio' (PSLF-eligible borrower/balance counts and qualifying-payment-count buckets), or 'discharges' (the actual processed-discharge totals, the table's core answer to #721). `program` is 'PSLF' for the first two sections (they don't break out by program) and one of 'Combined' / 'PSLF' / 'TEPSLF' / 'Limited Waiver' for 'discharges'. `metric_name` is a normalized snake_case identifier for FSA's own row label (e.g. "Total Balance Discharged" -> total_balance_discharged); the workbook's original labels are FSA's, not reworded here. `metric_value` is always expressed in the base unit named by `metric_unit` — dollar amounts are converted from the source's "$X billion"-style strings to whole USD, never left as billions.
dataset_type: snapshot — the whole table is replaced on every successful fetch (no year or period dimension; freshness: etag skips a re-fetch when FSA hasn't republished). `report_as_of_date` (last day of the covering month, parsed from the workbook's own "Cumulative Data as of Mon-end YYYY" label) is the only signal of which period a given row set covers — every row in one Iceberg snapshot shares the same value, and it advances only when FSA republishes with a newer month.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/bill_committ.tableComment: Committees and subcommittees a bill was referred to, one row per committee or subcommittee, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. Join to `bills` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number). `committee_system_code` is the Congress.gov committee code (e.g. hsju00 = House Judiciary). A subcommittee row (e.g. hsvr10) has `parent_committee_system_code` set to its full committee's code and NULL `chamber` and `committee_type`, which the source records only on the full committee. `committee_type` is Standing, Select, Special or Other. What each committee did with the bill (referred, markup, reported, hearings) is in bill_committee_activities.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/interconn.tableComment: Grid interconnection queue: one row per generation or storage project that has requested connection to the U.S. transmission grid, from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's "Queued Up" dataset (Rand et al., 2026 edition, requests from 2000 through the end of 2025, CC BY 4.0), which LBNL compiles from the queue files of 7 ISO/RTOs and 50 non-ISO balancing areas (~98% of installed U.S. generating capacity; Alaska and Hawaii not covered; transmission-connected generation and storage only, no load interconnection or distribution-connected projects). ~38,200 rows: ~8,500 active, ~4,800 operational, ~24,200 withdrawn, ~670 suspended (q_status). Answers "how much new generation or storage is waiting to connect in this county, and of what type" — the forward-looking supply-side half of siting questions; county_interconnection_queue is the per-county rollup. county_fips is the project's FIRST listed county only (the source states multi-county requests keep just the first); the ~1,770 rows (~5%) whose source FIPS is blank have a null county_fips, and 22 rows sit outside the U.S. (state MX/ON/MB). mw_1/mw_2/mw_3 are the rated MW of resource type_1/type_2/type_3; a hybrid such as Solar+Battery has both mw_1 and mw_2, so total project MW is their sum, and LBNL's own published totals additionally include imputed storage MW that this file omits (active requests sum to ~1,865 GW here against ~2,061 GW in the report; the 8,513 active rows here are ~3% more than the report's 8,244, whose basis the file does not identify). 16 rows carry a negative mw_1 (-4 to -75 MW) in LBNL's own workbook and are kept as published, so SUM(mw) over a set that includes them is very slightly understated. q_id is unique only together with entity, and not even then for 135 pairs, so source_row (the row's position in the source sheet) is the only row identifier; a few q_id values were converted to dates or numbers by Excel in the source. Dates: q_date request entered queue, prop_date proposed online, on_date became operational, wd_date withdrawn, ia_date interconnection agreement signed. as_of_year is the edition's cut-off year. county holds the name as the queue wrote it and occasionally a town rather than the county (40 of 2,634 FIPS have more than one spelling); county_fips is authoritative. Snapshot table: the source is replaced wholesale each edition, not appended. SOURCE DURABILITY: emp.lbl.gov and eta.lbl.gov sit behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that no non-browser client passes (verified 2026-09-25: HTTP 403, cf-mitigated: challenge), so the workbook is read from the copy redistributed under CC BY 4.0 in the Zenodo deposit 10.5281/zenodo.22287832 (files are immutable per record). That deposit is a third party's replication package, pinned to the 2026 edition; a new Queued Up edition needs source.url pointed at a newer deposit. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to geo.state_ref via state (= state_abbr).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/fda_drug_.tableComment:
FDA drug enforcement (recall) actions, one row per recall_number with severity classification (Class I/II/III), status (Terminated/Ongoing/Pending), and voluntary vs. FDA-mandated origin. Joins to fda_ndc_products only via recalling_firm/labeler_name text match — no structural NDC column is present in this table.

Tall layout: Census returns individual-country rows interleaved with its own built-in world-total and trade-bloc/continental aggregate rows in the same response, with no discriminator of its own — filter geo_level = 'country' before summing value_usd, or the total silently multiplies by every bloc/continent a country also belongs to (plus the world total). No quantity column: Census's QTY_1_MO/ UNIT_QY1 fields are unpopulated (always "0"/"-") at COMM_LVL=HS6, confirmed live across all 364,588 rows of a full month — quantity is only standardized at the HS10 grain, which this table doesn't fetch. trade_by_state's QTY_1_MO IS populated (state-level statehs endpoint reports it differently); use that table for quantity.

Closes the all-agency/all-performer field-of-science gap that nsf_federal_rd_obligations (rd_field hard-coded to "All fields") and nsf_herd_by_institution (real rd_field column, but scoped to university-performed R&D only) each leave open on their own. Does not cover experimental development obligations by field — NCSES's own field taxonomy was historically collected for research only, and the field breakdown for development obligations is not published as its own crosscut in this table.
field_level encodes the row's place in NCSES's own field hierarchy: 0 = grand total ("All fields"), 1 = a broad field of R&D, 2 = a detailed sub-field nested under the preceding level-1 row. Level-1 rows sum to the level-0 total; level-2 rows sum to their enclosing level-1 row. Pick one level to aggregate on — summing across levels double-counts, the same rollup-vs-leaf discipline as energy.eia_electricity_generation's sector_is_rollup/fuel_is_rollup flags. The FYs 2016-2025 source encodes this via each field-name cell's own style indent; the FYs 1993-2014 historical tables (a different NCSES publication era) instead encode it via 4 leading non-breaking-space characters per level baked into the field-name string itself — confirmed live 2026-09-13 against table 134 (FYs 2004-14): 0/4/8 leading NBSPs map to level 0/1/2 exactly. The FY2015 source (NCSES's intermediate "Data Explorer" era) uses a real style indent like the current edition, but at double the step size (2/4 for level 1/2, not 1/2) — confirmed live 2026-09-17. NsfRdByFieldTransformer normalizes the style indent to the file's own smallest positive indent before dividing, and falls back to counting NBSPs only when the style carries none, so all three vintages populate field_level identically. A field's taxonomy label can differ across the 2021 field-of-R&D revision (e.g. "Computer sciences and mathematics" pre-2021 vs. "Computer and information sciences" post-2021); both eras' labels are preserved as-is from the source. A field/year cell marked "NA" in the source is dropped — no row is emitted for it at all, not a row with a null value — because NCSES uses NA for two different reasons this table can't tell apart: a field that didn't exist under that year's taxonomy, or a "(preliminary)" most-recent year published only at the level-0/level-1 grain (NCSES withholds level-2 sub-field detail until the following year's edition finalizes it), which is why the newest year always has far fewer rows than the years before it. Re-running this table's full-refresh fetch after NCSES publishes the next edition picks up the finalized detail automatically — a low row count for only the single most recent year is expected, not a defect. The same mechanism explains why FYs 2013-14 carry only 9 rows apiece (level 0-1 only) against 41 for every other year in the FYs 1993-2014 range — confirmed live 2026-09-13, they were the newest, still-preliminary years as of the nsf14316 (FYs 2012-14) edition this table's historical rows are sourced from, and no later edition's equivalent long-run table has been located yet to backfill their level-2 detail (see govdata-ops#257). FY2015 itself is fully finalized (41 rows, full level-2 detail) — it was not the preliminary year of the edition it is sourced from (see below).
The FYs 1993-2014 historical vintages are sourced from NCSES publication nsf14316 (FYs 2012-14 edition) via its own long-run tables 133 and 134. The original nsf.gov/statistics/nsf14316/ URLs are dead — NSF now serves an "Archive Goodbye" redirect for that whole publication era with no static-file replacement — so these two are fetched from the Wayback Machine's mirror instead (re-verify-if-404s risk, same pattern already accepted for other individually-hosted sources in this codebase; a Wayback snapshot URL is otherwise permanent).
FY2015 is sourced from a third NCSES vintage: table 123 of the ncsesdata.nsf.gov "Data Explorer" era (edition fedfunds/2017, itself spanning FYs 2009-18 in one file — confirmed live 2026-09-17). Only FY2015 is kept from it; FYs 2009-14 and 2016-18 in that same file are discarded because the hist_2004_2014 and current vintages already source those years, and keeping them too would emit duplicate (year, rd_field) rows. The original ncsesdata.nsf.gov URL is dead (404, no redirect) — fetched via its Wayback Machine mirror instead, same re-verify-if-404s risk as the two nsf14316 vintages above.
Externally-compiled "federal R&D by field" series (e.g. AAAS, secondary policy trackers) report R&D total (research + development), not research alone, and will differ from this table by the development share of a given field — larger for fields with a substantial development component (life sciences via NIH, defense- adjacent engineering), smaller elsewhere. NCSES does not publish "development by detailed field" as its own crosscut — Table 83 breaks development out only by funding agency, never by field of science — so any "R&D by field" figure necessarily combines Table 91's research-by-field with an outside-NCSES allocation of development spending across fields under each compiler's own methodology. Both are correct at what they claim to measure; use this table for research-only field breakdowns, and NCSES agency- level tables (82, 83) or a third-party compiler for R&D total.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/acs_indus.tableComment: Industry mix of the civilian employed population 16 years and over by nativity, from the ACS 5-Year subject table S0501 (Selected Characteristics of the Native and Foreign-Born Populations), state level only. Answers "what share of industry X's workforce is foreign-born": for each of 3 nativity groups (total, native, foreign born) S0501 reports the PERCENT of that group's employed people working in each of 13 broad industries (columns <industry>_pct_<nativity>), plus the group's employed headcount (employed_<nativity>). Workers in an industry for a group = employed_<nativity> * <industry>_pct_<nativity> / 100; the foreign-born share of an industry's workforce = employed_foreign_born * <industry>_pct_foreign_born / (employed_total * <industry>_pct_total). Percentages are published rounded to 0.1, so derived counts carry that rounding on top of the ACS sampling error. Industries are the 13 broad groups S0501 publishes (no finer NAICS detail; finer industry by nativity exists only in ACS PUMS microdata). The naturalized-citizen / non-citizen split S0501 also publishes is not carried (the Census API caps a request at 50 variables). Values are null where the Census suppresses an estimate.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/sba_loan_.tableComment:
Small Business Administration 7(a) and 504 loan approvals (FOIA public data), one row per approved loan — federal credit activity by borrower geography, industry, lender, and approval fiscal year. Fanned out by program; each program is split across several year-range CSVs on the source site (year is a data column, not a partition), all streamed and concatenated by SbaLoansProvider. Reissued quarterly, so the whole program partition is overwritten each run. Joins to geo.state_ref via borrower_state. Source: data.sba.gov 7(a)-504 FOIA.
borrower_name and lender_name are unstructured — this table carries no EIN column, so there is no exact hub-key join. ref.canonical_org_entity carries each as an already-resolved identity (sba_borrower_name, sba_lender_name, each with an LEI when matched); join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/pep_compo.tableComment: Population Estimates Program (PEP) components of population change for every county, one row per county per data year (July 1 reference date): the population estimate, births, deaths, natural change (births - deaths), net international migration, net DOMESTIC migration (people moving between U.S. counties, the figure that shows whether a county is gaining or losing residents to other places), total net migration and the residual (change the components do not explain). Counts are people over the estimate year (July 1 of the prior year to June 30). The first year of each vintage is shorter: data year 2010 runs from the April 1, 2010 census base and data year 2020 from the April 1, 2020 base, so those two years carry about three months of births, deaths and migration. Data years 2010-2019 come from the final 2010-2019 vintage; data years 2020 onward come from the latest published vintage (the vintage column says which), so the series breaks at 2019/2020 because the 2020 vintage re-bases on the 2020 census. From the 2022 vintage Connecticut is published as its nine planning regions (county_fips 09110-09190) instead of its eight counties (09001-09015), so Connecticut rows for data years 2020 onward do not join geo.counties; every other county does. Complements pep_population (which has population and density only). The Census API serves components for data year 2019 only, so this table reads the bulk files co-est{vintage}-alldata.csv. Join to disasters.disaster_declarations or to disasters.ihp_housing_assistance_owners on county_fips. Source: www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/noaa_f.tableComment: NOAA Fisheries Economics of the United States (FEUS): the economic footprint of fishing by state, one row per geography x sector x impact measure (x imports basis for the commercial industry). industry is commercial (the seafood industry: commercial harvesters, seafood processors and dealers, seafood wholesalers and distributors, retail and importers) or recreational (marine recreational fishing expenditures: for-hire, private boat and shore trips, plus durable-goods expenditures). impact_type is jobs (unit jobs), or sales, income or value_added (unit thousand_usd, thousands of dollars), all modelled economic impacts including multiplier effects rather than direct landings revenue: use noaa_commercial_landings for pounds and dollars landed. Commercial rows come in two bases, imports_basis with_imports (counts the importer sector and the activity it supports) and without_imports; the two must not be added together, and a recreational row has no imports_basis. row_level separates the components from the rollups so nothing is double counted: for a state, the component rows (sectors, or for recreational the three trip modes) sum to the total row (sector 'Total Impacts' commercial, 'Total State Economic Impacts' recreational) within rounding. Recreational durable-goods spending is published only for the United States, where the national total ('Total United States Economic Impacts') equals the trip modes plus durable_expenditures; state durable_expenditures values are confidential (null) and a state total excludes them. Sum the components or read the total, not both. Geography is 23 coastal states plus the United States (geo_level national, state_abbr null); recreational reports East and West Florida separately and commercial reports Florida as a whole. noaa_region is the NOAA region of the state (null for the national rows and commercial Florida). impact_value is null where NOAA withholds a confidential value (about 22% of recreational rows, chiefly state durable expenditures). data_year is the year NOAA states for that geography (2021, except 2020 for commercial Florida); this is the latest-year snapshot published in the data tool, not a time series. Inland states and non-coastal territories are not covered. Join to geo.state_ref via state_abbr.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/eia_elect.tableComment: EIA API v2 electric power operational data. Monthly electricity generation (thousand MWh), total fuel consumption (MMBtu), fuel consumption for electricity generation (MMBtu), cost per MMBtu, sulfur content, and ash content. Broken down by state, energy source, and sector. One row per state + energy source + sector + year-month. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr. THIS TABLE CANNOT BE SUMMED NAIVELY — it interleaves rollup rows with the leaf rows they already contain, on all three axes at once, and a SUM that ignores any of them multiplies the answer: (1) energy_source_code mixes leaves with EIA's own rollups — 'ALL', 'FOS', 'REN' and 'NUC' each already total other rows, and even some leaf-looking codes are nested (COL = BIT + SUB + LIG). Use fuel_is_rollup to pick one level. (2) sector_code likewise carries '99' = "All Sectors" alongside the individual sectors it sums; see sector_is_rollup. (3) geo_level mixes 'state', 'division' and 'national' rows — see that column. For a state's annual generation mix, filter geo_level='state' AND sector_code='99', take the ALL/FOS/REN/NUC rows, and SUM across the 12 months — there is no annual sentinel row, so a per-year figure must be summed from months. Selecting a single month's value per category instead mixes different peak months and produces parts that do not add up to the total. The state_energy_mix view does exactly this and is the intended entry point for mix questions.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/housing/hmda_len.tableComment: Real census-tract-grain HMDA lending activity — the tract/county grain housing.hmda_loans cannot provide. That table's aggregations-endpoint `counties=` filter is accepted and echoed back by the API but never actually applied server-side (confirmed live 2026-09-11: Story County IA and Loving County TX, population ~64, both returned their entire state's total). Real tract/county grain requires the loan-level data instead: this table downloads CFPB's "Nationwide Data Subset" loan-level export (ffiec.cfpb.gov/v2/data-browser-api/view/nationwide/csv) for each year and aggregates to census tract via HmdaLoanLevelAggregateProvider — an embedded DuckDB query streamed directly off the downloaded file, never loaded into JVM heap as a row list. The API requires an explicit actions_taken filter alongside years or it silently returns a small undocumented partial subset instead of an error (confirmed live: omitting it returned ~261K rows for 2023; passing all 8 action codes returned the real ~1.11M). origination_count/ denial_count/origination_total_amount are counted from real loan-level records, not derived or estimated. tract_population/tract_minority_population_percent/ tract_to_msa_income_percentage are the source's own per-tract context fields (constant across a tract's loan records within a year), carried through for convenience. Complements housing.hmda_loans' state x action x purpose funnel view rather than replacing it — this table has no purpose/demographic breakdown by design, to keep the first tract-grain build scoped; that breakdown is a natural follow-on, not included here. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to geo.census_tracts via census_tract, where those exist.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/usitc_tarif.tableComment: USITC DataWeb imports-for-consumption with the duty breakout: one row per HTS-8 x partner country x year. The tariff counterpart to econ.trade_imports — hs6 (first 6 of hts8) is the join key back to the Census HS-6 import flows. Carries customs value, calculated duties, and the effective duty rate (calculated_duties / customs_value). Country is the DataWeb country NAME (the runReport grid reports names, not codes) — join hts_description via econ.usitc_tariff_schedule. Because a single DataWeb runReport is hard-capped at 20,000 rows AND a broad all-commodities year query is too slow to compute, the transformer CHUNKS BY HTS CHAPTER: one query per chapter (01..99, ex-77) at HTS-8 x country, merged into the year partition (replaced wholesale on re-run, overwritePartitions). Zero-trade rows are suppressed; requests are paced for DataWeb's rate limit. Requires a free DataWeb token (TRADE_USITC_API_TOKEN). NOTE: a single very large chapter can still exceed the 20k cap (the transformer WARNs and that chapter is a top slice); dutiable value, first-unit quantity, and import-program breakout are additional DataWeb measures not yet wired (their dataToReport codes require a DataWeb-UI network capture to confirm).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/crime/cde_reta.tableComment:
FBI Return A master file: agency-level monthly counts of Part I offenses (reported/unfounded/actual/cleared/juvenile-cleared) plus officers killed and assaulted, from the CDE bulk download (one national fixed-width file per year) instead of per-ORI API calls. One row per agency (ORI7) per month, unpivoted from the wide 12-month record. Cross-references cde_agencies via ori (ORI7 prefix).
Values are the FBI master file's own, unmodified. The file carries no per-month completeness flag: a month row exists for every agency-year, and an agency that did not report a month can hold 0 or a small late-adjustment count there, which is indistinguishable from a genuine low month. number_of_months_reported is a single header-level count and does not identify which months are empty, so 12 rows are not 12 reported months. Some agencies also carry a second record under the same ori (a different population_group, typically zero or small adjustments) that must be summed with the primary record. Some agencies record a whole year's counts in a single month (typically December), so month-level seasonality is unreliable; annual totals are the safer grain.
The FBI revises this master file for the current and recent years as agencies file late or corrected submissions (e.g. NYPD's 2024 monthly murder counts increased after initial publication); a fixed year=YYYY.zip URL is not a stable snapshot. The month dimension below is a pure cache-buster (not present in the URL) so every calendar month re-fetches and re-materializes each year, picking up FBI-side revisions instead of freezing the ingest-time snapshot. Even the fully revised FBI total for a year can still trail an agency's own published figure (e.g. NYPD's own site), since Return A submissions lag and consolidate on the FBI's schedule, not the agency's; that residual gap is a source/methodology difference, not a defect.

The single page (dol.gov/agencies/whd/state/minimum-wage/history) holds six HTML tables spanning disjoint "selected years" (1968-1981, 1988-1998, then every year 2000-present); years NOT shown on the page (e.g. 1969, 1973-1975, 1982-1987) are simply absent from this table, not a gap in ETL coverage. 55 jurisdictions per year: "Federal (FLSA)" (jurisdiction_type=FEDERAL), the 50 states (STATE), District of Columbia (DISTRICT), and Guam/Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands (TERRITORY — not in geo.state_ref, so state_fips is null for these three and for the FEDERAL row). raw_wage_text preserves DOL's own cell text verbatim, including its inconsistencies ("N.A." vs "NA", inconsistent "$" prefixing, a stray source typo like "4..65(g,,j)") — wage_amount (a clean hourly USD figure) is populated ONLY for the unambiguous single-value case (value_type=SINGLE); ranges (value_type=RANGE, e.g. a tipped-vs-standard spread), dual-track values (value_type=DUAL_TRACK, e.g. the pre-1978 multi-track FLSA system or a state's two-tier law), "..." (NOT_APPLICABLE — no separate jurisdiction law that year), "N.A."/"NA" (NOT_AVAILABLE), and anything else unparseable (OTHER, e.g. a non-hourly "/day" or "/wk" rate) are left null in wage_amount by design, never guessed — see raw_wage_text for the ground truth in every case. increased_from_prior_column reflects DOL's own bolding convention (its key states: "wage rates in bold indicate an increase over the previous year's rate" — the previous YEAR SHOWN, which is not always the previous calendar year before 2000). footnote_codes carries the raw trailing footnote marker(s) from inside a SINGLE cell's "[ ]"/"( )" (DOL's own lettered key on the source page defines them; not reproduced here since the definitions are not per-row data). dol.gov 403s every direct fetch from this build environment (a domain-wide Akamai edge block, confirmed even at the site root) — the same failure mode already solved in this schema for ssa_benefits_by_geography, so StateMinWageTransformer follows that precedent and fetches the page via the Wayback Machine (FiscalHttp.fetchViaWayback) rather than dol.gov directly; source.url below is the nominal/documentary URL, not what is actually requested. DOL updates this page roughly annually (a new year column appended each January); dataset_type=snapshot re-fetches and replaces the whole table on every run since the fetch is a single small page.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/state_cor.tableComment: Census Bureau Annual Survey of State Government Tax Collections (STC), ITEM_CODE=T41 ("Corporation Net Income Taxes") only — do not confuse with T40 (individual income tax; confirmed live, CA 2024 T40 = $123.1B vs T41 = $41.4B). One row per state x tax year, 50 states + DC (no territories — confirmed live: for=state:72 (Puerto Rico) returns no data). collections_thousands is in THOUSANDS of dollars and is NULL (not zero) for a state with no general corporate net income tax that year — confirmed live for 2024: Texas, Nevada, Washington, and Wyoming are NULL; South Dakota has no broad corporate income tax but its financial-institution franchise tax IS captured under T41 and returns a real value ($60.7M for 2024), so "NULL" means "no T41-classified tax," not "no state tax revenue at all." Source (per state per year): api.census.gov/data/timeseries/govsstatetax — this endpoint's for=state:* wildcard is unsupported (confirmed live: every combination of ITEM_CODE filter, get= field list, and for=state:* returned HTTP 204 with no body across the published 2016-2025 range), so each state is fetched with an explicit FIPS code. GOVTYPE and AGG_DESC are requested in the URL but not materialized as columns: both are constant for this item code (GOVTYPE=002 state government, AGG_DESC=STC017) and the API silently 204s the whole query if either is dropped from get= alongside an ITEM_CODE filter (confirmed live) — they stay in the URL as required request parameters only.
