s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/fmcsa_.tableComment:
FMCSA Company Census File — one row per USDOT-registered motor carrier (~4.47M rows), carrying registration, fleet size (drivers, CDL drivers, power/truck/bus units), operation type, hazmat authorization, and (for carriers that received a compliance review) the assigned safety rating and a per-carrier recordable_crash_rate. Event-level crash/inspection/ out-of-service records are NOT on this file (only ~54K carriers are ever rated); they publish as separate per-event SMS datasets (SMS Input - Crash 4wxs-vbns / aayw-vxb3, SMS Input - Inspection rbkj-cgst) and would be their own raw tables + a rollup view, per the one-source-per-table rule. Bulk CSV export of DOT Socrata dataset az4n-8mr2 — the whole set is downloaded in one unpaginated request and the partition overwritten each run, so this is a snapshot. Source: data.transportation.gov/api/views/az4n-8mr2/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD.
To reach a carrier's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on fmcsa_dot_number = dot_number — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the carrier's LEI/SEC CIK and its dot_number sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching carrier_name as text (including against sec.filing_metadata) finds the wrong entities and misses carriers filing under a differently-worded name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_schoo.tableComment: Annual kindergarten vaccination coverage and exemption rates, from CDC's School Vaccination Assessment Program (SchoolVaxView). National and state grain, by school year (e.g. "2025-26"); no county grain. vaccine covers DTP/DTaP/DT, MMR, MMR (PAC, Puerto Rico/American Samoa/Commonwealths reporting), Polio, Hepatitis B, Varicella, and a separate "Exemption" row-type (dose distinguishes Medical/Non-Medical/Any Exemption for those rows). geography_type is National (geography is either "United States" — weighted national estimate — or "U.S. Median" — median of state estimates, NOT the same number) or States (geography is the state name). coverage_estimate is a percentage; confirmed live 2026-09-27 against CDC's Sept 24, 2026 measles update: MMR/United States is 92.4% for 2025-26, down from 95.2% for 2019-20, matching the cited figures exactly. number_of_exemptions is populated only for Exemption rows. Complements cdc_covid_vaccinations (COVID-only, national, frozen at 2023-05-10) with a live, routinely-updated non-COVID childhood vaccination series.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/officials/presid.tableComment: Popular vote totals by state and candidate for the presidential general election, from the FEC's official post-election results workbook (fec.gov, "{year} Presidential General Election Results", published as XLSX). Richer than electoral_college_votes for the years it covers — actual vote counts, not just elector allocation — but coverage is NOT full-history: FEC only publishes this specific XLSX format for recent cycles (confirmed: 2024; unconfirmed further back — the source page lists only PDF, not XLSX, for cycles further back at the time this table was built, 2026-08-02). No predictable per-year URL exists (each year's file lives behind an opaque numeric document ID), so this transformer discovers the URL per year by scraping FEC's static results-and-voting-information listing page rather than templating a URL directly — a year with no matching link on that page yields zero rows for this table, not an error; check the ETL log for "no results link found" to distinguish "not published this way" from a real failure. One row per (year, state, candidate). Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/housing/hud_pit_.tableComment: HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) homeless counts by Continuum of Care (CoC), one row per (year, coc_number, metric_name). Source workbook is wide (HUD adds subpopulation/ demographic breakout columns most years - 25 columns in 2007 growing to 1,300+ by 2024) so this is melted long-format rather than carrying 1,300+ typed columns; metric_name is the source column header verbatim (e.g. 'Sheltered ES Homeless - Age 18 to 24', 'Overall Homeless Veterans') - see the HUD workbook's own 'field list, all years' sheet for the full taxonomy. A blank/suppressed source cell is omitted rather than written as a null count row. Includes a national total row (coc_number = 'TOTAL', coc_name = 'Total', state_abbr null - HUD leaves CoC Number blank for this row in the source). MO-604 spans Missouri and Kansas and is reported here as one combined CoC row; the companion by-state file splits its counts between MO and KS, so per-state rollups from this table will not exactly match hud_pit_counts_by_state for those two states. Source: huduser.gov/portal/sites/ default/files/xls/2007-2024-PIT-Counts-by-CoC.xlsb (annual PIT count cycle).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/fd_transacti.tableComment: Securities and property transactions disclosed by U.S. Senators, former senators and candidates, in the shape of member_stock_transactions: one row per transaction, from the STOCK Act periodic transaction reports (`source_part` = ptr) and from Part 4b of annual reports (`source_part` = annual_4b — transactions the annual report lists that were not reported on a PTR). Part 4a of an annual report, which only repeats already-filed PTRs, is not read, so a PTR transaction appears once. `owner` is Self, Spouse, Joint or Child and `owner_code` is the same in member_stock_transactions' convention (null for Self, SP, JT, DC). `asset_type` is eFD's asset category on PTRs (Stock, Corporate Bond, ...) and null for Part 4b rows, which have none. `transaction_type` is as eFD prints it (Purchase, Sale (Full), Sale (Partial), Exchange). `row_seq` is the row's 1-based position within its part of the report page (eFD's own `#` repeats in some 2014-2015 PTRs; it is kept in item_no). `amount_*` bounds the disclosed bracket; eFD never discloses an exact amount. The filing's dates and filer are in fd_filings.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/disast.tableComment: Canonical FEMA disaster-declaration record. One row per disaster-declaration-county-program-area combination. Partitioned by fiscal year declared (fyDeclared). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to sec.filing_metadata by state for risk-disclosure research. Refreshed daily (declarations issued continuously within 24h of signature). Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/DisasterDeclarationsSummaries. WARNING when using this table as a physical-hazard-exposure proxy: incident_type = 'Biological' covers the COVID-19 major disaster declarations of March-April 2020, issued once per state as a single non-geographic nationwide event. Left in a per-county or per-state declaration count, it registers as "a disaster" for nearly every county in the country and erases the physical-hazard variation a query is usually trying to measure. Filter incident_type != 'Biological' (or inspect the distinct incident_type values directly) before using declaration counts as a hazard-exposure or disaster-frequency metric.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/member_stock.tableComment: House members' (and their spouses' and dependent children's) STOCK Act Periodic Transaction Reports — stock, option and fund trades disclosed within 30-45 days of the transaction, from the Clerk of the House's own bulk financial-disclosure system. Not annual financial disclosures (outside income, asset/liability ranges, gifts) and not the Senate's parallel eFD filings, which are in fd_transactions (PTRs and annual-report transactions) and the other fd_* tables. `filing_id` groups the one or more transaction rows a single PTR lists; `row_seq` (from 1) is their order in the filing. `owner_code` is blank for the member's own holding, SP for a spouse, JT for a joint holding, DC for a dependent child. `asset_type_code` is the source's own abbreviation (ST, OP, OT, ...; see https://fd.house.gov/reference/asset-type-codes.aspx) with `ticker` parsed out of it separately when the source prints one; a private holding, fund or real property has no ticker. `asset_type_code` is null for 2015-2017 filings — that PTR template predates the asset-type-code column entirely (see member_stock_transactions_year_range comment). `amount_min`/`amount_max` are the disclosed bracket's bounds in dollars (`amount_max` null for the open-ended top bracket); the source never discloses an exact amount. Coverage starts in 2015, the earliest year the source's own filing-type coding distinguishes PTRs from other disclosure types; filings before 2015 exist but aren't identifiable as PTRs in the index.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/phmsa_.tableComment: PHMSA hazardous liquid pipeline accident reports (Form PHMSA F 7000-1), one row per accident, January 2010-present. phmsa.dot.gov itself 403s automated fetches; this pulls the identical bulk file from data.transportation.gov's open-data catalog instead — the catalog entry (resource 27nc-rsge) is a Socrata "href" pointer, not a queryable Socrata table, so the fetch targets its file attachment directly rather than the Socrata row API. Curated to a subset of the source's ~650 columns (safety outcome, cost, cause, and identity fields — not the full forensic investigation detail). Confirmed live: this snapshot is already deduplicated to one row per REPORT_NUMBER (no repeated SUPPLEMENTAL_NUMBER revisions), unlike the multi-supplemental versioning PHMSA's other endpoints can carry. For per-mile safety-rate normalization, join to phmsa_hazardous_liquid_mileage on operator_id + report_year. Only the 2010-present era is loaded; PHMSA also publishes three earlier eras (1986-2001, 2004-2009, pre-1986) under an incompatible pre-2010 form revision, not ingested here.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: Federal spending summarized by place-of-performance state x fiscal year — the spatial counterpart to the SOI revenue tables and one level up from the county-grain usaspending_by_county. Carries obligated_amount (all award types) alongside obligated_amount_excl_loans, which drops award types '07'/'08' (loans): loans report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's, which inflates place-of-performance totals for states with large loan servicers. CMS-funded awards are likewise attributed to the Medicare Administrative Contractor's state (North Dakota, Minnesota and Indiana host contractors paying Medicare claims for beneficiaries nationwide), so obligated_amount and obligated_amount_excl_loans are not a measure of spending landing in the state and must not be divided by population to rank states; use obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin for that. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/va_access.tableComment:
VA Access to Care facility-level appointment wait times, by facility and specialty — closes the wait-time/access-to-care gap in va_medical_facilities (which carries only identity/location). One row per (facility, specialty) as of the source's daily sliceEndDate. established_patient_wait_days / new_patient_wait_days are VA's own "estWaitTime"/"newWaitTime" days-to-third-next-available-appointment metrics; avg_wait_time_days is carried but was N/A for every row observed live 14 Sep 2026 (VA appears to have stopped publishing it — not fabricated as zero). Covers 20 specialty categories (AUDIOLOGY, CARDIOLOGY, DENTAL, DERMATOLOGY, ENDOCRINOLOGY, GASTROENTEROLOGY, NEUROLOGY, OB/GYN, OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY, ORTHOPEDICS, PAIN MEDICINE, PHYSICAL THERAPY, PODIATRY, PRIMARY CARE, PULMONOLOGY, SLEEP MEDICINE, UROLOGY, WOMEN'S HEALTH, OPHTHALMOLOGY, OPTOMETRY) — no dedicated Mental Health code exists in this legacy system (confirmed live: every apptType integer not in this list returns a byte-identical fallback response, not a Mental Health metric). The source's `patientType` query parameter (New_Patient/Established_Patient) was confirmed live to have no effect on the response — every row already carries both wait-time columns regardless — so it is a fixed request parameter here, not a dimension.
Snapshot table: the whole cross-product (state x specialty) is re-fetched and each state partition overwritten every run; history lives in Iceberg snapshots, not a year dimension. Source: VA's own public www.accesstocare.va.gov/PWT/getRawData API (no key, no auth; verified live against the real Antelope Valley VA Clinic, Lancaster CA — matches its known address and reported a 15-day AUDIOLOGY wait as of 2026-09-13). Coverage: 50 states + DC + PR (same set as housing.hmda_lar).
**Truncation risk**: the source returns a fixed legacy 32,768-byte response buffer, null-padded — not paginated. The largest state/specialty observed live (TX, PRIMARY CARE) used 28,841 bytes (88% of capacity); if a single state's facility count grows enough to exceed the buffer, that state's response would silently truncate mid-row rather than error. Re-verify content length if a future DQ run shows an implausibly low per-state facility count.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/lands/blm_oil_ga.tableComment:
Federal oil & gas lease acreage published by the Bureau of Land Management, one row per (state, fiscal_year), covering FY 2001-present. Two measures per row: leased_acres (BLM "Acreage in Effect", Table 2 — total federal oil & gas lease acreage still in force as of that fiscal year end) and producing_acres (BLM "Acreage of Producing Leases", Table 6 — the subset actually producing). Sourced from one combined XLSX per fiscal-year release; this table unpivots both wide sheets and joins on (state, fiscal_year) so each state-year gets a single row with both measures.
Enables per-acre royalty-productivity analysis when joined to lands.onrr_revenues on (state, fiscal_year) — revenue divided by producing_acres gives royalty per producing acre, matching the exact question this table was sourced for. Coverage is **Federal-only, excludes Indian leases** per BLM's own note in the source workbook — this is the same scope as onrr_revenues' Federal/land_class rows and joins cleanly on that basis. Table is a static snapshot: the whole file is re-fetched each run and the partition overwritten; history lives in Iceberg snapshots. No key required.
**URL drift caveat**: BLM publishes each new fiscal year's file at a URL that encodes the release month in the path (docs/2025-07/... for FY24 release, docs/2026-04/... for FY25 release, and so on). Rather than chase that per year, this table pins the URL to the FY24 file (published July 2025), whose combined XLSX already carries FY 2001-2024 in one download. On next FY release, update the URL to the newer file (whose combined XLSX will cover all years through the new one) — BLM's landing page at blm.gov/programs/energy-and-minerals/oil-and-gas/oil-and-gas-statistics is the authoritative index for locating the current URL.
**Known source quirk**: producing_acres exceeds leased_acres in a small number of rows (10 of 1200 in the FY24 file — Illinois, New York, Pennsylvania, Tennessee; excess ranges from 0.25 to ~150 acres). All affected states are minor producers; no major federal-lease state (Wyoming, New Mexico, Colorado, etc.) exhibits this. This reflects a reporting-boundary/timing difference between BLM's Table 2 (Acreage in Effect, point-in-time snapshot) and Table 6 (Producing Acres) rather than a join or parsing defect — treated as an expected small discrepancy, not a data quality failure.

NULL where the source cell is blank/null.\n"}

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/bill_text_ve.tableComment: Every published text version of a bill, one row per (version, format), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML; the `url` points at the text on govinfo.gov. `version_type` follows the bill through Congress using GPO's stage names — Introduced in House/Senate, Referred in Senate, Reported in House, Reported to Senate, Placed on Calendar Senate, Engrossed in House/Senate, Engrossed Amendment House/Senate, Considered and Passed House/Senate, Agreed to House/Senate, Enrolled Bill, Public Law, and older stage names such as Additional Sponsors House and Committee Discharged Senate. `format_type` is set only for the "United States Legislative Markup" (USLM) file; the plain XML row has NULL `format_type`. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/phmsa_.tableComment: PHMSA gas distribution pipeline incident reports (Form PHMSA F 7100.1), one row per incident, January 2010-present. Same data.transportation.gov open-data catalog route as phmsa_hazardous_liquid_incidents (catalog resource 27nc-rsge, the same multi-commodity "href" pointer entry; this fetches the Gas Distribution file attachment instead of the Hazardous Liquid one). Confirmed live: 1,550 rows, one per REPORT_NUMBER, no comma-padding rows (unlike the annual-report CSVs). Gas incidents report release volumes in thousand standard cubic feet (mcf) per Form field A7/A8, not barrels — unintentional_release_mcf/intentional_release_mcf are not comparable to phmsa_hazardous_liquid_incidents' _bbls columns. No offshore concept for local distribution systems (location_state_abbr/location_county_name only, unlike the onshore/offshore split gas transmission and hazardous liquid carry). Only the 2010-present era is loaded; PHMSA also publishes three earlier eras (1984-2004, 2004-2009 [sic, overlapping label on the source catalog], and 1970-mid1984) under incompatible earlier form revisions, not ingested here.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/banking/cra_smal.tableComment: Community Reinvestment Act aggregate small-business lending, from FFIEC's 2024 Aggregate flat file table A1-1 ("Small Business Loans by County -- Originations"). One record per (activity_year, state, county, msa_md, census_tract, income_group_total, report_level) reporting the number and dollar volume of small-business loans originated in that geography-and- income cell across all reporting institutions, broken out by loan-size bucket (<$100k, $100k-$250k, $250k-$1M) and separately for loans made to small businesses with gross annual revenues under $1M. Grain is set by report_level: NULL rows are the tract-x-income-group subtotals, '100' rows are the county-x-income-group totals, '200' rows are the county totals across all income groups, and '210' rows are the MSA/MD totals. Loan amounts arrive in thousands of USD from the source and are carried through unchanged. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: ffiec.gov/sites/default/files/data/cra/flat-files/{yy}exp_aggr.zip (one ZIP per activity year; 2016+ zips carry the per-table member cra{year}_Aggr_A11.dat, earlier years a single combined exp_aggr.dat holding every aggregate table — CraSmallBusinessLendingTransformer handles both and filters the combined stream to A1-1 records; 116-char fixed-width record layout parsed directly by that class — see it for why this table cannot use the shared file/etl HTTP+FIXED_WIDTH path).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/ntsb_a.tableComment: NTSB aviation accident & incident database — one row per aircraft involved in an event, with injury severity and fatal/serious/minor injury counts, aircraft damage level, FAR operating part, phase-of-flight code, probable-cause narrative, and event lat/lon. NTSB's own avall.zip is documented as spanning 1982-present, but the actual MIN(event_year) in this table should be checked directly (`SELECT MIN(event_year), MAX(event_year), COUNT(*) FROM ...` — there is no observedCoverage block here since this table has no year= partition to anchor one) rather than assumed from the source's nominal range. The download (avall.zip, ~95MB) is a single Microsoft Access database (avall.mdb, ~553MB) read in-JVM with Jackcess by NtsbAviationTransformer: the `aircraft` table (grain ev_id + Aircraft_Key) is streamed and joined to `events` (ev_id) and the `narratives.narr_cause` probable-cause text. The MDB has no county column, so only state_fips is derived (from USPS ev_state). Snapshot: the whole MDB is re-ingested and the partition overwritten each run. event_year is a column (not a partition) since one file carries all years; aircraft_n_number joins to faa_aircraft_master.n_number. Source: data.ntsb.gov/avdata/avall.zip.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/bill_related.tableComment: Bills the Congressional Research Service, the House or GPO link to a bill, one row per (bill, related bill, relationship), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `relationship_type` is one of Related bill, Identical bill, Companion bill, Cross-Congress related bill, Contained in public law, Public law contains the text, Procedurally related (also spelled Procedurally-related in older files), Related document, Text similarities, PrimaryCompanionBillBecameLaw, SecondaryCompanionBillBecameLaw; `identified_by` says who made the link (CRS, House, Senate, U.S. Government Publishing Office). `related_bill_type` uses the same lowercase slugs as `bill_type` (hr, s, hres, ...), so (related_congress, related_bill_type, related_bill_number) joins straight back to `bills`. The `related_latest_action_*` columns are the related bill's latest action as of this bill's last update and can lag `bills` for that bill. The source occasionally repeats an identical relationship, so the rows have no unique key.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/clinical_.tableComment:
Clinical trial studies from clinicaltrials.gov, one row per nct_id (PK) with overall_status, study_type, phase, enrollment_count, lead_sponsor, funder_type, and start/primary-completion/completion/update dates. Restricted by default to studies with a last-update-post-date on or after 2020-01-01. Joins to clinical_trial_conditions and clinical_trial_interventions (both on nct_id); see the trial_full view for a pre-joined denormalized version.
To reach a trial's lead sponsor's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on clinical_trials_nct_id = nct_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the sponsor's LEI/SEC CIK and this trial's nct_id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching lead_sponsor as text finds the wrong entities and misses sponsors filing under a differently-worded name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/lands/fia_tree_g.tableComment: USDA FIA growth-removal-mortality (GRM) annualized estimates by state, inventory year, species, and estimation type. Derived by joining per-state {ST}_TREE_GRM_ESTN.csv against {ST}_TREE.csv on TRE_CN to attach SPCD, then aggregating per-tree ANN_NET_GROWTH/REMOVALS/MORTALITY into per-group totals. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/stock_.tableComment: NOAA Fisheries Stock SMART assessment summaries for federally managed stocks: one row per stock assessment (about 3,500 assessments of ~430 stocks, assessment years 2005 to the latest), carrying the assessment's fishing mortality and biomass against the MSY reference points. f_fmsy_ratio above 1 means the assessed fishing rate exceeded Fmsy; b_bmsy_ratio below 1 means biomass was below Bmsy. A stock has several rows, one per assessment_year, so for current condition take each stock_id's latest assessment_year (or latest assessment_id); do not average across assessments. f_fmsy_ratio and b_bmsy_ratio are null where the assessment did not report an MSY proxy (many index-based and data-limited stocks), and f_unit / b_unit say what estimated_f and estimated_b are measured in (they are not comparable across stocks). is_fssi marks the Fish Stock Sustainability Index stocks. This is NOT the official Status of Stocks determination: NOAA publishes the overfished and overfishing flags only in PDF report tables, and they use per-stock thresholds (MSST, MFMT) that this table does not carry, so those flags are not here and must not be inferred from the ratios. Joins to noaa_commercial_landings on tsn (ITIS taxonomic serial number; null for some complexes) or scientific_name. Stocks span waters, not states: stock_area names the area (e.g. 'Gulf of Maine / Georges Bank') and jurisdiction the managing council or commission, so there is no state_abbr and a by-state rollup would double count; use region_name from the landings table to relate areas.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/fd_filings.tableComment: Every non-paper U.S. Senate financial-disclosure filing in the Senate eFD system (efdsearch.senate.gov), one row per filing: annual reports (Ethics in Government Act Parts 1-10), candidate and new-filer reports, STOCK Act periodic transaction reports (PTRs) and due-date-extension notices, for senators, former senators and candidates, by the year the report was filed. The detail of each filing is in fd_assets, fd_income, fd_transactions, fd_liabilities, fd_gifts, fd_travel, fd_positions, fd_agreements and fd_compensation (join on filing_id). `report_kind` is annual (annual, candidate and new-filer reports), ptr or extension_notice; `report_type` is the report's own type name. `view_status` is parsed when the report page was read, extension_notice when the filing is a notice with no report to read, and unavailable when the Senate no longer serves the page (candidate reports expire a year after the candidacy ends) — such filings are listed here but have no detail rows. Scanned paper filings (eFD's /search/view/paper/ pages, all of 2012-2013 and a few percent of later years) have no machine-readable text and are excluded; each year's count is logged by the ETL. `state` is the state eFD's per-state listing places the filer in; it is null for candidates and for the few senators that listing omits. Senate filings only: House annual reports are not sourced, and PTRs of the House are in member_stock_transactions. Use of these reports is restricted by 5 U.S.C. § 13107(c): not for credit rating, not for soliciting money, and commercial use only by news and communications media.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/mts_outlays.tableComment:
Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) Table 9 — federal receipts and outlays by OMB budget function/subfunction, published monthly (~8th business day after month-end), well ahead of OMB's own annual Historical Tables (see federal_outlays_by_function, which is the finalized full-year series with roughly a year's lag). Use this table for a current-fiscal-year "how much has been spent so far" question; use federal_outlays_by_function once the fiscal year closes and OMB's next edition finalizes it. Despite the "Table 9 — Summary" name in Treasury's own documentation, this table IS the by-function breakdown (confirmed live 2026-09-13): 33 classification_desc line items per record_date, covering both the receipts side (Individual Income Taxes, Corporation Income Taxes, Social Insurance and Retirement Receipts, Excise Taxes, and others) and the outlays side (National Defense, Medicare, Social Security, Net Interest, and others) via line_code_nbr (receipts: roughly 10-120; outlays: roughly 130-340). One row per (record_date, classification_desc) — current_fytd_rcpt_outly_amt is the fiscal-year-to-date cumulative figure as of that month-end, current_month_rcpt_outly_amt is that single month's amount, and prior_fytd_rcpt_outly_amt is the same fiscal-year-to-date point in the PRIOR fiscal year (Treasury's own year-over-year comparison column). Cross-checked live: FY2026 YTD through 2026-06-30 gives Net Interest (line_code_nbr='320') / Total (line_code_nbr='340') = 827.2B / 5517.9B = 14.99%.
The year dimension/partition below is CALENDAR year (Jan-Dec), not fiscal year — the ETL framework has no year+1 template variable to express an Oct-Sep fetch range in one filter string, so this iterates by calendar year instead (confirmed live 2026-09-13: a `record_date:gte:{year}-01-01,record_date:lte:{year}-12-31` filter returns all 12 months in one unpaginated call, same as avg_interest_rates' proven pattern). Every row still carries its own authoritative record_fiscal_year/record_fiscal_quarter columns from the source — filter on those for a fiscal-year query, not on the calendar-year partition.

Carries the auditee (name, address, EIN, UEI), the audit firm, the cognizant and oversight agencies, the opinion and internal-control findings flags and total federal dollars expended. auditee_uei is the placeholder GSA_MIGRATION for audit years 2016-2021 (filed before UEIs); auditee_ein is always present, so those years reach usaspending_assistance through the EIN-to-UEI mapping in the view fac_awards_vs_usaspending. EIN joins exempt_org_990 and ref.canonical_org_entity. Filings arrive up to 9 months after fiscal year end and are amended in place (resubmission_version, resubmission_status), and the file is a full daily extract, so each monthly run replaces the table. Contact people (names, e-mail, phone) are not loaded. Pre-2016 audits are in fac_audits_historic. Source: fac.gov/data/download (app.fac.gov/dissemination/public-data/gsa/full/general.csv).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/scotus_repor.tableComment: Every case decided by the U.S. Supreme Court and printed in the bound United States Reports on GovInfo: volumes 2 through 583, Court terms 1781 through 2017, about 30,800 cases. One row per case, partitioned by `year`, the term in which the volume's cases were decided (the first year of GovInfo's courtTerm; the earliest reporters span several years and count under their first). Terms from 2018 are in scotus_slip_opinions; scotus_cases combines the two. Outcome columns (`disposition`, `party_winning`, `votes_majority`, `votes_minority`, `chief_justice`, `opinion_writer`, `case_origin`, `cert_reason`, `scdb_issue_areas` and the rest of GovInfo's curated fields) come from GovInfo's MODS record, which takes them from the Supreme Court Database, and are present for volumes through 582 only; volume 583 (term 2017) has none, so `disposition` is derived from the opinion text and `disposition_source` says which. `disposition` uses one vocabulary either way: Affirmed (includes modified), Reversed, Reversed and remanded, Vacated and remanded, Affirmed and reversed (or vacated) in part [and remanded], Dismissed as improvidently granted. Text-derived values agree with the curated ones for about 96% of cases; the exceptions are how a remand is coded. `docket_numbers` are the Court's docket numbers read from the opinion (a consolidated case lists every docket whose number the text gives), not the SCDB-format `govinfo_docket_id`. `opinion_text` is the full text of the opinion PDF as extracted, in which the "fi" ligature loses its "i" (e.g. "affrmed", "fnal"). Original-jurisdiction cases have no disposition.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/officials/senate.tableComment: U.S. Senate statewide returns by candidate, every election 1976 to 2024 (25 even years plus the 2021 Georgia runoffs, 3,945 rows), from the MIT Election Data + Science Lab (CC0; Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/PEJ5QU, file 1976-2024-senate-state, found through the Dataverse API at each fetch so a new release is picked up; the dataset has no guestbook). One row per candidate per party line per election round: year, state, whether it is a special election, the stage, the candidate, the party label as published and a normalised major-party field, votes and the published total. Each cycle elects one class (33 to 35 seats) and special elections for vacated seats add rows with special=true in the same year (Georgia 2020 carries two Senate races, the regular Perdue-Ossoff one and the special Loeffler-Warnock-Collins one). Stages as published: gen general election; runoff a runoff (the 2022 file's GEN RUNOFF is stored as runoff); pre appears only for Georgia 1992 and 2008, where pre is the first-round general election and the same year's gen rows are the decisive runoff; the Georgia 5 January 2021 runoffs (Ossoff, Warnock) are stage runoff with year 2021, although they decide the 2020 cycle's two Georgia seats, so the 2020 gen rows of Georgia are first rounds. Fusion tickets: before 2024 a candidate on several party lines (New York, Connecticut) has a row per line and the vote is the SUM over rows; the 2024 New York rows carry one combined label such as DEMOCRATIC/WORKING FAMILIES. The views senate_race_results and senate_seats_won sum a candidate's lines and assign D or R when any line is a D or R line. Quirks kept as published: write-ins lumped in rows with candidate null (write_in_aggregate); vote buckets (Over Votes, Undervotes, Blank Vote, Scatter, Void, Other, None of these candidates) are candidate_kind residual; uncontested races (Louisiana 1978 to 1992 and a few others) carry candidate_votes 1 and total_votes 1 (uncontested=true), a placeholder; the unofficial flag is true for some 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2024 rows the Lab had not yet updated; version_date is the Lab's finalisation date and differs by row (2021-01-14 for 1976 to 2020, 2023-09-20 for 2022, 2024-12-12 and 2025-11-20 for parts of 2024); total_votes counts the ballots the state reports for the race and, where a state includes undervotes, can exceed the sum of candidate votes. Joins: state_fips to geo.state_ref.state_fips; state_name to officials.members.state_name (senators have district null there); candidate-level joins to members would be name matching and are not attempted (the Lab carries no bioguide id). The Congress that a class elected in year Y joins is (Y - 1786) / 2 (2024 is Congress 119). Source: https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/PEJ5QU.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/nass_livestoc.tableComment: USDA NASS QuickStats livestock and poultry inventory head counts by county and state, annual — cattle, hogs, sheep, chickens, turkeys, etc. Fetched with statisticcat_desc=INVENTORY only, so production/marketings for animals & products are not in this table. Tall layout; use commodity_desc + class_desc for a specific animal class and unit_desc for the unit (HEAD). reference_period_desc cadence varies by series: most classes report one annual snapshot ('FIRST OF JAN'), but on-feed cattle classes report a separate row per month ('FIRST OF JAN' through 'FIRST OF DEC') — summing across reference_period_desc for those classes double-, triple-, or 12x-counts the same animals rather than adding distinct populations. Filter to a single reference_period_desc before aggregating. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/edu/crdc_schools.tableComment: CRDC school-level civil-rights/equity data consolidated from four Urban Institute sub-endpoints, selected via the crdc_topic dimension: directory (charter/magnet/ alternative-school flags), chronic-absenteeism (chronically-absent student counts by race/sex/disability/LEP subgroup), offenses (firearm, homicide, rape, and assault incident counts), and teachers-staff (FTE teachers/certified-vs-uncertified/counselors/ psychologists/nurses/security/law-enforcement). Each row belongs to exactly one crdc_topic, so most columns are null outside their topic's rows. Joins to ccd_schools via ncessch (crdc_id equals ncessch for schools in the NCES universe; null ncessch means a non-NCES private/charter school with only a crdc_id). Collected by the Dept of Education Office for Civil Rights on an irregular, roughly-biennial schedule — not a strict 2-year interval, and not every topic shares the same loaded years: see observedCoverage below for the table-wide year set, but per-topic availability varies within it (e.g. offenses has no 2013 data even though teachers-staff does; year 2022 currently carries only chronic-absenteeism, not teachers-staff/offenses). CRDC's own known survey years are 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, and the 2020-21 cycle (which lands here as two separate years, 2020 and 2021, not consolidated into one) — 2011 is a known CRDC survey year with no rows currently loaded in this table.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/dart_a.tableComment: Annual adult fish passage counts at Columbia basin dams and fishways (Columbia Basin Research DART, from USACE and public utility district counts): Chinook, Jack Chinook, Steelhead, Wild Steelhead, Sockeye, Coho, Jack Coho, Chum, Pink, plus Shad, Lamprey and Bull Trout, one row per project x year x species. 17 projects on the Columbia, Snake, Yakima, Wenatchee and Willamette rivers; Bonneville back to 1938. This is the closest keyless run-size signal for WA and OR salmon (Bonneville is the first dam up the Columbia, so its Chinook/Steelhead/Sockeye counts approximate the total Columbia return); it is a passage count at a dam, not a per-stock escapement estimate. Adults counted at Lower Granite and the other Snake dams are headed to Idaho spawning grounds but the dams are in Washington, so state_abbrs gives the dam's location, and spans_states = true marks Columbia dams on the WA/OR border (BON, TDA, JDA, MCN): do not add those to a by-state sum. Counts are not additive across dams in the same river (the same fish is counted at each). Hatchery fish are included except where the species column says Wild.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/usgs_minera.tableComment: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (MCS) per-commodity salient statistics, long-format: one row per (release, commodity, country, statistic, statistic_detail, data_year). Covers production, imports, exports, consumption, price, reserves, capacity, employment, stocks, and net import reliance (statistic = 'Net import reliance') for ~127 mineral commodities — verified live 2026-09-11 against MCS 2026 (Copper NIR 38/44/41/41/45% for 2020-2024 matches the published USGS Copper chapter; Gallium NIR 100% every year matches zero US primary production). Joins to trade_imports/ trade_exports via `commodity` (name-based; no shared commodity code exists between USGS and Census HS classifications). `year` is the MCS release year (partition column); `data_year`/`data_year_text` is the calendar year (or, for a handful of multi-year aggregate rows, a text range like "2021-24") the statistic describes. `value_num` is null for a non-numeric annotation (USGS's own withheld/not-available markers) — the original text is preserved in `value_text`, never fabricated as a number. Hosted on ScienceBase (USGS's own data-release platform, not a third-party mirror); each release's item id is not derivable from its year, so this table is built by ScienceBase catalog discovery rather than a templated URL — see the provider class comment for the discovery mechanism.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/acs_count.tableComment: American Community Survey 5-year county-to-county migration flows: for each reference county (county_fips) and each other area it exchanged residents with, the people who moved IN from that area (lived there one year before the survey, live in the county now), the people who moved OUT to it, and the net, each with its 90 percent margin of error. It is origin-destination flow data, unlike acs_migration (counts by prior residence only). It is a survey of people, so it covers households that file no tax return and is not cut off at the IRS reporting threshold, but every figure is a sample estimate with a wide margin of error for small flows (moved_in_moe often exceeds moved_in). One row per vintage x reference county x other area. other_area_type says what the other area is: county (other_area_fips is a 5-digit county FIPS; the county-to-county flows), county_subdivision (a 10-digit county plus minor civil division code, in the states that publish MCD flows; these overlap the county rows, so filter them out before summing), or world_region (Asia, Europe and so on, other_area_fips NULL; moved_out and net are NULL because outbound moves abroad are not measured). year is the last year of the 5-year ACS window (year 2020 = ACS 2016-2020). Coverage 2010 through 2020: Census stopped publishing county-to-county flows after the 2016-2020 window (the 2017-2021 release is county-to-state only), so there is no later year. Each flow is listed from both ends, once under each reference county. Puerto Rico municipios appear from 2012. Join county_fips to geo.counties; join disasters.disaster_declarations on county_fips for flows in disaster-hit counties. Source: Census Data API api.census.gov/data/{year}/acs/flows (census.gov/topics/population/migration/guidance/ county-to-county-migration-flows.html). Requires CENSUS_API_KEY.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_count.tableComment: Provisional 12-month-ending drug overdose death counts by county of residence, from CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release (VSRR) program. Currently updated (not a frozen historical archive). County-level drug overdose mortality is NOT obtainable from CDC WONDER — its API rejects location grouping for National Vital Statistics System mortality data even though the interactive web UI offers it (confirmed live) — so this Socrata feed is the only public source for this grain. Counts of 1-9 are suppressed for privacy (see footnote).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/lobbying_fil.tableComment: Every lobbying filing made under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, one row per filing: LD-1 registrations (a lobbyist or firm registering to lobby for a client) and LD-2 quarterly activity reports, with their amendments and terminations. `filing_type` says which (decoded in lobbying_filing_types: RR = Registration, Q1 = 1st Quarter Report, and so on). The registrant is the lobbying firm or organization; the client is who it lobbies for (often the same when an organization lobbies for itself). `income` is what a lobbying firm reports receiving from the client and `expenses` is what an organization reports spending on in-house lobbying; each is set on only some filings, as reported (rounded by the filer). `filing_year`/`filing_period` is the reporting period the filing covers. What was lobbied on is in lobbying_activities and the people involved in lobbying_activity_lobbyists. Registrant contact names and telephone numbers and the name of whoever posted a filing are deliberately not carried. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.

The individual contributions are in lobbying_contribution_items and any PACs the filer controls in lobbying_contribution_pacs. The report's own address is not carried — for an individual it is a home address — only the filer's state and country. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/cfoi_state_.tableComment: BLS Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries (CFOI) workplace fatality rates by state of incident and industry sector, all ownerships (private and government combined), one partition per reference year from 2018 through the newest year BLS has published. The rate is fatal work injuries per 100,000 full-time-equivalent workers, computed by BLS from CFOI counts and state hours worked. One row per (jurisdiction, industry_sector, year) with a published rate; industry_sector is 'All industries' (the jurisdiction's overall rate) or one of 13 sectors: Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting; Mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction; Construction; Manufacturing; Wholesale and retail trade; Transportation and utilities; Information; Financial activities; Professional and business services; Education and health services; Leisure and hospitality; Other services, except public administration; Public administration. Answers "which state and industry combination has the highest fatality rate" and "how do death rates differ between industries and states". Where BLS printed "-" (fewer cases than the publication threshold, or no data) there is no row, not a zero, so most jurisdiction-by-sector cells are absent; the overall rate is published for every jurisdiction. Jurisdictions are the 50 states, DC (jurisdiction_type DISTRICT) and New York City (CITY), which BLS lists as an indented sub-row of New York: it is a subset of the New York rows, so do not add it to them, and its state_fips is null. State rows include government workers within their industry sector and BLS warns state rates are not comparable across states with different industry mixes or with national industry rates. Only rates are held here, not counts of deaths. Reference year Y is published by BLS between December of Y+1 and February of Y+2.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/snap_bene.tableComment: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) persons/households participating and total/average monthly benefits, by state x year x month — the nutrition- assistance counterpart to ssa_benefits_by_geography's income-benefits data, both geo-keyed and comparable against usaspending_by_state. USDA FNA publishes one zip covering FY1989-present (one workbook per fiscal year inside), not a per-year URL, so this table has no year fetch dimension — the provider parses the full history from one download and materialize partitions by the year column found in each row, same as fiscal's other single-workbook bulk sources. Excludes P-EBT (Pandemic EBT) figures, which USDA reports separately. FY2019 (Oct 2018-Sep 2019) carries a source-published distortion: because of the partial federal government shutdown, most February 2019 benefits were issued in January 2019, so month 1 of FY2019 shows roughly double a normal month's total_benefits_usd and month 2 shows almost none, and the per-state fiscal-year Total row (month IS NULL) averages persons and households over those two months as published, which pulls the FY2019 average persons_participating below the surrounding months.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/wildfi.tableComment: USFS Wildfire Risk to Communities (WRC) county-level summary — one row per county, from the workbook's own "Counties" sheet (3,144 rows, one per US county/equivalent). Forward-looking hazard/exposure measures, not after-the-fact burn perimeters (see wildfire_perimeters for those). Metrics are building-fraction-based (buildings_fraction_minimal/indirect/direct_exposure), not raw Census housing-unit counts — the closest federal equivalent to a "housing-unit risk" statistic, but a building-count proxy rather than a literal housing-unit statistic. burn_probability_* and risk_*_rank are state/national percentile ranks (0-1), not raw probabilities. Complements disasters.wildfire_perimeters (which records only fires that already happened) with a genuinely forward-looking hazard measure. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: wildfirerisk.org (official USFS product, mandated by the 2018 Consolidated Appropriations Act; hosted off the .fs.usda.gov domain, same acceptable pattern already used for housing.hud_subsidized_housing).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/weather/coops_hi.tableComment: Observed high and low water events (tide extremes) from NOAA CO-OPS NWLON tide gauges, one row per event per station: roughly 2 to 4 per station per day (H/L semidiurnal, HH/LL on mixed tides). Source is the CO-OPS Data API (product=high_low, api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov, keyless, public domain; requests are limited to 365 days, so the ETL pulls one station-year per call). Heights are meters above MLLW (current tidal epoch) in UTC time, as verified (preliminary for recent months). Stations inactive in a year return no rows. Pair with coops_tide_predictions: observed minus predicted extreme is the storm-surge / anomaly signal, precomputed in the coops_daily_surge view. Join coops_stations on station_id for state_fips, latitude and longitude, and to geo.state_ref; coastal flooding in the disasters schema joins on state. Great Lakes stations are excluded (no tides); currents are not included.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/ihp_va.tableComment: FEMA Individuals and Households Program (IHP) valid registrations aggregated to one row per disaster number x county (about 11,000 rows over the 634 disasters from DR-1439, November 2002, on), from OpenFEMA IndividualsAndHouseholdsProgramValidRegistrations v2 (26.2 million registration-level rows). Per row: registrations and their split by owner/renter, primary residence, reported home damage, destroyed, flood damage and FEMA inspection; eligibility and award counts for IHP, Housing Assistance, Other Needs Assistance, SBA, Transitional Sheltering; homeowner and flood insurance; the self-reported gross income bands and household size; and the dollars awarded, FEMA verified loss and unmet need. Adds to ihp_housing_assistance_owners/_renters (which are disaster x county x city x ZIP, keyed on FEMA's area name): income bands, insurance, household size, awards by type, destroyed and unmet need exist only here; the county is the damaged dwelling's own county, so a tribal area's registrations are assigned to the counties they sit in (the owners/renters tables leave those with a null county); and the registrations are not limited to the rows the housing-assistance tables publish. Joins to disaster_declarations on disaster_number and to geo.counties on county_fips. county_fips is the registration's own fips; about 3 percent of the registrations (whole counties of some disasters) carry none and take the code from the declaration of the same disaster number, state and area name (counted in fips_from_declaration_registrations); those a declaration does not resolve to one county have a null county_fips and one row per state and area name (80 rows, 1.0 percent of registrations). Nearly all of those are FEMA's catch-all disaster numbers 6001, 6405, 6501, 6502 and 9801-9808 (about 264,000 registrations, 1.0 percent, among them 199,864 in Camden County GA under DR-6502): they have no declaration, so they join to nothing in disaster_declarations and carry dates that do not match a disaster. Only registrations in Individual Assistance declared counties appear. Amounts are sums over registrations and are 0, never null, when nothing was awarded. Source: the OpenFEMA bulk Parquet file of the dataset (fema.gov/about/reports-and-data/openfema/v2/ IndividualsAndHouseholdsProgramValidRegistrationsV2.parquet), aggregated with DuckDB.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/ihp_ho.tableComment: FEMA Individuals and Households Program (IHP) housing assistance to RENTERS, one row per disaster number x county x city x ZIP (about 148,000 rows): valid registrations, FEMA inspections with a degree of damage (none, moderate, major, substantial; renters get no dollar damage figure because FEMA inspects only the items they own), and the assistance approved (rental, other needs; repair/replacement is not available to renters). Pair with ihp_housing_assistance_owners for the owner side. Joins to disaster_declarations on disaster_number and to geo.counties on county_fips. county_fips is taken from the declaration of the same disaster number and county name in disaster_declarations' source (DisasterDeclarationsSummaries designated areas), which is how FEMA spells the area; it is null for tribal areas (FEMA gives them no county) and for area names no declaration lists, and those rows still carry the ZIP code to join geo.zip_county_crosswalk. The county is as the applicant reported it (the system infers it from the address and the applicant may override it). Aggregate to county with GROUP BY disaster_number, county_fips; the view disasters_ihp_housing_by_county does that for owners and renters together. Declared disasters from DR-1439 (November 2002) on; only registrations in Individual Assistance declared counties appear, so a county that was not IA-declared has no row. Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/HousingAssistanceRenters.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/uscis_i76.tableComment:
Work-permit (Employment Authorization Document, EAD) applications processed by USCIS, from the quarterly Form I-765 report of the Department of Homeland Security / USCIS Chief Data and Analytics Office. One row per fiscal year x fiscal quarter x EAD eligibility category x filing type. The category is the immigration basis for the permit (ead_category codes such as A03 refugee, A055 granted asylum, A124/C19 TPS, C08 pending asylum application, C09 pending adjustment of status, C26 H-4 spouse of H-1B worker, C33 DACA; ead_category_description gives the USCIS wording). filing_type is Initial, Renewal, Replacement or Not Requested. Counts are receipts (applications received in the quarter), approvals and denials (decisions made in the quarter, which may relate to applications received earlier), and pending (applications awaiting a decision at quarter end). fiscal_year is the U.S. federal fiscal year (Oct 1 - Sep 30): fiscal_quarter 1 is October-December of the previous calendar year.
CAUTION: these are application FLOWS and a pending backlog, NOT counts of people currently holding a valid work permit, and one person can file more than once. There is no industry or occupation breakdown in any USCIS release; do not use this table for employment by industry. Counts are restated by USCIS in later releases. Pending cannot be reconstructed by summing quarters. Coverage starts at FY2025 (the earliest quarterly workbooks USCIS still publishes as xlsx); FY2026 Q1 is not published by USCIS and is absent. Source: https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/immigration-and-citizenship-data

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/trade_impor.tableComment: Monthly U.S. goods imports by HS-6 commodity and origin country, including CIF charges (Census International Trade timeseries, imports/hs endpoint). Tall layout: Census returns individual-country rows interleaved with its own built-in world-total and trade-bloc/continental aggregate rows in the same response, with no discriminator of its own — filter geo_level = 'country' before summing value_usd, or the total silently multiplies by every bloc/continent a country also belongs to (plus the world total). No quantity column: Census's GEN_QY1_MO/ UNIT_QY1 fields are unpopulated (always "0"/"-") at COMM_LVL=HS6, confirmed live across all 239,647 rows of a full month — quantity is only standardized at the HS10 grain, which this table doesn't fetch. trade_by_state's QTY_1_MO IS populated (state-level statehs endpoint reports it differently); use that table for quantity.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/irs_gross.tableComment:
IRS SOI Table 1-5, "Gross Collections, by Type of Tax and State" — one row per state/area per fiscal year, wide across the 11 tax-collection measures the table publishes. Sourced to close the gap federal_spending_vs_income_tax_by_state_year documents explicitly: that table carries individual income tax only, so a balance-of-payments computation built from it alone makes every state look net-positive (confirmed against the NY State Comptroller's official FFY2023 report, whose Rockefeller/OMB methodology finds NJ/MA/WA as real net donors). business_income_taxes (corporate) and excise_taxes here close the biggest part of that gap.
**Structural IRS limitation — cannot be fixed at ETL time**: IRS combines FICA with individual income tax withheld (individual_withheld_and_fica_tax), and SECA with individual income tax payments (individual_payments_and_seca_tax), in this state-level report. A clean payroll/FICA-only-by-state figure is not obtainable from any IRS SOI state-grain publication — this is the same reason federal_spending_vs_income_tax_by_state_year never carried it. The combined columns are still the correct denominator for a balance-of-payments computation (each captures both components), just not separable into payroll-tax-alone.
Non-state rows are kept, not dropped, matching soi_income_by_county's kept county-total convention: 'United States, total' (the national aggregate) and three non-state buckets IRS reports separately ('U.S. Armed Service members overseas and Territories other than Puerto Rico', 'Puerto Rico', 'International', 'Undistributed') all get state_abbr NULL — filter WHERE state_abbr IS NOT NULL for a clean 50+DC sum.
Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/{YY}dbs01t05co.xlsx (FY2019-2024 combined tax-type workbook; sheet name and filename convention both changed for FY2025 — see the source block). Scoped to FY2019+ (this modern combined-workbook format) rather than IRS's full history back to the 1990s — pre-2019 files are the legacy .xls binary format with a plausibly different layout, unverified and out of scope here.

The three native_born components are also exposed as their own columns — born_in_pr_island_areas in particular is analytically live on its own (most of Florida's Puerto Rico-born population), not just a summand. The full row identity is native_born + foreign_born = total_population, and at the component level born_in_us + born_in_pr_island_areas + born_abroad_american_parents + naturalized_citizen + not_a_citizen = total_population; both are DQ-asserted.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/environment/egri.tableComment: EPA eGRID (Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database) regional emission rates — one row per eGRID subregion per year (~27 subregions, e.g. RFCE, CAMX, ERCT), with annual net/nonbaseload generation, total NOx/SO2/CO2/CO2e emissions, overall output emission rates (lb/MWh, all fuels combined), and per-fuel-type output emission rates for NOx/SO2/CO2 broken out by coal, oil, gas, and fossil-fuel-total (also lb/MWh), plus each fuel's share of subregion generation (coal/oil/gas/nuclear/hydro/ renewables generation_pct). This is the SRL (subregion) tab of eGRID's multi-tab XLSX workbook — the workbook also carries UNT/GEN/PLNT (unit/generator/plant-level) and ST/BA/NRL/US (state/balancing-authority/NERC-region/national) tabs; none of those have this fuel-type breakdown (plant-level rates are for the whole plant, dominated by its single primary fuel) and none are in this table. EPA publishes eGRID roughly every 1-2 years, historically each January of year+2 (eGRID2023, released 2025-01 and revised 2025-06, covers 2023 generation/emissions). The download URL is unpredictable — it embeds a publish date and a revision suffix that both vary by year and are not derivable from the data year — so this transformer discovers the year's workbook link by scraping EPA's historical-egrid-data listing page, falling back to download-data for the most-recently-released vintage (not yet moved to the historical archive at build time, 2026-08-02, eGRID2023 was download-data-only). A year with no discoverable link yields zero rows for that year, not an error — check the ETL log for "no data workbook link found" to distinguish "not published this way" from a real failure.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/mrip_r.tableComment: NOAA Fisheries MRIP recreational fishing effort, in angler trips, by year x wave x state x fishing mode x area fished, 1981 to the latest published year, with standard error and percent standard error. One trip is one angler fishing for one day. Pair with mrip_recreational_catch (same keys) to compute catch per trip. Atlantic and Gulf coasts from Maine to Mississippi plus Hawaii; Louisiana, Texas, the Pacific coast and Alaska are absent from recent years. Florida appears under two sub-regions (South Atlantic and Gulf of America). A null angler_trips is an estimate MRIP did not produce for that cell, not zero trips. Standard errors do not add across rows. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_place.tableComment: CDC PLACES model-based county estimates of adult chronic disease, health-risk-behavior, prevention, disability and social-need prevalence (Socrata swc5-untb, 2025 release; data years 2022 and 2023), ~3,000 counties x ~40 measures x crude/age-adjusted. This is the county-grain source for asthma (measureid CASTHMA, 'Current asthma among adults'), COPD, coronary heart disease, diabetes, etc.; cdc_brfss carries the same topics only at state grain. Estimates are small-area model outputs from BRFSS (or ACS) with 95% confidence limits, not counts of cases; data_value is a percent of adults. Each county-measure appears twice (Crude and Age-adjusted prevalence) — filter data_value_type to avoid double counting. Covers disease prevalence only; EPA regulatory-impact-analysis projections (avoided deaths/illnesses per rule) are per-rule PDF documents with no structured feed and are not in this table. CDC republishes PLACES under a new Socrata dataset id each annual release, so the source url here is a re-verify-on-new-release item.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/cdfw_g.tableComment: California Department of Fish and Wildlife GrandTab adult Chinook salmon escapement for the Central Valley (Sacramento River system), served by SacPAS (Columbia Basin Research): annual escapement, i.e. adult fish that returned from the ocean to spawning areas or hatcheries, for the four runs (Winter, Spring, Fall, Late-Fall) split by origin (In-River natural spawning vs Hatchery), one row per run x origin x year with an estimate, 1952 onward (years with no estimate are absent, not zero). state_abbr is always CA. This is the California run-size series for Chinook; add In-River and Hatchery for a run total, and sum the four runs for the Central Valley total (the SacPAS 'All' selections are those sums and are not stored again). Values for the latest years are preliminary (is_preliminary = true) and are revised. Sacramento system only: San Joaquin tributaries and per-stream breakdowns are not in this table, and the Klamath and Smith basins are not covered by GrandTab. Estimates mix methods (carcass mark-recapture, video weirs, redd expansion, hatchery counts), so year-to-year jumps can partly reflect method changes.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/entitleme.tableComment: Social Security and Medicare spending by place-of-performance state x fiscal year, isolated by CFDA/assistance-listing number rather than derived from usaspending_by_state's award-type totals — the entitlement-program counterpart to that table and to ssa_benefits_by_geography (which carries SSA's own county-grain administrative beneficiary/program detail but lags further due to its Wayback-archive dependency). The two Medicare programs inherit the same place-of-performance distortion documented on usaspending_by_state's obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin column: CMS-funded awards report place of performance at the Medicare Administrative Contractor's location, not the beneficiary's, so states hosting a MAC (e.g. ND/Noridian, MN, IN, KY, PA, SC, CT) show implausibly large totals relative to population — confirmed live at FY2025 scale for both Medicare programs here. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_drug_.tableComment: Provisional national and HHS-region drug overdose death counts by named drug, from CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release (VSRR) program (Socrata 8hzs-zshh). Currently updated. Drugs are fentanyl, heroin, oxycodone, cocaine, methamphetamine, amphetamine, xylazine, ketamine, MDMA, gabapentin, bromazolam and mitragynine. Each row is one jurisdiction x month x drug and the period is a 12-month-ending window: a row is the count over the twelve months ending in its month. A death is counted under every drug involved, so drug counts overlap and must not be summed. Jurisdictions are 'United States' and the ten HHS regions ('Region 1' to 'Region 10'), by state of occurrence. This is the table for separating fentanyl and other illicit-drug involvement from prescription opioids such as oxycodone; state-level opioid drug classes are in cdc_state_drug_overdose_deaths, and prescription dispensing volume is in cdc_opioid_dispensing_rates_state and cdc_opioid_dispensing_rates_county.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/housing/county_h.tableComment: FHFA annual all-transactions House Price Index at county grain (developmental series), 1975 through the latest published year. One row per (county, year). Complements house_price_index, whose master file stops at state/MSA/national: this is the only county-level price index in the corpus, so it supports county-pair event studies (e.g. FEMA declarations in disasters.disaster_declarations against geo.county_adjacency neighbors). annual_change_pct is the year-over-year percent change; hpi is cumulative appreciation indexed to 100 in the county's first recorded year; hpi_1990_base / hpi_2000_base rebase to 100 in 1990 / 2000 and are null for counties with no value in that base year. County-years with samples too small to publish are absent or null (FHFA reports "."). Nominal, not inflation- adjusted. Snapshot table: the whole workbook is re-fetched and overwritten each run. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: fhfa.gov/hpi/download/annual/hpi_at_county.xlsx.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_nndss.tableComment: Weekly provisional case counts for nationally notifiable infectious diseases (measles, pertussis, mumps, salmonellosis, Lyme disease, tuberculosis-adjacent conditions not already covered by cdc_wonder_tb, and ~130 others), from CDC's National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS). State/territory/HHS-region/national grain, by MMWR year and week. Currently updated weekly (confirmed live 2026-09-27: latest data is MMWR week 37 of 2026). disease carries a suffix distinguishing case classification for some conditions (e.g. "Measles, Imported" vs "Measles, Indigenous" — sum both for a total). current_week_count/previous_52_week_max/cumulative_ytd_current_year/ cumulative_ytd_previous_year are the source's four case-count measures; each has a companion _flag column that is populated INSTEAD of the count when CDC did not publish a number — see each flag column's comment for the code meanings. Do not treat a NULL count as zero; a flag value of "-" (no reported cases) is the only code that means zero, "U" (unavailable) and "NN"/"N" (not nationally/jurisdictionally notifiable) are not. Complements cdc_wonder_std_morbidity (STI-specific, 1984-2014, frozen) and cdc_wonder_tb (tuberculosis-specific, 1993-2024) with a live, broader disease panel; there is no county grain here (NNDSS publishes at state/territory grain only). reporting_area/location1/ location2 casing is inconsistent across years in the source itself (confirmed live 2026-09-27: ALL CAPS for 2022 rows, mixed case e.g. "Connecticut" for current 2026 rows) — use UPPER()/LOWER() when joining or filtering on state name rather than assuming one casing convention.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/exempt_or.tableComment: Nonprofit/tax-exempt financials from IRS Form 990 e-file XML — one row per filing (OBJECT_ID) for the IRS receipt year. The provider reads the per-year index CSV, then streams each TEOS XML zip, extracting header identity and Part I summary financials with version-defensive local-name matching across 990 / 990-EZ / 990-PF. For full Form 990 returns (return_type 990) it also carries Part I line 15 (salaries, other compensation, employee benefits) and line 16b (fundraising expenses), the Part IX line 25 functional-expense columns (A total, B program service, C management and general, D fundraising), Part IX line 5 officer compensation, and the Part VII Section A compensation columns D/E/F summed over the listed persons; these are null on 990-EZ, 990-PF and 990-T returns, which do not report those parts. Overhead ratio is functional_expenses_mgmt_general + functional_expenses_fundraising over functional_expenses_total. NTEE is not in the XML — join to exempt_org_master on ein. Joins to ref/EIN. Source: apps.irs.gov/pub/epostcard/990/xml/{YEAR}/. Two indexed receipt-2023 filings, 202313409349100901 (Aurora Care Foundation Inc, 990-PF) and 202301929339300110 (Northwestern Memorial Hospital, 990-T), are in no published IRS zip and are absent from the table; the load logs and counts each as known absent and fails on any other indexed filing it cannot find.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/pesticide_use.tableComment: USGS NAWQA Pesticide National Synthesis Project estimated annual agricultural pesticide use by county, active-ingredient compound, and year — low and high estimate methods (epest_low_kg / epest_high_kg, kilograms applied) for the conterminous United States, reflecting two different assumptions used when Crop Reporting District-level survey data was incomplete. Compiled from every county-level release the source currently publishes: final annual files for 1992-2012, the 2013-17 (ver 2.0) consolidated final release, and single-year preliminary releases thereafter. Preliminary years cover far fewer compounds than the finalized series — 2019 holds only 69 of the ~400 compounds present in 2013-2018 — because USGS calculates preliminary estimates as soon as data becomes available from its survey provider, ahead of the full compound set. A finalized 2018-2022 release restoring the full compound list is scheduled by USGS for December 2026 and will replace these preliminary partitions on reprocess; until then, filter to year <= 2018 for a compound set that is stable across years. Excludes seed-treatment pesticide application beginning in 2015 (the survey provider discontinued those estimates) and excludes the separate state-level-by-crop-group series (different grain, not in this table). Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/nass_farm_ope.tableComment: USDA NASS QuickStats farm counts and farm-size distribution — Census of Agriculture (source_desc=CENSUS, every 5 years: 1997, 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022; county- and state-level) plus the annual "Farms and Land in Farms" survey (source_desc=SURVEY, state-level only). Tall layout: filter domain_desc='AREA OPERATED' + statisticcat_desc='OPERATIONS' for farm count by acreage size class (domaincat_desc, e.g. 'AREA OPERATED: (1,000 OR MORE ACRES)'), domain_desc='ECONOMIC CLASS' for farm count by sales-value size class, or domain_desc='TOTAL' + statisticcat_desc='OPERATIONS' for the plain total farm count. statisticcat_desc='AREA OPERATED' carries acres operated (farm size in acres, not a count) under the same domain breakdowns. Also carries organic-status, financing-source, and NAICS-classification breakdowns for the same farm population — filter statisticcat_desc/domain_desc for the measure needed. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code; combine with nass_land_values (land value per acre) for farm-consolidation-vs-land-value analysis.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/officials/federa.tableComment: Every Article III federal judge ever commissioned, from the Federal Judicial Center's own Biographical Directory of Article III Federal Judges export. Verified against a live download (2026-08-01): the real CSV is 201 columns wide — up to 6 repeating groups of ~33 court/appointment columns each (a judge elevated District -> Circuit -> retired-then-recalled etc. gets multiple groups), plus separate "Other Federal Judicial Service", "School"/"Degree", and free-text career columns. This table maps a curated 12-of-33 fields per group (the appointment-identity and confirmation-timeline columns) and drops the education/career/committee-vote detail for MVP scope — not a parsing limitation, a deliberate cut. Ingested as one row per judge (one source, minimal reshape); a future `federal_judgeships` view could UNION ALL the 6 groups into one row per appointment if downstream queries need that grain.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/phmsa_.tableComment: PHMSA hazardous liquid pipeline operators' annual report (Form PHMSA F 7000-1.1), Part A (operator identity) through Part E (pipe-age distribution) fields, one row per (report_year, operator, commodity) — the per-mile normalization denominator for phmsa_hazardous_liquid_incidents (join on operator_id + report_year). Same data.transportation.gov bulk-file route as the incidents table (catalog resource aemm-7pyq, an "href" pointer; this fetches its file attachment directly). The source ZIP splits each year's annual report into ~11 "Part" CSVs (Part A-E, F-G, H, I, ... R); only the Part A-E file is ingested here, since it alone carries total_miles (Part D) and mileage-by-installation-decade (Part E) — the fields this warehouse needs. Confirmed identical column layout across 2017-2024 (the years the source publishes as separate Part-CSVs; extractPattern merges all matching entries into one table). 2010-2016 exist only as whole-workbook XLSX files (one per year, sheet "HL AR Part A to E") rather than separate Part-CSVs, but confirmed live to carry the exact same 88-column header as the 2017+ era — a PhmsaHazardousLiquidMileageHistoricalTransformer responseTransformer parses those years via POI and appends them to the 2017+ CSV text extractPattern already produces, so this table now covers 2010-present.

Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/HousingAssistanceOwners.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/weather/asos_obs.tableComment: Sub-daily surface observations (one row per METAR report) for the 15 US airport ASOS stations that prediction-market daily-high-temperature contracts settle on: KLAX, KMIA, KAUS, KATL, KSFO, KSEA, KHOU, KLGA, KNYC (Central Park), KMDW, KORD, KDEN, KBKF, KDFW, KDAL. Source is the Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS archive (https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/asos.py), a university-hosted mirror of NWS/FAA ASOS and MADIS METAR feeds, not an agency endpoint; re-verify if it starts failing. report_type separates three feeds: 'routine' (hourly METAR, ~minute :53), 'special' (SPECI, issued when conditions change), and '5min' (MADIS high-frequency METAR, every 5 minutes, available from about 2016). Years before a feed existed return no rows for it. observation_time_utc is UTC. Temperatures are kept as reported: air_temp_f / air_temp_c are IEM's parse of the METAR body (whole degrees; null on 5min rows), temp_c_tgroup is the exact tenths-of-a-degree Celsius from the METAR remarks T-group (present on most rows, including 5min), and metar is the full raw report text. A 5-minute and a routine report can share one minute, so (station_id, observation_time_utc, report_type) is not unique; add metar for a unique key. -61 C in temp_c_tgroup (METAR 'M61/M61') is the ASOS sensor-missing marker, kept as reported; filter it when taking daily maxima/minima. air_temp_f/air_temp_c occasionally disagree with the raw report, so prefer temp_c_tgroup when precision matters. The daily maximum over observation_time_utc rows differs from the official NWS daily climate-report maximum (ghcnd_daily tmax_c); this table is the record needed to reproduce the highest-observation-of-the-day measure. Use observation_date (UTC day) to group, not local day. No auth needed.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/omb_appor.tableComment: OMB-approved apportionments (SF-132 schedules) for every federal budget account, one row per schedule line of each approval iteration, by fiscal year FY2022-present. Apportionment is the step where OMB releases appropriated budget authority to an agency by quarter or by project, so this is where withheld, deferred or footnoted-away funds show up: the free-text footnote_text column carries OMB's conditions on the money, including language withholding funds pending review and proposed-rescission or deferral notices. It is the account-level counterpart to mts_outlays_by_function and federal_outlays_by_function, which stop at function totals. Key by (tafs_iteration_id, line_number, line_split); a later iteration of the same account (iteration) restates the whole schedule, so compare iterations rather than summing them. line_number is the SF-132 line (1000 = unobligated balance brought forward, 1100/1200 = appropriations, 1920 = total budgetary resources, 6001-6004 = category A apportioned by quarter, 6190 = total budgetary resources available); approved_amount is in dollars as published. begin_poa/end_poa are the period of availability years and availability_type_code is 'X' for no-year money. A footnote no line references is kept as a row with null line_number. Covers OMB apportionment actions only: GAO Impoundment Control Act decisions and the rescission packages transmitted to Congress are separate publications and are not in this table. Source: apportionment-public.max.gov, the JSON rendition of each posted apportionment.

Sorting a mixed set by period_instant alone silently buries every duration-context row behind NULL-sorts-first semantics, reading as \"coverage stopped here\" when it hasn't (see the sec-filing-contexts-mixed-instant-duration-sort recipe). The two source columns are perfectly complementary in production (confirmed live: 0 rows with both NULL, 0 rows with both populated), so this COALESCE has no ambiguous case to special-case.\n"},{"id":12,"name":"segment","required":false,"type":"string","doc":"NULL for a consolidated (company-wide) fact; non-NULL for a fact broken out by a sub-category. THIS IS THE JOIN PATH TO DIMENSIONAL BREAKDOWNS — loan class, business segment, geography, product line. Format is a semicolon-joined list of XBRL \"Axis=Member\" pairs, e.g. \"us-gaap:FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis= fbc:CommercialRealEstateLoansMember; us-gaap:FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis= fbc:MortgageLoansHeldForInvestmentMember\" — the Member after each '=' names the actual sub-category and is namespaced to the FILER'S OWN taxonomy prefix (here 'fbc:'), not a fixed vocabulary, so search it with ILIKE on the category name (e.g. '%CommercialRealEstate%', '%Office%', '%Multifamily%') rather than an exact match. To pull the dollar value for a sub-category: find its context_id here (filtering segment + cik + accession_number to one filing keeps this cheap), then join financial_line_items.context_ref = context_id (same cik + accession_number) and read value_numeric there for the concept you want.\n"},{"id":13,"name":"scenario","required":false,"type":"string","doc":"Scenario dimension information (XML fragment)"}]}

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/industry_gd.tableComment:
GDP by industry from the BEA GDPbyIndustry dataset, national, annual and quarterly, across the 22 BEA summary industry groups (11 agriculture through 81 other services, plus GFG/GFE/ GSLG government). TableID=ALL is requested, so all 39 BEA tables land here and table_id selects the measure: 1 value added in millions of dollars, 5 value added as a percent of GDP, 6 components of value added, 7 those components as a percent of value added, 8 and 11 chain-type quantity and price indexes, 10 real value added. Units are a property of table_id, not of the row — the units column is always null because GDPbyIndustry returns no per-row unit.
On the component tables (6 and 7) industry_description carries the COMPONENT name rather than the industry name: 'Gross operating surplus', 'Compensation of employees', 'Taxes on production and imports less subsidies', plus one row named for the industry that totals to 100 percent (table 7) or to total value added (table 6). Gross operating surplus is BEA's profit measure, so table 7 gives an industry profit margin directly — filter industry_description = 'Gross operating surplus' and read value as percent of value added. Use industry_code to pick the industry on those tables, not industry_description.

Joins to national_forests via forest_code and to geo.states via state_abbr. Units_accomplished and uom describe harvest volume (CCF, MBF, ACRE, etc.).
