Source: EDW_TimberHarvest_01/MapServer/{layer} where layer is dispatched per year by UsfsTimberLayerResolver — layer 11 covers 2021+, layer 0 covers 2011-2020, and layers 1-7 could in principle reach as far back as 1820, but this table is only ever fetched from GOVDATA_START_YEAR forward (see observedCoverage below for the real floor actually loaded) — the 1820 figure describes what the source's older layers contain, not what's in this table. The service hard-caps maxRecordCount at 2000 regardless of the requested resultRecordCount (a single year can hold 4x that); UsfsFactsTransformer pages on exceededTransferLimit via resultOffset rather than making one request per year. All layers publish the identical 71-field schema.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/nass_crop_pro.tableComment: USDA NASS QuickStats field-crop statistics — production, area planted, area harvested, yield, condition, and progress — by county, state, and nation (agg_level_desc COUNTY, STATE, NATIONAL; NATIONAL rows carry state_alpha 'US' and state_fips_code '99', with a null county_fips). NASS publishes its own national estimate, which is not the sum of the state rows, so use NATIONAL rather than summing states for a national series. Tall layout — filter statisticcat_desc for a specific measure and unit_desc for its unit; reference_period_desc is annual ('YEAR') for production/yield/area but weekly ('WEEK #nn') or monthly for condition/progress measures, so filter statisticcat_desc before comparing reference_period_desc across rows. NassQuickStatsTransformer drops the in-season vintages NASS also publishes for production/yield/area (reference_period_desc 'YEAR - AUG/SEP/OCT/NOV FORECAST' or 'YEAR - JAN/MAR/JUN/AUG/ SEP/OCT/DEC ACREAGE') so this table carries only each year's final published annual estimate for those measures, not every in-season revision. agg_level_desc carries COUNTY and STATE rows for the same commodity/year side by side, each independently summing to the true total (COUNTY rows for a state already sum to that state's STATE row, including 'OTHER (COMBINED) COUNTIES' placeholder rows — one per asd_code — for counties NASS suppresses from individual disclosure); filter to a single agg_level_desc before aggregating, since summing across levels multiplies the total. PRODUCTION additionally carries a parallel unit_desc='$' series (crop value) alongside the physical unit_desc='BU' series for the same key; filter unit_desc to one before summing — combining agg_level_desc and unit_desc unfiltered inflates a national PRODUCTION total roughly 5x. domain_desc/domaincat_desc and class_desc are further crosstab dimensions, not row-count noise — 'TOTAL'/'ALL CLASSES' is the aggregate row, everything else is a breakdown (e.g. domain_desc 'ECONOMIC CLASS', class_desc a named cultivar); filter both to 'TOTAL'/'ALL CLASSES' for a single per-geography annual figure. Likewise prodn_practice_desc/util_practice_desc distinguish irrigated-vs-not and grain-vs-silage submeasures — filter to 'ALL PRODUCTION PRACTICES'/the desired utilization for a single total. source_desc is 'SURVEY' (the continuous annual series) or 'CENSUS' (the quinquennial Census of Agriculture, years ending 2 or 7); most CENSUS rows have no SURVEY counterpart and carry commodities/geographies SURVEY doesn't cover, but where both report the identical annual total ('TOTAL'/'YEAR') for the same commodity/class/practice/ geography, NassQuickStatsTransformer drops the CENSUS duplicate so the annual series stays single-valued and comparable year over year. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code; also joinable to disasters drought/storm tables by county+year for yield-impact analysis. For the current season's weekly condition and progress with week-ending dates and national rows, use nass_crop_progress.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_state.tableComment: State-level monthly provisional counts of live births, deaths, and infant deaths, from CDC's Vital Statistics Rapid Release (VSRR) program. State-level Natality is NOT obtainable from CDC WONDER — its API rejects location grouping for NVSS data even though the interactive web UI offers it (confirmed live) — so this Socrata feed is the only public source for state-grain birth counts. Also gives state-level all-cause and infant mortality trend, independent of cdc_mortality (data.cdc.gov, different endpoint) and cdc_wonder_cause_of_death (national-only, cause-specific).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/weather/hms_smok.tableComment: NOAA Hazard Mapping System (HMS) satellite smoke detection aggregated to county level. Daily smoke coverage by density category (smoke_coverage_pct, heavy_smoke_pct, medium_smoke_pct, light_smoke_pct). NESDIS's own polygon archive is available from 2005, but this table's own observedCoverage below is the source of truth for what's actually loaded here — check it rather than assuming a 2005 floor or full year-to-year continuity (there is currently a 2014 gap). Downloads daily smoke polygon shapefiles from NESDIS (https://satepsanone.nesdis.noaa.gov/pub/FIRE/web/HMS/Smoke_Polygons/Shapefile/), performs a JTS spatial intersection against TIGER/Line county boundaries, and emits per-county coverage percentages. One batch per year+month; each batch processes all days in that month. The raw smoke plume polygon geometries (WKT) behind these percentages are retained separately in hms_smoke_polygons for spatial re-analysis against other boundaries. Uses HmsSmokeSpatialJoinProvider.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/eia_power.tableComment: EIA Form 860 annual electric generator inventory. One row per generator (plant + generator ID + year), sourced from BOTH the archive's "Operable" sheet and its "Retired and Canceled" sheet (2011 onward; earlier archives carry only an operable-equivalent). A generator therefore has a row in a given report_year's archive whether it was running that year or had already stopped — filter operating_status IN ('RE','CN') to isolate the latter, and read retirement_year for when it actually happened, as distinct from planned_retirement_year (a forecast made while still operating). Includes plant and utility identifiers, geographic location (state, county, city, lat/lon), NERC region, balancing authority, technology, prime mover, energy sources, capacity (nameplate, summer, winter, minimum load), ownership type, and energy storage flag. Transformer downloads and parses the annual ZIP archive from EIA. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_utility_annual via utility_id.

Station-level port counts by charging level (ev_dc_fast_num / ev_level1_evse_num / ev_level2_evse_num) and available connector types (ev_connector_types, comma-separated — e.g. CHADEMO, J1772, J1772COMBO, TESLA). Source: developer.nlr.gov (NREL's API host as of the 29 May 2026 migration off the retired developer.nrel.gov domain; confirmed live).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/hospital_.tableComment: CMS Hospital Provider Cost Report (HCRIS) financials — one row per hospital per cost-reporting fiscal year, from CMS's own pre-aggregated extract (no raw HOSP-10 worksheet join needed; CMS already did it). Current snapshot only (FY2023, ~6,100 hospitals, verified live 2026-09-11) — CMS replaces this dataset in place with each year's newly finalized cost reports, so there is no per-year id to backfill history from; a prior year's data is not retrievable through this API once superseded. Cross-checked live: Mayo Clinic Hospital Rochester (CCN 240010) shows Net Patient Revenue ~$3.70B, Net Income ~$1.24B for FY2023 — plausible for a major academic medical center. Financial fields are as CMS reports them (a facility with a fiscal year spanning parts of two calendar years is assigned to fiscal_year by its Fiscal Year End Date). Joins to cms_pos_facilities/cms_pos_termination_history via provider_number (CCN) for a real payer-mix-vs-closure-risk analysis — the pairing ops#186 originally asked for. Also carries this same CMS extract's balance-sheet and operating-expense fields (cash_on_hand, current/total assets and liabilities, total_operating_expense, depreciation_cost, cost_to_charge_ratio) — the source for an operating margin (net_income_from_patient_services / total_patient_revenue) or days-cash- on-hand ((cash_on_hand / (total_operating_expense - depreciation_cost)) * 365) ratio; neither ratio is stored precomputed since either can be divide-by-zero for a facility with no reported operating expense. Confirmed live 2026-09-26: this same CMS dataset (44060663-47d8-4ced-a115-b53b4c270acb) has no Medicare-specific, self-pay/uninsured, or private-insurance revenue field — only Medicaid and stand-alone CHIP are broken out; a Medicare/uninsured/ private payer-mix split is not available from this extract.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fec/independent_.tableComment:
Independent expenditures — spending by committees and individuals for or against candidates that is not coordinated with the candidate's campaign. Includes Super PAC spending. Source: independent_expenditure_{YYYY}.csv (CSV with headers).
FEC accepts filings without amount-plausibility vetting, so the bulk file carries spam/prank line items of $50M to $10B (e.g. 2022 and 2024 candidates filing $9,999,999,999-scale "expenditures"); a raw SUM(amount) is inflated roughly 10x to 23x in 2022, 2024 and 2026. Every row is kept and amount is never altered; amount_implausible marks the rows to exclude. Any total, ranking or per-candidate aggregate of amount must filter WHERE amount_implausible IS NOT TRUE. A filer amending a filing resubmits the whole thing under a new file_num (amendment_indicator A1/A2/A3, prev_file_num naming the file_num it replaces) rather than correcting it in place, so the superseded filing's rows stay in this table alongside the amendment — use the independent_expenditures_current view (superseded_by_amendment) to exclude them from a SUM/count.

The FeatureServer view is named "Class I Railroads" but its RROWNER1 (dispatcher/owner) field is not itself restricted to Class I carriers — hundreds of short- line/regional/passenger owner codes are also present in the underlying segments (verified live 2026-09-21) — so the source query filters RROWNER1 to the current AAR Class I roster (BNSF, CSXT, NS, UP, CN, CPKC) explicitly and aggregates server-side (GROUP BY STCNTYFIPS, RROWNER1; SUM(MILES), COUNT(OBJECTID)). s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/esa_sa.tableComment: Endangered Species Act status of every Pacific salmon, steelhead and Atlantic salmon listing entity from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service ECOS species report (NOAA Fisheries is the lead agency for these): one row per Evolutionarily Significant Unit (salmon) or Distinct Population Segment (steelhead, Atlantic salmon), covering Chinook, coho, chum, sockeye, pink, steelhead and Atlantic salmon. esa_status gives the designation (Threatened, Endangered, Experimental Population, Non-Essential, Under Review, Resolved Taxon, Status Undefined, Not Listed), status_category the listed / not listed / petitioned bucket, and listing_date, ECOS's listing date as published (blank for three of the four experimental populations, present on a few Resolved Taxon rows). Use it to read population trends against recovery status, e.g. which states have listed salmon: state_abbrs is the comma-separated states each ESU/DPS spans (ECOS has no state column, so this is derived from the ESU name; null where ECOS gives no geography). A snapshot of current status, not a history of listing changes. Pink salmon and landlocked sockeye (kokanee) have no listed units. Join to geo.state_ref by splitting state_abbrs.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/edu/district_ass.tableComment: NCES EDFacts state-assessment proficiency results, district (LEA) grain — the district-grain achievement side of a spend-vs-outcome analysis that f33_district_finance's dollar figures need (see that table's comment, and district_naep_spending's, both of which explicitly note the absence of this data until now). One row per LEA x year x grade (3-12), math and reading/language-arts side by side. Source: Urban Institute's Education Data Portal mirror of NCES EDFacts (educationdata.urban.org, ODC-BY v1.0 license — free redistribution with attribution, no key required), itself sourced from state education agencies' federally-mandated assessment reporting. leaid is the source's own 7-digit NCES LEA ID, already zero-padded — joins directly to ccd_districts.leaid and f33_district_finance.leaid. CRITICAL CAVEAT (source's own documented limitation, not an artifact of this table): each state administers its own assessment with its own standards and proficiency cutoffs, so proficiency rates are NOT comparable across states — only meaningfully comparable within the same state, or as a same-district trend over time. This is a materially weaker comparability guarantee than SEDA's cross-state-standardized scale; SEDA was evaluated as the ideal source for this gap but its data use agreement explicitly bars redistribution ("non-transferable" license) and for-profit use, so it could not be onboarded here. Proficiency shares are reported as a range (..._pct_prof_low/high) rather than a point estimate for small subgroups, per the source's own student-privacy suppression rules — the range narrows as the tested population grows; ..._pct_prof_midpt is the source's own range midpoint, not independently computed here. Virginia's 2016-17 grade 5-8 math results are flagged by the source itself as erroneously low (users referred to VDOE's own reporting instead) — left as-is here since this table mirrors the source verbatim. This endpoint's "all students" aggregate is fetched (race/ sex/disability subgroup breakdowns live on separate sub-endpoints and are out of scope for this table — one table mirrors one source endpoint). Years 2009-2018 and 2020 only; the source has not published 2019 (which errors, not just 404s, on this endpoint) or any year after 2020, so this table cannot track current-year district achievement — only the historical window that overlaps f33_district_finance. All six numeric outcome fields (read/math _num_valid, _pct_prof_low/high/midpt) can carry the source's own negative sentinel codes instead of a real count or percentage — confirmed live via the source's own api-variables endpoint: -1 = Missing/not reported, -2 = Not applicable, -3 = Suppressed data (distinct from the _low/_high range-reporting convention above, which only applies to genuine non-negative percentages). Observed live on this table: -2 and -3 together on 6.3% of rows. These are meaningful metadata, not corrupted data, so this raw table keeps them as-is — any aggregation (SUM/AVG/ratio) MUST exclude negative values first (value < 0), or the sentinel codes get silently averaged in as if they were real percentages.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/lands/padus_fede.tableComment:
USGS GAP Analysis Project's authoritative federal-fee-land layer (Federal_Fee_Managers_Authoritative_PADUS, part of PAD-US) — one row per federal-fee-land polygon (~5,361 features) with owning/managing agency (own_type/own_name, mang_type/mang_name), designation_type, state_abbr, acres, and a simplified WGS84 boundary polygon (geometry_wkt). Federal-fee ownership only (not the full multi-hundred-thousand-polygon PAD-US inventory across all ownership classes — state/tribal/local/NGO/private land is out of scope here). No county_fips column; assigning per-county ownership shares requires a spatial join (DuckDB ST_Intersects) against geo.counties, which is a natural follow-up view, not done at ingest time. Snapshot table with no year partition (refreshed via overwritePartitions). Answers the per-county, cross-agency federal-fee-ownership-share need behind D-054 in one place — own_type/mang_name lets a query filter or compare ownership across USFS, BLM, NPS, and other federal managers without joining three separately-sourced tables. national_forests and nps_units now also carry their own geometry_wkt (their unit's own boundary polygon, captured directly at ingest); blm_field_offices carries only a point location (see its column comment). Also gives disasters.wildfire_perimeters a federal-fee-land layer to compute federal-vs-nonfederal wildfire exposure against (D-176). Source: Federal_Fee_Managers_Authoritative_PADUS/FeatureServer/0 (official USGS GAP Analysis Project ArcGIS org, item v01gqwM5QqNysAAi).
WARNING: do not SUM(acres) for a total federal-fee acreage figure — this layer's own rows are not mutually exclusive despite its "Authoritative" name. Verified live 2026-09-12 directly against the source FeatureServer (not an artifact of this table's ingestion — our own SUM(acres) matches the source's own aggregate query exactly): summing all 5,361 rows gives ~2.25B acres, near the entire land area of the US; even filtering to category='Fee' (ownership, excluding Proclamation boundaries) still gives ~2.10B acres. Grouping by mang_name shows BLM/USFS/NPS/USACE/USBR sums are each close to their independently known real totals (e.g. USFS ~193M acres, matching the National Forest System almost exactly) — the inflation is concentrated in FWS, whose rows include near-duplicate polygon pairs for the same unit at nearly identical (not exactly equal) acreage, e.g. Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument appears twice (310,260,466 and 310,260,380 acres), Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument three times (283,392,764 / 283,392,311 / 88,143,702 for a "Monument Original" sub-record), Mariana Trench NWR twice (50,559,347 / 50,559,316), Arctic NWR twice (19,637,182 / 19,637,012). This is a source data-quality defect in PAD-US's own authoritative layer, not fixable by de-duplicating on any single column here. A query needing a real distinct-area total should use CRS's published federal land figure (~640-650M acres) rather than SUM(acres) on this table, or compute a true union area via ST_Union/ST_Area over geometry_wkt (costly but correct). This table remains the right source for per-parcel attribute lookups, agency/designation filters, and spatial joins (e.g. against geo.counties or disasters.wildfire_perimeters) where exact row-for-row overlap doesn't matter.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/edu/f33_district.tableComment: Census Bureau Annual Survey of School System Finances ("F-33"), individual-unit file — one row per public school district (LEA) per fiscal year. Source: the Census Bureau's published elsec{yy}t.txt comma-delimited file, one per fiscal year (14,088 LEAs in the verified FY2023 file). leaid (source column NCESID) is the Census Bureau's own copy of the NCES LEA ID and joins directly to ccd_districts.leaid and geo.school_districts.sd_lea. Unlike ccd_districts (a staffing/enrollment directory with no dollar figures at all), this table carries the actual survey dollar aggregates: total_revenue_thousand, total_expenditure_thousand, and current_expenditure_thousand are reported in thousands of dollars (the source's own convention, not converted here — see each column's comment); per_pupil_current_expenditure, per_pupil_instruction_expenditure, and per_pupil_support_services_expenditure are the source's own per-pupil dollar figures (PPCSTOT/PPITOTAL/PPSTOTAL), computed by the Census Bureau from fall membership, not derived here. A two-year data lag applies (dataLag: 2 below) — the Census Bureau's most recently published fiscal year is real time minus roughly two years (verified live 2026-08-21: the FY2024 file was the latest published, FY2025 was not yet available). Verified live against the FY2023 file: NCESID is unique per row (0 duplicates) and always 7 digits; none of TOTALREV/TOTALEXP/TCURSPND/ PPCSTOT/ENROLL carried a negative value in that file, so (unlike CCD) this table does not null out negative sentinel codes — none were observed, but this has only been checked for FY2023/FY2024. Per-pupil caution: the file includes tiny and non-operating units (county special-school operators, education service districts, units with an ENROLL of 1-15) whose source per-pupil figures run into the millions of dollars. An unweighted AVG of per_pupil_current_expenditure across all rows is dominated by them; use a median, weight by enrollment (SUM(current_expenditure_thousand)*1000/SUM(enrollment)), or filter on enrollment and unit_type/school_level first.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/weather/coops_st.tableComment: Tidal datum elevations per CO-OPS tide gauge, in meters above station datum (STND), from the Metadata API datums.json. One row per station. Water levels in coops_high_low and coops_tide_predictions are meters above MLLW, so mllw_m converts them to station datum and navd88_m (when published) ties them to NAVD88. Columns hold the current published epoch (epoch, e.g. '1983-2001'): MHHW, MHW, MTL, MSL, MLW, MLLW, NAVD88, plus LAT/HAT where published. A datum a station does not publish is null.

Excludes the source file's self-pair row (every county's block starts by listing itself) — 3,234 excluded in the verified live file, matching the county count. year is a fetch/vintage marker, not a field carried by the source file itself — the Census Bureau publishes one evergreen, non-year-versioned file (confirmed live: county_adjacency2023.txt/2024.txt/2025.txt all 404; only the un-suffixed county_adjacency.txt resolves), so this table is re-fetched under each configured year purely to give the ETL pool a freshness/re-fetch cadence. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/lobbying_act.tableComment: What each filing says was lobbied on, one row per lobbying activity within a filing (usually one to a handful, one per general issue area). `general_issue_code` is one of the 79 issue areas in lobbying_issue_codes (e.g. DEF = Defense, HCR = Health Issues). `description` is the filer's free-text statement of the specific issues, and is where particular bills, regulations and programs are named (for example "H.R. 1" or "FY26 defense appropriations") — there is no structured bill identifier, so matching to the bill_* tables means reading that text. `activity_seq` numbers the activities within the filing from 1 in the order the API lists them. Join to lobbying_filings on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/acs_congr.tableComment: American Community Survey 5-year demographics and economics for every U.S. House district, one row per vintage year x district: total population, median household income, per capita income, median age, unemployment rate, poverty rate, share aged 65 and over, bachelor's degree or higher, foreign-born share, home ownership, median rent and home value, and housing cost burden (renters and mortgaged owners paying 30 percent or more of income on housing). Counts come with derived percentages (the _pct columns; NULL when the denominator is zero). It is a survey, so every figure is a sample estimate (margins of error are not loaded) and medians are NULL where the Census suppresses them. Covers the 435 voting districts plus the non-voting delegates (district 98: District of Columbia and Puerto Rico) for each vintage from 2012; the placeholder rows the API returns for states whose districts are not defined in a vintage (Connecticut, Illinois, Michigan and New Hampshire in some years) are not stored. year is the last year of the 5-year ACS window (year 2022 = ACS 2018-2022). District lines change at redistricting, so each ACS vintage is tabulated on one Congress's lines; the congress column says which (for example 118). Never compare a district across Congresses without checking that congress matches, because the same cd_fips can cover different territory. Do not join geo.congressional_districts on cd_fips alone: its year is a TIGER boundary vintage, so join to the boundary year whose Congress matches. Dollar figures are in inflation-adjusted dollars of the vintage year, so compare incomes across vintages only after adjusting. Use with fec.candidate_district_profile and officials members for district-grain election analysis. Source: Census Data API api.census.gov/data/{year}/acs/acs5 with for=congressional district. Requires CENSUS_API_KEY.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/atc_fa.tableComment: FAA Air Traffic Controller Workforce Plan, Appendix "Facility Staffing Targets" — one row per En Route (ARTCC) or Terminal (Tower/TRACON) ATC facility: its CRWG (Collaborative Resource Workgroup) staffing target, current CPC/CPC-IT/developmental/ total on-board counts, and the plan's 3-year CPC attrition projection (projected_attrition_yr1/yr2/yr3, relative to as_of_date's year — the plan's own column headers are absolute calendar years that shift with every edition, e.g. "2025*/2026*/2027*" in the 2025-2028 plan). ~313 facilities (23 En Route, ~290 Terminal) as of the 2025-2028 plan. Parsed via AtcFacilityStaffingTransformer, which re-derives and cross-checks the PDF's own "En Route Total"/"Terminal Total" subtotal rows against the parsed facility rows and fails loudly on any mismatch. Current-plan snapshot only — FAA does not publish prior editions at a stable URL, so no history is retained upstream to backfill (same treatment as cms_pos_facilities/faa_aircraft_master for a periodically-overwritten single-URL source). Source: FAA Office of Finance and Management, Controller Workforce Plan (Section 221 of Public Law 108-176, as amended). Does NOT carry FAA runway incursion data — no clean self-service source for that was found as of 2026-09 (see govdata-ops#285): FAA's own runway-incursion Tableau dashboard (explore.dot.gov) and its USDOT-datahub Socrata mirror are both inaccessible without credentials/an access grant this corpus does not have.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/state_occup.tableComment: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) state-level employment headcount for science/engineering occupations, cross-industry, all ownership, for OEWS reference years 2010 through the newest published (May 2025 as of the September 2026 build), one partition per reference year. Areas are the 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Virgin Islands (54), keyed by 2-digit FIPS in state_fips. Occupations: 17-0000 (Architecture and Engineering Occupations) and 19-0000 (Life, Physical, and Social Science Occupations) are stable across all years. Software developers are published under whichever SOC code BLS's workbook carries for that year and are NOT remapped, because the definitions differ: 2010-2018 carry two codes, 15-1132 (Software Developers, Applications) and 15-1133 (Software Developers, Systems Software) - sum them for a total; 2019-2020 carry the single code 15-1256 (Software Developers and Software Quality Assurance Analysts and Testers, which folds testers in); 2021 onward carry 15-1252 (Software Developers, testers split out to 15-1253 and not included here). Filter on occupation_code for the era you mean and do not chart the software rows as one continuous series across 2018/2019 or 2020/2021. Computer Occupations as a whole (15-1xxx) is not included - it contains many non-engineering roles. Closes the gap left by patents.patent_grants (inventor location only, excludes non-inventing R&D staff and academic researchers) and research.nsf_herd_by_institution (dollars, not headcount): this is real state-level occupation-count data, the true denominator a research-workforce-concentration question needs. One row per (state, occupation) per reference year; a cell BLS marks ** (suppressed, small-count) has no row, not a zero.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/eia_utili.tableComment: Power-outage frequency and duration by electric utility: EIA-861 reliability indices SAIDI (average minutes of interruption per customer per year), SAIFI (average interruptions per customer per year) and CAIDI (average minutes to restore per interruption, = SAIDI/SAIFI). One row per utility + state + year, annual, data years 2013 onward (published with a ~3-year lag; the newest year is current-3). Sourced from the "Reliability_States" sheet of the Reliability workbook in the same annual EIA-861 ZIP archive that eia_utility_annual downloads (the Reliability_Territories sheet, covering only Puerto Rico/Guam/American Samoa, is out of scope). Each metric is reported under up to three bases: with Major Event Days (storms and other extreme events included), without Major Event Days (normal-conditions reliability), and — IEEE basis only — with loss-of-supply outages removed. Utilities report under either the IEEE 1366 standard (ieee_* columns) or their own non-IEEE standard (other_* columns); the two bases are not comparable, so they are kept in separate column groups and a utility usually fills only one group (the other is null). Reporting is voluntary for many small utilities, so coverage is partial and varies by year. Use the *_without_med columns to compare underlying grid reliability across regions and the *_with_med columns to see storm and extreme-event exposure. There is no statewide roll-up in this table; average across utilities weighting by ieee_customers/other_customers. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_utility_annual via (utility_id, report_year).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/officials/electo.tableComment: Electoral College vote allocation by state, for President and Vice President, from the National Archives (NARA) official per-election results page (archives.gov/electoral-college/{year}) — the government's own record of the Electoral College outcome, not a poll or projection. One row per (year, state, office, candidate). Verified stable across 200 years of live pages (1824, 1876, 1960, 1980, 2000, 2020, 2024): each page has a state-by-state table whose "For President"/"For Vice-President" header groups carry a colspan equal to however many candidates received at least one elector that year — parsed dynamically, not a fixed column count. `candidate_party` is populated only for the winner and the top losing candidate (the only two NARA names on the page's own summary block); other candidates' party is null — NARA's per-election page does not state it for anyone else, including write-in/faithless-elector recipients. Coverage defaults to 1976-2024 (presidential_year_range) — see that dimension's comment for why 1789 isn't the floor. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_name (same caveat as members: DC has 3 electoral votes since the 23rd Amendment but is not itself a state, so 3-elector DC rows will not resolve against a strict state_ref join in years before 1961 if the range is widened).

All political committees registered with the FEC. Includes PACs, party committees, campaign committees, and Super PACs. Contains committee type, designation, connected organization, treasurer, and filing frequency. Source: cm{YY}.zip bulk download (pipe-delimited, no header).
To reach a committee's connected organization FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on fec_committee_id = committee_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the org's LEI/SEC CIK and its committee_id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching connected_org_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses orgs filing under a differently-worded name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: Top 100 procurement-contract recipients by obligated dollar amount for each place-of-performance congressional district x fiscal year — the contracts-only counterpart to usaspending_recipients_by_district. The ranking is computed server-side by USAspending's spending_by_category/recipient endpoint over contract and IDV award types only (award_type_codes A, B, C, D, IDV_A-IDV_E; the same set as usaspending_by_district.obligated_amount_contracts), so grant, direct-payment and loan recipients never occupy a rank. Use this table, not usaspending_recipients_by_district, for "which contractors dominate a district" questions; the all-award-types table ranks universities, health systems and benefit administrators alongside contractors. Same columns, same request shape and same top-100 ceiling (the API's page-size maximum) as usaspending_recipients_by_district: a district with concentrated contract spending is fully captured, one with many small dispersed contractors below the 100th rank is not. An aggregate "MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS" row (null recipient_id/uei/duns) is USAspending's own bucket for sub-reporting-threshold transactions; it is kept as a ranked row and flagged by is_aggregate_recipient. recipient_duns is the endpoint's "code" field (9-digit legacy DUNS-shaped identifier); recipient_uei is USAspending's own UEI when known; recipient_id is USAspending's internal recipient hash. cd_fips matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips exactly. A district's obligated_amount here is not bounded by usaspending_by_district.obligated_amount_contracts for that district/year: the district total nets every recipient's transactions, including large downward de-obligations from recipients outside this table's top 100, while each row here is one recipient's own gross positive sum. YEAR SCOPE: defaults to the 2 most recent complete fiscal years (usaspending_recipient_district_year_range); one API call per (year, district), so GOVDATA_START_YEAR widens it at ~8 minutes per added year. Joins to geo.congressional_districts via cd_fips. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/ (plus one spending_by_geography call per year to enumerate current districts).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/noaa_c.tableComment: NOAA Fisheries FOSS annual landings by state and species, 1950 to current-2. Two collections: 'Commercial' (pounds, dollars; ~3,200 rows/year in recent years) and 'Recreational' (MRIP estimates; fish_count, and pounds where estimated; from 1981). Salmon rows are flagged is_salmon = true with salmon_species (chinook, coho, sockeye, chum, pink, atlantic, pacific_unspecified) and salmon_origin ('coastal' for Alaska, Pacific Coast, New England etc.; 'great_lakes_stocked' for the Great Lakes region, where salmon are stocked non-native fish) — filter salmon_origin = 'coastal' for wild-stock states. Alaska dominates (2022: ~381M lb sockeye, ~216M lb pink, ~82M lb chum); CA, OR, WA also report every year. This is harvest, not run size or escapement: it tracks population trends only loosely, since regulation, closures and market affect it. For Columbia River adult counts see the planned dart_adult_counts table. NOAA publishes several source rows per state + species + source + collection (MRIP and confidential-species rows are split), so there is no primary key: always SUM(pounds), SUM(dollars) or SUM(fish_count) grouped by the keys you need. state_name 'PROCESS AT SEA' (2008+) is landings processed offshore: state_abbr is null and is_state = false, so exclude it from by-state rollups. FLORIDA-EAST and FLORIDA-WEST both map to state_abbr 'FL'. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ref/canonical_or.tableComment:
THE CROSS-SOURCE JOIN TABLE FOR ORGANISATIONS — a wide crosswalk you join on, carrying one nullable foreign key per source alongside a _confidence sibling for each. Use it to define a SET by exact predicate rather than by matching names: "every firm that files with the SEC and holds patents" is `WHERE sec_cik IS NOT NULL AND patents_assignee_id IS NOT NULL`, then a direct join to sec.filing_metadata on cik and patents.patent_assignees on assignee_id. No name matching, no match rate, no candidate review. The resolve_entity tool is for the other case — a person handed you one name and you need its keys.
One row per SOURCE MENTION, not per real-world org: a company whose patents are split across three assignee_ids gets three rows, all sharing one canonical_entity_id and canonical_name, each carrying a different patents_assignee_id. Identity columns (canonical_name, lei, sec_cik) are resolved across the whole org and repeated on every one of its rows, so a cross-source predicate still matches on a single row — and now returns every key a source holds for that org rather than one arbitrary representative. COUNT rows here and you are counting mentions; COUNT DISTINCT canonical_entity_id to count organisations. An org identified only in patents.patent_assignees (never resolved) still gets a row, with lei left null. Nullable FK columns point at each source's natural key; a "_confidence" sibling column (high | low | null) accompanies every FK.
Consumer tables, each carrying a cross-reference back to its own FK column here: fec.committees (fec_committee_id), sec.insider_transactions (sec_reporting_person_cik), sec.institutional_holdings (sec_manager_cik), patents.patent_assignees (patents_assignee_id), patents.trademark_owner (patents_trademark_owner_id), health.fda_drug_approvals (fda_sponsor_name), health.fda_drug_recalls (fda_drug_recalling_firm), health.fda_device_recalls (fda_device_recalling_firm), health.fda_ndc_products (fda_labeler_name), health.cms_open_payments (cms_paying_entity_name), health.clinical_trials (clinical_trials_nct_id), environment.ghg_facilities (ghg_parent_company_name), energy.eia_utility_annual (eia_utility_id), energy.eia_coal_mines (eia_coal_controller_name, eia_coal_operator_name), transport.fmcsa_carriers (fmcsa_dot_number), transport.faa_aircraft_registry (faa_registrant_name), fiscal.exempt_org_master (exempt_org_ein), fiscal.sba_loan_approvals (sba_borrower_name, sba_lender_name), research.nsf_herd_by_institution (nsf_herd_inst_id), edu.ipeds_institutions (ipeds_unitid), law.lobbying_registrants (lobbying_registrant_id), law.lobbying_clients (lobbying_client_id), law.lobbying_foreign_entities (lobbying_foreign_entity_name), law.lobbying_affiliated_organizations (lobbying_affiliated_org_name), law.lobbying_contribution_pacs (lobbying_pac_name), law.lobbying_contribution_items (lobbying_contributor_name, lobbying_payee_name, lobbying_honoree_org_name). Structured-key sources (a per-row id/CIK/EIN already on the source table — fec_committee_id, sec_reporting_person_cik, sec_manager_cik, patents_assignee_id, patents_trademark_owner_id, eia_utility_id, fmcsa_dot_number, exempt_org_ein, clinical_trials_nct_id, ipeds_unitid, lobbying_registrant_id, lobbying_client_id) get an exact join here on that id; unstructured sources (name-only, no per-row id) get the fuzzy-resolved identity this table already carries, so a cross-schema link still avoids re-running the fuzzy match by hand.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/research/nsf_fed.tableComment:
NSF NCSES Survey of Federal Funds for R&D — federal R&D obligations by state or location x funding agency for the latest fiscal year in the publication (Table 60). Values in current USD thousands (note: Table 7's nsf_federal_rd_obligations reports USD millions — different unit, same survey). funding_agency names are normalized to the full department/agency name nsf_federal_rd_obligations already uses (e.g. Table 60's "DOD" header becomes "Department of Defense") so the two tables' agency values line up for a join. Answers "which places get the most federal (and defense) R&D money, by agency" at state grain — the DOD column is this table's state-level view of defense R&D spending; NCSES's own DOD-specific RDT&E table (Table 63, by performer and RDT&E sub-category) is a narrower, DOD-only cut not carried here.
Table 60's per-location "Total" column (sum across the twelve agencies) is not emitted as its own row — same rollup-omission convention as nsf_federal_rd_obligations dropping Table 7's per-agency total column: summing the twelve funding_agency rows for a state recovers it. state_fips is populated only for the 50 states + DC (FK to geo.state_ref); it is null for "All locations" (the national total row, this table's equivalent of nsf_federal_rd_obligations' "All agencies" row), "Outlying areas" (a territories subtotal), the five individual territories, "Other areas", "Offices abroad", and "Undistributed" — none of those resolve to a real state FIPS code, the same best-effort-FK limitation nsf_herd_by_institution.state_fips already documents for territory institutions. "Undistributed" carries a value for only DOD and the grand total; every other agency column is NA there and is not emitted as a row.
Only the publication's latest fiscal year is available at this state x agency grain — like nsf_federal_rd_obligations, each past edition only ever published its own latest FY in this table, so there is no bulk historical backfill of state x agency detail; history accumulates one year per edition going forward. NCSES's own Table 97 (state x year, FYs 2016-24) covers the historical trend at state grain but carries only the all-agency total, no agency split — considered and rejected as a separate table here since it would add a year dimension with no agency detail to join against this table's agency rows.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/ssa_oasdi.tableComment:
SSA "OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County" (Tables 4 & 5, December snapshot) — one row per county per state per year (plus one state-total row per state/year), wide across the 8 beneficiary-type breakdowns SSA publishes: retired workers, spouses/children of retired workers, widow(er)s-and-parents, children of deceased workers (survivors), and — the reason this table was sourced — **disabled_workers_count/amount**, the SSDI caseload/payment figures no other table in this warehouse carries (census.acs_disability is self-reported disability prevalence, a different measure entirely). Sourced for shock-vs-disability-rolls analysis (Autor-Dorn-Hanson style): actual program enrollment against a labor-market shock, rather than a self-reported-prevalence proxy.
Deliberately excludes the same tables' "Aged 65 or older, by sex" (Men/Women) columns — a different demographic cross-tab of the same totals, not part of the beneficiary-type breakdown this table carries.
**Coverage**: 50 states, no DC (SSA's per-state directory listing has no dc.xlsx — confirmed live 13 Sep 2026; DC's OASDI figures exist only in the national/state-level Table 2/3 files, out of scope for this county-grain table) and no territories (PR/VI are published but excluded — no matching geo.counties FK). county_fips is NULL for each state's own total row (SSA labels it "Total, <State>" with its own state FIPS in the ANSI-code column rather than a real county code) — kept, not dropped, matching this schema's kept-total-row convention elsewhere; filter WHERE county_fips IS NOT NULL for a clean county-only sum.
**Akamai UA gate**: www.ssa.gov 403s a blank UA and a plain "GovData/1.0" identifier alike (confirmed live) but passes "Wget/1.21.3" — the opposite of CDC WONDER/BLS's own UA gotchas (those block a self-identifying UA and require blank/curl-like instead). The gate applies to the FIRST request, not just a re-download — both the source: block's headers and SsaOasdiCountyTransformer's own re-download need this UA set explicitly.
minYear 2005 (raw, pre-dataLag) reaches back to the oldest XLSX-format county file, FY2004 (2003 and earlier are PDF-only scans, not worth backfilling).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.schemaJson: {"type":"struct","schema-id":0,"fields":[{"id":1,"name":"county_fips","required":false,"type":"string","doc":"5-digit county FIPS code (FK to geo.counties)"},{"id":2,"name":"county_name","required":false,"type":"string","doc":"County name as reported by USAspending (no state qualifier)"},{"id":3,"name":"obligated_amount","required":false,"type":"double","doc":"Aggregated obligations for the fiscal year (USD), all award types"},{"id":4,"name":"obligated_amount_excl_loans","required":false,"type":"double","doc":"Aggregated obligations for the fiscal year (USD), excluding loan award types '07' (direct loans) and '08' (guaranteed/insured loans). Loans report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's, which inflates obligated_amount for counties with large loan servicers; this figure is a truer measure of spending actually landing in the county. Under the Federal Credit Reform Act, a loan award's obligated amount is its estimated subsidy cost, re-estimated annually, and a downward reestimate or negative subsidy can make a county/year's net loan-type obligation negative; when that happens, this figure is arithmetically larger than obligated_amount, since excluding a negative-valued subset raises the total rather than lowering it.\n"},{"id":5,"name":"obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin","required":false,"type":"double","doc":"obligated_amount_excl_loans further excluding CMS (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services) funded awards — matches usaspending_by_state's column of the same name; see that table's comment for the nationwide evidence. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: Federal spending summarized by place-of-performance county x fiscal year — the county-grain counterpart to usaspending_by_state and the outlay side of soi_income_by_county. From USAspending spending_by_geography (geo_layer=county, all award types, FY expressed as Oct-Sep); ~2,800 counties per year. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Award types span contracts, IDVs, grants, direct payments and loans, so totals are wider than a contracts-only USAspending screen — filter in SQL if you need the A/B/C/D contract slice alone. Carries obligated_amount_excl_loans alongside obligated_amount because loans (award types '07'/'08') report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's. For per-capita, join census.acs_population rather than using USAspending's own population reference, which is 2020 decennial. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/.
s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.columnCommentsJson: {"obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin":"obligated_amount_excl_loans further excluding CMS (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services) funded awards — matches usaspending_by_state's column of the same name; see that table's comment for the nationwide evidence. CMS-funded awards report place of performance at the Medicare Administrative Contractor's location, not the beneficiary's, which concentrates Medicare claims spending into the specific counties hosting MAC contractors' offices.\n","county_fips":"5-digit county FIPS code (FK to geo.counties)","obligated_amount":"Aggregated obligations for the fiscal year (USD), all award types","county_name":"County name as reported by USAspending (no state qualifier)","obligated_amount_excl_loans":"Aggregated obligations for the fiscal year (USD), excluding loan award types '07' (direct loans) and '08' (guaranteed/insured loans). Loans report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's, which inflates obligated_amount for counties with large loan servicers; this figure is a truer measure of spending actually landing in the county. Under the Federal Credit Reform Act, a loan award's obligated amount is its estimated subsidy cost, re-estimated annually, and a downward reestimate or negative subsidy can make a county/year's net loan-type obligation negative; when that happens, this figure is arithmetically larger than obligated_amount, since excluding a negative-valued subset raises the total rather than lowering it.\n"}

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: Top 100 recipients by obligated dollar amount for each place-of-performance congressional district x fiscal year — the recipient/contractor-name counterpart to usaspending_by_district, deferred from that table's build as "materially heavier" until a cheaper mechanism was confirmed live: USAspending's spending_by_category/recipient endpoint accepts a place_of_performance_locations filter shaped {country, state, district_current} and returns a server-side pre-aggregated, pre-ranked (descending by amount) recipient list in a single unpaginated call per district/year -- no per-award pagination needed, unlike UsaSpendingAwardSearchProvider's mechanism for the broadband_*_awards tables. SCOPE: exactly the top 100 recipients per district per year, matching the API's own page-size ceiling (limit=100 is the max; 500 is rejected as "above max '100'") -- not an attempt at every recipient in a district. A district with concentrated spending is fully captured; one with many small, dispersed recipients below the 100th rank is not. An aggregate "MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS" row (null recipient_id/uei/duns) appears in most districts for sub-reporting- threshold transactions USAspending itself buckets together, and is kept as a real ranked row. recipient_duns is the endpoint's "code" field (9-digit legacy DUNS-shaped identifier); recipient_uei is USAspending's own UEI when known; recipient_id is USAspending's internal recipient hash (present even when DUNS/UEI are not, except for the MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS aggregate). cd_fips matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips exactly, decoded the same way as usaspending_by_district. YEAR SCOPE: defaults to the 2 most recent complete fiscal years (usaspending_recipient_district_year_range), narrower than usaspending_by_district's 2018-present default -- this table makes one API call per (year, district) versus that table's 3 calls per year total, so a full 2018-present backfill is ~442x heavier; GOVDATA_START_YEAR overrides for a wider backfill when wanted. Joins to geo.congressional_districts via cd_fips. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/ (plus one spending_by_geography call per year to enumerate current districts, matching usaspending_by_district's own district list rather than a hard-coded one).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/officials/house_.tableComment: U.S. House general-election returns by district and candidate for 24 cycles: 1976 to 2018 from the MIT Election Data + Science Lab (CC0), as the Lab's GitHub repository MEDSL/constituency-returns publishes them (release dated 2019, commit cca36bc159), and 2020 and 2022 from the Federal Election Commission's official results workbooks (source 'FEC' against 'MEDSL' in the source column). 2024 IS MISSING: the Lab's 1976-2024 release (Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/IG0UN2) sits behind a Dataverse guestbook that requires a name, e-mail, institution and position, so an automated job cannot fetch it, and the FEC has not published a 2024 House results workbook (fec.gov lists only the 2024 candidate list and presidential results); 2024 is to be added when the FEC publishes it. One row per candidate per party line per district election round: year, state, district, whether it is a special election or a runoff, the stage (gen general election, pri primary, null when the Lab gave none), the candidate, the party label as published and a normalised major-party field, votes and the published total. Fusion tickets: in states that let a candidate appear on several party lines (mostly New York and Connecticut, also Maryland and South Carolina) each line is its own row with its own votes and the same candidate name, so a candidate's vote is the SUM over rows, never one row; party_major is D or R per line only when that line is the Democratic or Republican party itself (the Conservative or Working Families line of a Republican or Democrat is OTHER on its own row), which is why the views house_race_results and house_seats_won assign a candidate to D or R when any of the candidate's lines is a D or R line. Nothing is merged in this table. Other quirks kept as published: district 0 is an at-large state (at_large=true, cd_fips ends 00); write-ins are lumped in rows with candidate null (candidate_kind write_in_aggregate) and vote buckets (Blank Vote, Scatter, Over Vote, Other) are candidate_kind residual; uncontested races carry candidate_votes 1 and total_votes 1 (uncontested=true), which is a placeholder, not a count; 39 2018 rows are marked unofficial; the file is not a Congress roster, so a candidate who won a special election appears under special=true. Redistricting: results are by the district map in force that year (new maps in 1982, 1992, 2002, 2012, and the court-ordered mid-decade Texas redraws of 1996 and 2006, which appear as extra special, runoff and null-stage rounds; 2022 uses the 2020-census maps), so a (state, district) pair is a different place before and after a redistricting year and is not comparable across them without a crosswalk. Louisiana 2002 district 5 is a runoff round after an open first round (Louisiana 2020 district 5 likewise, FEC). FEC ROWS (2020, 2022), read from the workbook's 'US House Results by State' sheet with strict parsing (an unknown header, state, party label or subtotal fails the fetch; every district's rows must sum to the sheet's own district total and the winner flag must name the leader): only the 50 states' general elections are loaded, stage gen, from the General Votes and General Runoff columns; primaries, primary runoffs and the per-party and combined subtotal rows are not. The delegates (DC, AS, GU, MP, PR, VI) are not loaded, as the Lab's series has none. Vacancy-filling special elections are not loaded (the Lab's series has none either; they sit on the FEC 'Special Elections' appendix), except Indiana 2 in 2022, whose unexpired-term election is on the main sheet beside the full-term one and is special=true. Fusion tickets (New York, Connecticut, Oregon, South Carolina, Alaska): each party line of a candidate is its own row with its own votes, as in the Lab's data; the FEC 'Combined Parties' rows and combined-total columns are not read. Oregon and a few other states publish one combined total under a combined label (D/WF, D/IP/WF), which is one row whose party_published joins the lines with '/'. A combined label is credited to the major party only when it contains exactly one of D or R and the candidate has a primary or convention entry; otherwise it is OTHER (Connecticut 4 2020 Brian Merlen, labelled D/IP, is OTHER). Write-ins: the FEC's 'Scattered', 'All Others' and 'Anyone Else' lines are write-in aggregates (candidate null, candidate_kind write_in_aggregate, writein true); named write-in candidates (party W) are kept as candidate rows with writein true and party null, which is more granular than the Lab's 2018 rows (one named write-in in all of 2018). Party labels are the workbook's own codes resolved through its 'Party Labels' sheet and lower-cased (party_published 'democratic', not the Lab's 'democrat'); party_major D covers D, DFL and DNL (Democratic-Nonpartisan League), R covers R, everything else is OTHER; the star after a code (R*, D*) marks a convention nominee and is dropped; W(x)/x (a primary write-in who is on the general ballot as x) is x; two codes are aliased to the label the sheet defines (AVP to APV, Approval Voting Party, in 2020; GS to GSA, God Save America, in 2022). A candidate taken off the ballot by a court (the '#' result of a Montana 2020 Green) has no row. Uncontested races: the FEC prints 'Unopposed' for Florida 25 (2020) and Florida 5 and Louisiana 4 (2022), which become the Lab's marker, candidate_votes 1 and total_votes 1 (uncontested true, a placeholder); other races whose opponents did not appear carry the FEC's real counts. At-large districts are district 0 (FEC 00), as the Lab. Runoffs: a General Runoff value makes a second round, runoff true, beside the first round (runoff false), as the Lab does for Louisiana. Ranked-choice contests (Maine 2 and Alaska at-large in 2022): candidate_votes and total_votes are the LAST round's counts of the instant runoff tabulation, as the Lab's Maine 2 in 2018 is, with ranked_choice true and the first-choice count in first_choice_votes; eliminated candidates carry 0 in the last round, and write-ins that the tabulation excludes (the Scattered line) have no row, so the round total is the tabulation's. Rows from the Lab have ranked_choice null (its 2018 Maine 2 rows are last-round counts, unflagged). A candidate who appears in two districts (a redistricted incumbent) is two unrelated rows; nothing is merged across districts or years, and the FEC file carries no stable candidate key that the table keeps. total_votes is, in both sources, the sum of every row of the round including write-ins. DISCONTINUITY at 2018/2020: party_published vocabulary changes (the Lab's 'democrat' to the FEC's 'democratic'; use party_major across the boundary); candidate names are the FEC's first and last name columns joined as 'first last' (a suffix the FEC puts in the first-name column stays there: 'Martin, Jr. Lemelle'), not the Lab's spellings, so names do not join across the boundary; version_date is null on FEC rows (the workbooks carry only a month, October 2022 for 2020 and February 2025 for 2022, named in source_release); unofficial is false on FEC rows (an official-results publication); the Lab's per-year set of vote buckets (Blank Vote, Scatter, Over Vote) does not exist in the FEC data; the FEC rows are the states' certified results while the Lab's may carry unofficial flags. Joins: state_fips to geo.state_ref.state_fips; state_name to officials.members.state_name; members.district equals district and the Congress seated after the election is (year - 1786) / 2 (year 2018 is Congress 116); cd_fips (state FIPS + 2-digit district, 00 at large) matches geo.congressional_districts cd_fips for the same map vintage, which geo carries from 2021 only. Candidate-level joins to members would be name matching and are not attempted (the Lab carries no bioguide id). Sources: https://github.com/MEDSL/constituency-returns (1976-2018-house.csv; codebook and license on the Dataverse record doi:10.7910/DVN/IG0UN2) and the FEC workbooks federalelections2020.xlsx and federalelections2022.xlsx under https://www.fec.gov/introduction-campaign-finance/election-and-voting-information/.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/regional_fo.tableComment: Monthly CPI-U Food at Home (SAF11) index level (not seasonally adjusted, base 1982-84=100) for the 4 U.S. Census regions (Northeast, Midwest, South, West). Sibling to regional_cpi (all items) — same 4 region area codes, item SAF11 instead of SA0. Food at Home subcomponents and Food Away From Home are not published sub-nationally by BLS (confirmed against cu.series — only the top-level SAF11 aggregate has region/metro rows); for those, see food_cpi (national only). For metro-area food CPI, see metro_food_cpi.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fisheries/mrip_r.tableComment: NOAA Fisheries MRIP (Marine Recreational Information Program) recreational catch by year x wave x state x fishing mode x area fished x species, 1981 to the latest published year. Measures: harvest in fish (landings_fish = claimed + reported), fish released alive (released_fish), total catch (total_catch_fish) and harvest weight (landings_pounds, landings_kg), each with a standard error and percent standard error. Companion to noaa_commercial_landings, whose collection = 'Recreational' rows carry only an annual state x species fish_count and pounds; this table adds wave, mode, area, the harvest-versus-released split and the uncertainty. Coverage is the Atlantic and Gulf coasts from Maine to Mississippi plus Hawaii (17 states in 2022); Louisiana, Texas, the Pacific coast and Alaska are surveyed by state agencies and are absent from recent years, so use noaa_commercial_landings for them. Florida appears under two sub-regions (South Atlantic and Gulf of America), so state_abbr alone does not identify a row. species_code is MRIP's 10-digit species code and species_name its common name in upper case; it does not carry the ITIS tsn used in noaa_commercial_landings, so match species by name (approximate). Estimates are survey-based: check *_pse (above 50 = unreliable) and never treat a null as zero. One row per wave x state x mode x area x species; sum landings_fish or total_catch_fish across waves/modes/areas for annual totals (standard errors do not add). Source files are replaced in place when estimates are revised. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/scotus_slip_.tableComment: Every opinion of the U.S. Supreme Court in the "Opinions of the Court" listing on supremecourt.gov, Court terms 2017 to the current term: the cases the bound volumes in scotus_reports_cases do not cover (term 2017's opinions before March 21, 2018 are in volume 583 there). One row per case, partitioned by `year`, the term (October of `year` to the following summer). `holding_summary` is the Court's own one-line statement of the holding from the listing. `docket_numbers` are read from the opinion (a consolidated case lists every docket its footnote numbers; `listing_docket` is the one the listing gives). `disposition` is derived from the opinion's syllabus, so `disposition_source` is always opinion_text; it uses the vocabulary of scotus_reports_cases (Affirmed (includes modified), Reversed, Reversed and remanded, Vacated and remanded, Affirmed and reversed (or vacated) in part [and remanded], Dismissed as improvidently granted) and can also be Reversed in part and remanded, Reversed in part, vacated in part, and remanded, Vacated in part and remanded or Reversed in part and remanded in part where the Court affirmed no part, or Application granted / Application denied for an order on an emergency application (a docket such as 24A884). It is null for an original-jurisdiction decree. `us_citation` is null while the listing shows only a volume and print part (609/2) and has no page yet. `opinion_text` is the full text as extracted from the PDF, in which the "fi" ligature loses its "i" (e.g. "affrmed", "fnal"). `author_initials` is PC for a per curiam and otherwise the justice's initials as the listing prints them.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/eia_capac.tableComment: EIA Form 860M generator inventory, one annual snapshot per snapshot_year. Captures planned additions and planned retirements with capacity (nameplate, summer, winter, energy storage). Transformer parses the XLSX directly. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_power_plants via plant_id. GRAIN — READ BEFORE AGGREGATING: this is a CUMULATIVE SNAPSHOT, not a change log. One row per generator per snapshot_year, so a single addition or retirement event REAPPEARS in every later snapshot it survives into — measured live, additions with change_year 2020-2024 appear in 1 to 6 distinct snapshot_years each. The row count therefore grows every year by construction (25,986 in 2016 to 38,359 in 2025) without any new events. SUMming nameplate_capacity_mw across snapshot_year multiplies every event by the number of snapshots it appears in: for change_type='Addition' and change_year 2020-2024 that is 746,721 MW across 18,688 rows, against 5,236 real generator-years — roughly 3.6x EIA's own published additions of ~40 GW/yr. To total real capacity change, first reduce to one row per (plant_id, generator_id, change_year) — e.g. pick the newest snapshot_year per generator with QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY plant_id, generator_id, change_year ORDER BY snapshot_year DESC) = 1 — and only then aggregate. snapshot_month is NULL on every row: only the December file is ingested, so the column carries no information and must not be used to disambiguate snapshots.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fedregister/fr_d.tableComment: Text of each Federal Register document, one row per document_number (joins to fr_documents). summary is the preamble SUMMARY paragraph (a few hundred characters, the agency's own statement of what the document does); body_text is the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section of a rule, proposed rule or notice — background, discussion, the agency's reasoning and responses to comments, usually thousands of characters and up to about a million for the largest rules — and the whole text of a presidential document (executive order, proclamation, memorandum), which has no such section. The regulatory text itself (amendatory instructions and CFR text) is part of body_text when the XML places it inside SUPLINF. summary is NULL for documents without a SUMMARY (most presidential documents); body_text is NULL for the few documents with no body element. Use this table for text search; use fr_documents for title, agency, CFR references, RIN and dates.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/broadband.tableComment: ARRA (American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, 2009) broadband stimulus award-level grants — one row per award, with recipient, dollar amount, performance period, and recipient location (county-grain via county_fips). Covers both ARRA broadband programs: NTIA's Broadband Technology Opportunities Program (BTOP, CFDA 11.557, middle-mile/institutional/public-computing infrastructure) and RUS's Broadband Initiatives Program (BIP, CFDA 10.855, last-mile rural infrastructure). DQ-validated 2026-09-11: real awards under both programs (e.g. BTOP's EAGLE-NET ALLIANCE, $100.6M, Broomfield County CO; BIP awards to rural school districts and health clinics). Closes the ARRA third of the "federal broadband award geography" sourcing gap alongside broadband_reconnect_awards (ReConnect) and broadband_bead_state_allocations (BEAD, state-grain only); RDOF/CAF-II remain FCC/USAC-administered, not CFDA awards — see broadband_high_cost_disbursements (carrier/state grain — RDOF has no address-level source publicly available) and broadband_caf_deployment_locations. A one-time, closed-out 2009-2011 program: full crawl each run (not year-partitioned), whole result set small enough (low thousands of awards across both CFDA numbers, DQ-confirmed: 241 for 11.557 + 2,454 for 10.855) that a full refresh is cheap. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (program_numbers filter, award types 02/03/04/05 — grants only, no contracts/loans in either program).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/ssa_benef.tableComment: SSA OASDI and SSI beneficiary counts and total benefit dollars by county x program x benefit type x year — the largest federal mandatory-spending stream, geo-keyed and comparable per county against soi_income_by_county and usaspending_by_state. SSA publishes only multi-sheet XLSX reports on a WAF-protected host that 403s non-browser clients, so the provider fetches the Wayback-archived workbook (oasdi_sc / ssi_sc) and parses the per-state county tables (Table 4 counts + Table 5 dollars for OASDI; Table 3 for SSI). The ANSI Code column carries the county FIPS directly. beneficiary_type is a mutually-exclusive published category (OASDI leaves sum to 'total'). Amounts are the December total monthly benefits, in whole USD; avg_monthly is per beneficiary. SSI per-category dollars are not published (only the total).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/bills.tableComment: Every bill and resolution introduced in the U.S. Congress, one row per bill, from the GovInfo Bill Status bulk data (the same data the Congress.gov API serves). Partitioned by `congress` (e.g. 119 = 2025-2026) and `bill_type`: hr (House bill), s (Senate bill), hjres / sjres (joint resolutions), hconres / sconres (concurrent resolutions), hres / sres (simple resolutions). `bill_number` is unique only within (congress, bill_type). `latest_action_text` / `latest_action_date` are the best single status signal (e.g. "Became Public Law No: 119-21.", "Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary."); `law_type` and `law_number` are populated only once a bill is enacted. Sponsor columns carry the first listed sponsor. `action_count` and `cosponsor_count` count the rows in bill_actions and bill_cosponsors for the same bill; committee referrals, subjects, text, related bills, amendments, votes, titles, summaries, CBO estimates, committee reports and notes are in the other bill_* tables (bill_committees, bill_subjects, bill_text_versions, bill_related_bills, bill_amendments, bill_recorded_votes, bill_titles, bill_summaries, bill_cbo_cost_estimates, bill_committee_reports, bill_notes, ...). The current Congress changes daily at the source and is re-pulled monthly; completed Congresses are static. The source publishes the 108th Congress onward; the default GOVDATA_START_YEAR (2010) starts at the 111th.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/lobbying_con.tableComment: The individual contributions listed on LD-203 reports, one row per item: who gave (`contributor_name`, often SELF for an individual lobbyist), who received it (`payee_name`, typically a campaign committee or PAC) and in whose honor (`honoree_name`). `contribution_type` is feca (contribution to a federal candidate, committee or party), he (honorary expenses) and so on, decoded in lobbying_contribution_item_types. Join to lobbying_contribution_reports on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/fdi_direct_.tableComment: BEA Direct Investment (DI) statistics from the Multinational Enterprises (MNE) dataset. Balance-of-payments direct investment: position (stock), income, financial transactions, equity, debt instruments, and reinvested earnings. Inward (foreign investment in the U.S.) and outward (U.S. investment abroad), by partner country or by industry. Tall layout: one row per statistic (series_id) x area/industry (row_code) x year.
s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/fdi_direct_.columnCommentsJson: {"row_code":"Country or industry code (matches the classification partition)","column_code":"Statistic sub-breakdown code","row_label":"Country or industry name","table_scale":"Units for data_value (e.g. 'Millions of Dollars', 'Thousands of Employees')","column_label":"Statistic sub-breakdown name","data_value":"Statistic value in the units given by table_scale (null when BEA suppressed the value)","series_name":"Human-readable statistic name","time_period":"Data year (YYYY)","series_id":"BEA MNE series identifier. The MNE dataset is a long-format cube: one row per (series_id, row_code, column_code, time_period), and each row carries its own label in series_name, so read series_name rather than memorizing codes — there is no separate series reference table. Ingestion requests SeriesID=all, so the loaded domain is whatever BEA publishes for the requested direction and classification; enumerate it with SELECT DISTINCT series_id, series_name. Common values: 30 = U.S. direct investment position abroad, 22 = foreign direct investment position in the U.S., 27 = direct investment income. ALWAYS filter on series_id before aggregating — positions (stocks), income, and financial flows share this column and are not additive. Scale comes from table_scale, not from the raw data_value.\n"}

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/nws_zo.tableComment: NOAA National Weather Service zone-to-county correlation file — one row per (NWS public forecast zone, county) pair, ~4,800 rows covering ~3,980 zones. Crosswalk for storm_events rows with cz_type = 'Z', whose county_fips is NULL: join storm_events.state_fips = state_fips AND storm_events.cz_fips = zone. A zone covering several counties appears once per county (~10% of zones), so the join fans out; count rows per (state_abbr, zone) to allocate. Built from every NWS release still downloadable (weather.gov/gis/ZoneCounty lists the current one; the Mar 2024 file is also still served): each zone takes its counties from the newest release containing it, recorded in release, so zones NWS has since retired stay joinable. Zones absent from all of those releases (e.g. Guam, parts of Louisiana) are not covered. zone_lat/zone_lon are NWS's zone centroid, repeated on each county row. Source: weather.gov (NWS), keyless.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/environment/wate.tableComment: USGS county-level water-use census for 2015 (usco2015v2.0.csv, USGS data release https://doi.org/10.5066/F7TB15V5, cited in USGS Circular 1441) — one row per county (3,223 counties/county-equivalents, all 50 states + DC/PR/USVI). Reports total population and, per sector (public supply, self-supplied domestic, industrial, irrigation, livestock, aquaculture, mining, thermoelectric power), withdrawals in million gallons per day (Mgal/d) broken out by groundwater/surface-water and, where applicable, fresh/saline; thermoelectric is further split into once-through vs. recirculating cooling with power generated (GWh) and consumptive use. total_withdrawals_mgd/total_fresh_groundwater_mgd/total_fresh_surfacewater_mgd/ total_saline_withdrawals_mgd are cross-sector sums; total_consumptive_use_partial_mgd covers only irrigation + thermoelectric (the only sectors USGS estimates consumptive use for in this release) — not a full-sector total, per USGS's own "Partial" naming. Verified live 2026-09-21: summing total_withdrawals_mgd nationally gives 321.7 Bgal/d, matching USGS Circular 1441's published 322 Bgal/d 2015 total; Monroe County, MI (DTE's Monroe coal plant, Lake Erie once-through cooling) shows 1,791 Mgal/d thermoelectric withdrawal and 25,252 GWh generated, consistent with that plant's known ~3,400 MW nameplate capacity. IMPORTANT CAVEAT — this is a WITHDRAWAL-CAPACITY proxy for "does this county have a track record of sector water use," not a legal water-rights/allocation record: it does not show unallocated headroom, permitted-but- unused rights, or legal availability under drought curtailment. USGS publishes this compilation once every 5 years (Circulars 1950-2015 then per-category ScienceBase releases from 2020); this table currently holds only the 2015 vintage — the last year published as one combined all-sector county file — see the dataset_type note above for why later vintages are not mechanically addable. Joins geo.states via state_fips and geo.counties via county_fips.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/national_wa.tableComment:
National establishment counts, employment levels, total wages, and average weekly wage from BLS QCEW (Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages), broken out by NAICS industry code (industry_code) and ownership sector (own_code) — the national-aggregate counterpart to state_wages. Sources BLS's own published national total for each industry/ownership cell, not a sum of state_wages rows: summing state_wages across states systematically understates industries where several states suppress the cell for disclosure reasons (disclosure_code='N') — confirmed live 2026-09 on NAICS 3352 (household appliance manufacturing, own_code='5'/private): only ~39-46 of 51 jurisdictions report a non-suppressed value in state_wages, giving a state-sum employment figure of 32,911-36,179 for FY2023, while this table's own national row for the same industry/ownership cell (area_fips='US000', agglvl_code='16') reports 63,044 — matching BLS's own published national CES/QCEW figure for that industry directly. Use this table whenever a query needs a true national total for a specific industry or ownership cross-section; state_wages remains the source for state-level detail.
agglvl_code at the national grain: '10' = grand total (all industries, all ownerships, own_code always '0'); '11'-'15' = successively finer NAICS depth (sector through 6-digit) at own_code='0' (all ownerships combined); '16'-'18' = the same NAICS depths broken out per ownership sector (own_code='1'/federal, '2'/state, '3'/local, '5'/private — pick the sector via own_code, matching state_wages' own_code semantics); '94'/'95' are two standing summary rows at industry_code='10' for own_code='8' (federal government excluding some categories) and '9' (total government), not industry detail. Any industry-specific national query must pin agglvl_code together with industry_code and own_code, the same discipline state_wages documents for its own agglvl_code column.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fec/ca_contribut.tableComment: Itemized contributions received by California state candidates, parties, and ballot-measure committees (Cal-Access Form 401/460/465 Schedule A/C/I), including intermediary/conduit and loan-interest detail. One row per contribution line item; PK is (filing_id, amend_id, line_item, form_type) — an intermediary contribution files a companion record (form_type I) alongside its underlying contribution (form_type A) sharing the same filing_id/amend_id/line_item, so form_type is required to disambiguate. rec_type is 'RCPT' for the vast majority of rows but a real minority (~0.006%) are 'E530' — Form 497 24-hour/10-day late contribution reports, co-mingled into the same TSV by the source. Source: Cal-Access full-database export, RCPT_CD.TSV member. Covers 2000-present. A small number of source rows (<0.001%) have a NULL filing_id/amend_id/line_item — a known Cal-Access export data-quality gap, not a transform defect.

Cumulative monthly snapshot sharded across four regional files (eo1..eo4), fetched and concatenated in one pass. subsection_code 03 = 501(c)(3); ruling_date/tax_period are YYYYMM. Anchors exempt_org_990 on EIN. Dollar amounts fold the sign into the value. Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/eo{1..4}.csv.
