s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/medicare_.tableComment:
CMS "Medicare Geographic Variation - by National, State & County" Public Use File — one row per (year, geography, age group), 2014-2024. Sourced to close the Medicare fee-for-service spending-by-state gap #67 identified: USAspending's award-based federal-spending totals omit ~$1.0T (FY2023) in Medicare FFS payments entirely, since they never post as discrete awards.
**Curated subset, not the full PUF**: CMS's source file has ~250 columns — payment, standardized-payment, and utilization-rate detail broken out separately for inpatient, outpatient, ASC, SNF, IRF, LTCH, home health, hospice, ED, procedures, tests, imaging, DME, ambulance, and several Prevention Quality Indicator (PQI) admission-rate measures, each further split by raw vs. per-capita vs. per-user vs. pct-of-total. This table carries only the headline totals (total/inpatient/outpatient/DME/hospice payment and per-capita figures) plus beneficiary counts and Medicare Advantage participation — the columns the spending-by-state question needs. Extending to the full category breakdown is a straightforward follow-up (same source, same grain) if a future need requires inpatient-specific or PQI-specific detail.
**Standardized vs. raw payment**: total_medicare_stdz_payment removes each area's geographic price adjustment (wage index, GPCI, etc.), isolating utilization intensity from local price levels — the figure to compare *how much care* an area's beneficiaries use. total_medicare_payment is the actual dollar amount paid — the figure for a spending/fiscal question. Use stdz for utilization comparison, raw for spending totals.
**Suppression**: CMS suppresses small-cell values (denoted '*' in the source) for privacy — these parse to NULL here via TRY_CAST rather than a fabricated 0. Small counties and the '<65'/'>=65' age-group splits are the rows most often affected; 'All' age-group rows are rarely suppressed.
**Geography**: geo_level is 'National', 'State', or 'County'. geo_fips is the 2-digit state FIPS or 5-digit county FIPS (FK to geo.state_ref/geo.counties); NULL for National rows and for the 'ZZ' catch-all state code CMS uses for unknown/foreign/territory beneficiaries (fully suppressed in every year checked). age_level is 'All', '<65', or '>=65' — filter to 'All' for a single row per geography/year unless the age split itself is needed.
**URL drift caveat**: CMS's data.cms.gov file path encodes an upload date (sites/default/files/2026-04/...) that changes when CMS re-publishes the combined file with a new year appended. Re-verify the URL against the dataset's landing page (data.cms.gov/provider-summary-by-type-of-service/medicare-geographic-comparisons/ medicare-geographic-variation-by-national-state-county) if this table stops updating.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/lobbying_act.tableComment: The federal bills each lobbying activity names, one row per (activity, Congress, bill type, bill number), derived from the free-text `description` in lobbying_activities by fixed rules, so a join to the bill_* tables does not need each user to parse text. `bill_type` uses the bills table's values (hr, s, hjres, sjres, hconres, sconres, hres, sres) and `bill_number` is unique only within (congress, bill_type): join to bills on all three. Recognised forms: "H.R. 1", "HR 1", "HR1", "S. 123", "S123", "H.J.Res. 5", "S.J.Res. 5", "H.Con.Res. 5", "S.Con.Res. 5", "H.Res. 5", "S.Res. 5", with an optional "No.". `congress` comes from an explicit tag next to the reference ("H.R. 1 (118th)", "H.R. 1, 118th Congress", "118th Congress: H.R. 1") and `match_basis` is explicit_congress_tag; with no tag it is the Congress in session on the filing's posting date and `match_basis` is inferred_from_posted_date — drop those rows for a strict analysis, since an untagged number may name an older Congress's bill with the same number. A tag naming a Congress later than the one in session at posting cannot be right: that row has a null `congress` and `match_basis` unresolved_tag, and is kept rather than guessed. Not captured: numbers that only follow a list ("H.R. 1, 2 and 3" yields H.R. 1) and spelled-out names ("House Bill 1"). The same bill and Congress is one row per activity, with an explicit tag winning over an inferred one. This table does not judge whether a reference is the sponsor's bill or an older bill of the same number beyond what the tag and posting date allow. Precision, hand-checked against the description text in a 2026 Q1-Q3 sample (12 explicit, 40 inferred rows): every row was a real bill reference; the 2 explicit rows with a wrong or missed tag were fixed by the rules above, and 1 of the 40 inferred rows named an older Congress's bill (the Congress is only as good as the posting-date inference, so treat inferred rows as probable, not certain). `reference_text` is the matched text. Join to lobbying_activities on (filing_uuid, activity_seq). Partitioned by `year` and `quarter` like lobbying_activities: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time). A past partition never changes; the current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records); the extraction is this project's. The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/census/acs_housi.tableComment: Occupied housing unit counts split by tenure (owner-occupied vs renter-occupied) and age of householder, from ACS 5-year table B25007 ("Tenure by Age of Householder"), at state and county levels. Age bands match B25007's published structure: 15-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-74, 75-84, 85+ (nine bands, identical for owners and renters). Lets a generation-cohort ownership analysis be computed directly in-engine — same age band, same vintage — rather than relying on third-party CPS reprocessing. A true generation-matched historical series still requires stitching multiple ACS vintages across the cohort's aging trajectory; this table exposes the single-vintage building block.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/officials/member.tableComment: Every House/Senate member per Congress they served, from the Congress.gov API per-Congress member list endpoint (the modernized Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress). One row per (bioguide_id, congress) pair — a member serving multiple congresses has multiple rows. `terms_json` is the member's full chamber service history (all congresses, not just this row's), as a JSON array of {chamber, start_year, end_year}. `party_name` is the party held in this row's Congress (from the detail endpoint's partyHistory; a mid-Congress switch resolves to the party held when that Congress ended), so a party switcher's rows differ by Congress. Chamber is not a column: `district` is null for senators and non-null (0 = at-large) for House members. A Congress holds more rows than seats because mid-Congress replacements each get a row, so party control is not a plain COUNT. `state_name` and `district` are as reported by the per-Congress list endpoint. Coverage is bounded by `congress_range` (see dimension_values comment) — not full 1789-present history by default. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_name (full name; geo.states is a year-vintaged boundary snapshot and not a valid FK target — see constraints below). Territorial delegates (Puerto Rico, Guam, etc.) won't resolve against state_ref, which covers 50 states + DC only.

Operations of U.S. affiliates of foreign firms (inward) and foreign affiliates of U.S. firms (outward): employment, total sales, total assets, value added, net income, capital expenditures, R&D expenditures, and affiliate trade in goods. FDA medical device recall (enforcement) actions, one row per cfres_id. Complementary to fda_drug_recalls, but carries recall_status (Terminated/Ongoing) and root_cause_description instead of a Class I/II/III severity field — this table has no classification column. s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/phmsa_.tableComment: PHMSA gas distribution operators' annual report (Form PHMSA F 7100.1-1), one row per (report_year, operator, commodity) — the per-mile normalization denominator for phmsa_gas_distribution_incidents (join on operator_id + report_year). Same data.transportation.gov bulk-file route as phmsa_hazardous_liquid_mileage (catalog resource aemm-7pyq, the same multi-commodity "href" pointer; this fetches the Gas Distribution file attachment). Unlike the hazardous-liquid annual report, this source publishes one flat CSV per year (not split into lettered Parts), but the column set still drifts slightly year to year (278 cols in 2017-2022, 274 in 2023, 300 in 2024 — all differences are trailing excavation-damage-detail columns not used here); the ETL's zip-merge aligns columns by name across files with differing headers, not position, so this is safe. Confirmed live: the 2020-2024 files carry comma-only padding lines (81-145 per year) that parse into all-NULL rows without a rowFilter, same defect class as phmsa_hazardous_liquid_mileage. An operator can file more than one commodity row per year (Natural Gas, Propane Gas, Landfill Gas, Synthetic Gas, Hydrogen Gas), so report_number — not operator_id + report_year — is the unique key. total_services (individual customer service-line count) has no analog in the hazardous-liquid table; gas distribution systems are sized by service count as well as main mileage. 2010-2016 exist only as whole-workbook XLSX files (one per year, single sheet "GD AR <year>") rather than separate per-year CSVs; a PhmsaGasDistributionMileageHistoricalTransformer responseTransformer parses those years via POI and appends them to the 2017+ CSV text extractPattern already produces, so this table now covers 2010-present. Confirmed live: the 2010-2014 workbooks (237 cols) carry no COMMODITY field at all — it was only added starting with the 2015 workbook (278 cols, matching the 2017+ header exactly) — so commodity is NULL for 2010-2014 rows rather than guessed; every other target field (including report_number as a clean unique key) is present for the whole 2010-2016 span.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/ahrf_phys.tableComment: HRSA Area Health Resources File (AHRF), county-level release — one row per U.S. county (fips_st_cnty; 3,235 counties/county-equivalents in the 2024-2025 release, including territories). AHRF ships raw physician/population COUNTS only — no per-100k rate column exists upstream — so primary_care_physicians_per_100k and total_active_physicians_per_100k are computed here from the matched count and population columns. primary_care_physicians is HRSA's "Phys, Primary Care, Patient Care" measure: non-federal MD+DO physicians in patient care, excluding hospital residents and physicians aged 75+, sourced from the AMA Physician Masterfile. total_active_physicians is all non-federal active MDs plus DOs (all specialties, not primary-care-filtered). AHRF is a wide file — each variable is a family of year-suffixed columns (e.g. phys_nf_prim_care_pc_exc_rsdt_23, phys_nf_prim_care_pc_exc_rsdt_22, ...) rather than one row per year, and each annual release adds a newest-year column while keeping older ones. AhrfPhysicianSupplyTransformer scans the header at load time for the highest-numbered suffix present and records which data year it picked in physician_data_year / population_data_year — so a stale suffix never silently ships; the years advance automatically as HRSA adds columns in future releases. rural_urban_code is the USDA ERS Rural-Urban Continuum Code (1-9; lower = more urban), useful for physician-shortage/rural-access analysis alongside the supply counts. Source: data.hrsa.gov/data/download, "Area Health Resources Files" county CSV distribution.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/ers_commodity.tableComment: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns: per-acre (field crops) or per-cwt/ per-head (milk, cow-calf, hogs) cost of production vs. gross value of production, by commodity, USDA Farm Production Region (7 regions plus a U.S. total), and year (1996-present). Tall — one row per commodity x region x year x category x item. category groups rows into gross value of production, operating costs, allocated overhead, costs listed (their sum), net value (value less total costs listed), production practices (irrigated/dryland share), and supporting information (price, yield). Covers 9 field crops (corn, cotton, barley, peanuts, rice, sorghum, oats, soybeans, wheat) and 8 livestock categories (milk, cow-calf, and 6 hog production types). Updated twice yearly (preliminary annual estimates in May, final in October). Complements ers_farm_income (farm-SECTOR aggregates) and nass_crop_production (physical production/value, no cost side) with the per-crop cost-vs-revenue breakdown neither provides.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/gas_pipel.tableComment: U.S. natural gas transmission pipeline network — one row per pipeline segment (~32,900 segments nationwide), sourced from EIA and mirrored as a public ArcGIS FeatureServer under Esri's Federal_User_Community org (the layer's own listing: "checked monthly for updates"; EIA's own Energy Atlas hosting for this layer is not currently available — verified live, not the PA Department of Health's Pennsylvania-only re-clip of the same underlying EIA data found during initial research, which this table does NOT use). Confirmed nationwide via a spot-check of returned segments across Illinois, Minnesota, Arizona, Utah, Nevada, and Colorado — not just the Marcellus-region subset the PA mirror is limited to. geometry_wkt carries each segment's own WGS84 line geometry (LINESTRING or, for a small number of segments, MULTILINESTRING); length_m is EIA's own projected segment length in meters, not a WGS84-degree approximation. No county field is present at the source — join geometry_wkt against geo.counties (DuckDB ST_Intersects) for county-grain rollups, following the same spatial-join pattern as lands.county_federal_fee_land_share; see energy.county_gas_pipeline_presence for a pre-built rollup. pipeline_type is Interstate or Intrastate (EIA/PHMSA classification); status is "Operating" for every row in the live source despite the field's stated Active/Inactive/Abandoned vocabulary — a real constant, not a transform bug. A small fraction of segments (~0.2%, confirmed live) carry no geometry at all; geometry_wkt is null for those rather than the row being dropped, so segment_id stays a complete FID census.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_morta.tableComment: CDC/NCHS mortality statistics at the state level (annual data also includes a United States total row). Unions annual (bi63-dtpu: NCHS leading/113-cause deaths and age-adjusted rate per 100,000, 2000 US standard population, 1999-2017) and weekly provisional data (source_type=weekly) from two Socrata vintages of the same "AH Weekly Death Counts by State and Select Causes" series: 3yf8-kanr (no COVID columns; loaded here from 2014 through 2019, not just 2018-2019 as its nickname might suggest) and muzy-jte6 (2020-2023, adds COVID-19 columns). Weekly rows carry an All Cause total for every state-week 2014-2023, plus a COVID-19 underlying-cause count for each 2020-2023 state-week (two rows per state-week in those years). The annual series with cause_name 'All causes' ends at 2017, so weekly All Cause rows are the only all-cause series after 2017. The 2020-2023 weekly rows cover the 50 states, DC, New York City, Puerto Rico and a United States total, by state of occurrence. source_type distinguishes annual from weekly, and age_adjusted_rate is populated for annual rows only.
s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_morta.columnCommentsJson: {"week_ending_date":"Week-ending date; weekly rows only, null for annual","cause_name":"Cause-of-death name; NCHS leading cause (annual), or All Cause / COVID-19 (weekly; COVID-19 for 2020-2023 only)","full_cause_name":"Detailed cause name (NCHS 113-cause for annual; All Cause / COVID-19 detail for weekly)","year":"Data year of deaths; MMWR year for weekly rows","age_adjusted_rate":"Age-adjusted deaths per 100,000 (2000 US std pop); annual only","source_type":"annual or weekly","state":"State/jurisdiction; annual includes a United States total row","deaths":"Number of deaths for the cause/period (weekly rows: All Cause total or COVID-19 underlying-cause deaths, per cause_name). NULL means CDC suppressed this week's count under its small-cell privacy threshold (typically <10), NOT that zero deaths occurred — confirmed live (2,296 weekly state-level COVID-19 rows carry this NULL). Do not treat NULL as 0 in a SUM; a plain SUM(deaths) already excludes these rows correctly by SQL's own NULL-skipping behavior, but an explicit COALESCE(deaths, 0) or an outer join that backfills a missing week with 0 would silently convert real suppression into a false zero. CDC signals weekly COVID-19 suppression in the source with a companion flag_cov19ucod field on weeks where the underlying-cause count field is absent; CdcMortalityResponseTransformer maps both to NULL. A zero COVID-19 count is a real zero.\n"}

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/trade_impor.tableComment: Monthly U.S. goods imports by HS-10 commodity and origin country, curated to the HS-2 chapters carrying critical-mineral and metal commodities (25 salt/earths/stone, 26 ores/slag/ash, 28 inorganic chemicals, 72-76 iron/steel/copper/nickel/aluminum, 81 other base metals incl. tungsten/molybdenum/cobalt/rare-earth metals) — follow-up to trade_imports/trade_exports: Census's GEN_QY1_MO/UNIT_QY1 quantity fields are unpopulated ("0"/"-") at the HS-6 grain those tables fetch, but ARE standardized at HS-10 (verified live: I_COMMODITY=2504101000 -> GEN_QY1_MO=2263678 UNIT_QY1=KG; the HS-6 prefix 250410 returns 0/-). A full un-curated HS-10 month is too large to fetch wholesale (far more rows than the ~213k/month at HS-6); this table scopes to 9 chapters via Census's own I_COMMODITY prefix-wildcard filter (I_COMMODITY={chapter}*, verified live to behave as a true prefix match, not exact-match) — one fetch per (year, month, chapter), ~1k-17k rows each. Tall layout: Census interleaves individual- country rows with its own world-total and trade-bloc/continental aggregate rows in the same response — filter geo_level = 'country' before summing value_usd or quantity, or the total silently multiplies by every bloc/continent a country also belongs to (plus the world total). quantity_unit varies by commodity within a chapter (KG, T, NO, M2, DOZ, ...) — never sum quantity across differing quantity_unit values.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/nfip_m.tableComment: FEMA's own property-level NFIP repetitive-loss aggregation — one row per structure that has ever met a Repetitive Loss (RL) or Severe Repetitive Loss (SRL) threshold (~240k rows), with total_losses (paid-claim count since 1978) and most_recent_date_of_loss per property. Ingested as the authoritative answer to "how concentrated are flood claims in properties that flood repeatedly": nfip_claims has no property/building identifier, and lat/lon (rounded to 1 decimal) or census_tract are both far too coarse to derive a per-property repeat-claim count from claims alone (many distinct properties share one rounded coordinate or tract). This table is FEMA's own property-level rollup, not a proxy. nfip_rl/nfip_srl are the insurance-claims-based categories; fma_rl/fma_srl are the separate Flood Mitigation Assistance grant-eligibility categories (see column comments for the exact thresholds) — a property can qualify under either, both, or neither pair. mitigated_indicator/insured_indicator reflect current status as of as_of_date, so a property already bought out or demolished can still appear (per FEMA's own dataset description). census_block_group is not carried here: FEMA's own file renders it in lossy scientific notation (e.g. "2.2055E+11" for a 12-digit code), destroying the digits after the leading county FIPS — county_fips (from fipsCountyCode, full precision) is the reliable location join instead. Distinct from nfip_claims (realized paid losses, one row per claim, not per property) and nfip_policies (policy-term coverage/premium transactions). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: fema.gov/api/open/v1/NfipMultipleLossProperties.

EIA Form 861 annual electric utility survey. Covers all electric utilities, retail power marketers, and energy service providers. Fields include entity type, NERC region, service type, customer counts and sales by sector (residential, commercial, industrial, transportation), revenue, peak demand, and net generation. One row per utility + year. The transformer downloads and parses the annual ZIP archive of XLSX files from EIA. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
To reach a utility's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on eia_utility_id = utility_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the utility's LEI/SEC CIK and its utility_id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching utility_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses utilities filing under a differently-worded name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/research/nih_awa.tableComment:
NIH award-level grant microdata from RePORTER's POST /v2/projects/search API — one row per funded project per fiscal year, with award_amount and activity_code (mechanism, e.g. R01/F32), closing the gap that nsf_federal_rd_obligations/nsf_herd_by_institution leave open: those are agency/institution TOTALS, not individual-award size or count. Answers "is award size/count shifting toward fewer-bigger or more-smaller grants" directly.
RePORTER caps every query at offset<=14999 (confirmed live — a higher offset returns a plain error, not an empty page), and a single fiscal year runs ~85,000 awards nationally, well over that. NihReporterAwardsProvider slices by agency_ic (NIH Institute/Center) to stay under the cap per (year, IC) query — the largest IC (NCI) was ~13,200 awards in a single year when this was checked live, versus the ~15,000 ceiling — and walks each slice's own pages to exhaustion, so the (year, IC) union is the true complete population for that year, not a sampled prefix. Not NCSES data (unlike the rest of this schema — see the schema-level header note); NIH itself, added because this schema is where funding- input data already lives.
Coverage starts at FY2010 and follows the calendar forward, so an award-size trend spans more than a decade of NIH funding. RePORTER's data goes back to FY1985; lower minYear on the year dimension to reach further back. NSF's counterpart at the same grain is nsf_award_projects; the two share fiscal_year and a recipient state, and together cover the bulk of federal research grants.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/research/nsf_her.tableComment:
NSF NCSES Higher Education R&D (HERD) survey — R&D expenditure by academic institution × S&E field × funding source × year, from the per-year institution microdata (herd{year}.csv, a tall EAV file). Projects the two R&D-expenditure question families: "Federal expenditures by field and agency" (funding_source=Federal, federal_agency=column) and "Nonfederal expenditures by field and source" (funding_source=column). 2008-2009 use NCSES's predecessor questionnaire (different question text, no per-field nonfederal-by-source cross-tab); NsfHerdTransformer maps both vintages into this same shape (see its class javadoc). Values in USD thousands. Carries the IPEDS UnitID crosswalk into edu (2010+ only — not published pre-2010) and state_fips into geo; the finest-grained NCSES table (institution grain). For the state×year rollup used in the patents-per-R&D-dollar productivity join, see research_herd_rd_by_state_year.
For 2010+ rows, prefer joining ipeds_unitid directly to edu.ipeds_institutions — it is already on this row. For pre-2010 rows (no ipeds_unitid) or a cross-schema identity beyond edu, join ref.canonical_org_entity on nsf_herd_inst_id = inst_id instead of matching the institution name as text.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/cdc_wonde.tableComment: Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) report counts by year reported and state/territory, from CDC WONDER database D8. CAUTION: VAERS is a raw, unverified self-reporting system — reports can be filed by anyone (patients, providers, manufacturers) with minimal validation, a report being present does NOT establish that the vaccine caused the reported event, and the data includes known data-entry errors (e.g. a small number of reports dated before VAERS existed in 1990). Use for signal detection / reporting-volume trends only, never as evidence of causation. Public access to full VAERS detail was expanded May 2025; older third-party WONDER "saved queries" for this database predate that change and are no longer valid — this table's fields were rebuilt against the current form.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/ag/nass_crop_pro.tableComment: USDA NASS weekly Crop Progress report, national and by state, for field crops — CONDITION (percent of acreage rated very poor / poor / fair / good / excellent) and PROGRESS (percent planted, emerged, blooming, harvested, ...). One row per (week_ending, commodity, class, practice, data item, geography). Filter statisticcat_desc and unit_desc: the condition units sum to 100 for a given week, commodity and geography; progress units do not. week_ending is the Sunday the survey week closes (NASS releases the report the following Monday), so it joins directly to weekly series such as cftc.cot_disaggregated_futures.report_date. The current season loads as it is published. Season coverage varies by commodity and state (e.g. corn April-November) and the ratings series begin per commodity in the 1980s or later; NATIONAL rows carry the acreage-weighted US rating, which cannot be rebuilt from state rows. Annual county/state production, yield and area are in nass_crop_production.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/broadband.tableComment: FCC Connect America Fund Phase II (CAF-II) subsidized broadband buildout — one row per deployed location (near-address grain: lat/long, street address, and 15-digit census_block, whose first 5 digits are the county FIPS), filed annually by the carrier as it completes buildout milestones. Sourced from USAC's own open-data platform (opendata.usac.org, dataset r59r-rpip — the same underlying "CAF Map" data usaspending itself can't reach, since CAF-II is an FCC/USAC Universal Service Fund disbursement, not a CFDA federal-assistance award), filtered to fund_type IN ('CAF II', 'CAF II Auc') — this dataset also carries ACAM/ACAM II/CAF-BLS/RBE/AK Plan rows for other high-cost programs, out of scope here. RDOF rows do not yet appear in this feed (RDOF winners are still mid-buildout under a 10-year plan; only carrier-level disbursement/location-count totals exist for RDOF today, not individual addresses) — closes the CAF-II third of the "federal broadband award geography" sourcing gap, not RDOF. ~4.8M rows across 2015-2025 (2016-2021 the heaviest reporting years). Joins to geo.counties by taking the first 5 digits of census_block.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: Every federal assistance transaction (grants, cooperative agreements, direct payments, loans, insurance) by federal fiscal year (Oct-Sep; year = the fiscal year of action_date), one row per award action (award x modification), from USAspending's award data archive (all-agency Assistance Full files, FY2007 onward; roughly 6-9 million rows per recent year, about 115 million in all). Carries the recipient (UEI, DUNS, parent, name, address, county and congressional district), the program (cfda_number = Assistance Listing / ALN), the awarding and funding agency, place of performance, period of performance and dollars. federal_action_obligation is additive across rows (sum it for obligations by year, recipient or program); total_obligated_amount and total_outlayed_amount_for_overall_award are cumulative per award and repeated on every row of that award, so take one row per assistance_award_unique_key (the latest action_date) before summing outlays. Outlays are only available as that cumulative per-award figure. Loan rows report the subsidy cost as the obligation and the face value in face_value_of_loan. recipient_uei joins to fac_audits.auditee_uei (Single Audit filings) and cfda_number to fac_federal_awards (see the view fac_awards_vs_usaspending); recipient_duns joins the pre-UEI FAC years; there is no EIN in USAspending, so EIN reaches it through fac_audits. Individuals' awards carry a masked recipient and no UEI. Contracts are not in this table. Source: files.usaspending.gov/award_data_archive (URL resolved through api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/bulk_download/list_monthly_files/).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/transport/bts_ts.tableComment: Monthly national freight and passenger activity from BTS's Transportation Services Index dataset (Socrata bw6n-ddqk), Jan 2000 to the latest release (about a 2-month lag), one row per month. truck_d11 is the seasonally-adjusted Truck Tonnage Index (the American Trucking Associations for-hire tonnage series, the monthly national truck freight volume measure); alongside it are the Freight/Passenger/Combined TSI, seasonally-adjusted rail carloads and intermodal, waterborne tonnage, pipeline barrels, air freight ton-miles and VMT, plus Federal Reserve industrial production and manufacturing output for direct freight-vs-output comparison. Index values are 2000=100 (truck_d11 and TSI); other columns carry their own units in the column comment. Values are revised in later releases, and the ETag gate refetches the whole ~320-row series each time it changes. Source: data.bts.gov/resource/bw6n-ddqk.json.

Stores CVSS v2 and v3.1 base scores with their vector strings, plus a CVSS v4.0 base score (no v4.0 vector column), vuln_status, and pipe-delimited CWE IDs. The canonical CVE registry — see kev_catalog for the smaller subset known to be actively exploited, and vulnerability_cwes for the CVE-to-CWE junction.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/environment/ocea.tableComment: Monthly sea surface temperature (SST) and SST anomaly for the 11 U.S.-adjacent NOAA large marine ecosystems (LMEs), 1985 to present — one row per (LME, month). Source is the NOAA Coral Reef Watch CoralTemp v3.1 5 km monthly mean analysis served by the CoastWatch ERDDAP dataset NOAA_DHW_monthly_Lon0360 (keyless; public domain, cite NOAA Coral Reef Watch). The grid is thinned server-side to every 5th cell (0.25 degrees) and each cell center is assigned to the first LME polygon containing it (NOAA LME boundary set, simplified; point-in-polygon on the cell center); cells over land or outside every LME, and cells with no SST, are dropped. mean_sst_c and mean_sst_anomaly_c are unweighted means of the cell values in degrees Celsius. The anomaly is the monthly mean SST minus the CoralTemp monthly-mean climatology, whose baseline period is 1985-1990 plus 1993 (derived from 1985-2012 data and re-centered; see https://coralreefwatch.noaa.gov/product/5km/methodology.php), so recent anomalies are against a mid-1980s reference and run warm. cell_count is the number of valid 0.25 degree cells averaged, so area is roughly cell_count x ~690 km2 at 40 N. Region key: lme_number / lme_name (the fisheries regional_ecosystem names follow the same LME naming) and state_abbrs, a comma-separated list of the coastal states whose adjacent waters the LME covers (the Caribbean Sea LME spans the whole Caribbean basin, not just PR and VI, and the Beaufort Sea LME extends into Canadian waters). Months NOAA has not yet published return no rows. Pairs with the fisheries landings and salmon tables on lme_name, year and month.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fec/individual_c.tableComment: Itemized individual (donor-level) contributions to federal committees exceeding $200 per cycle. transaction_type spans both ordinary contributions (15/15E/22Y) AND code 10 (giving to Super PACs/Hybrid PACs/nonfederal soft-money accounts) — 10 is uncapped and by dollar volume is typically the single largest code (2024: $6.2B vs. $3.6B for 15), so a query that only knows 15/15E/22Y silently undercounts total giving, especially per-donor. See the transaction_type column comment for the full code list. Largest FEC dataset (~4-5GB per cycle, 20M+ records); contains donor name, employer, occupation, amount, date, and memo text (vectorized for inferred relationship discovery). Distinct from committee_contributions (committee-to-candidate money) and intercommittee_transactions (committee-to-committee transfers). Source: indiv{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header). DIRECTION: committee_id is the RECIPIENT committee (join fec.committees on committee_id + year for its details) and contributor_name is genuinely the donor (individual) here — unlike committee_contributions/intercommittee_transactions, this table's column names match their roles. PERFORMANCE: always filter on the year partition first — this is the largest FEC table by row count and an unfiltered or non-partition-filtered aggregate can exceed a 30s query timeout. Donor-name lookup ("what has this person given") is NOT currently supported even with a year filter: contributor_name has no sort order/clustering, so a name-filtered scan of one year's partition (tens of millions of rows) still exceeds the 30s statement timeout in production — confirmed 2026-09-29 (see kenstott/govdata-ops#780). Do not attempt a name-filtered query against this table until #780's remediation (a donor-summary table or sortOrder+ reprocess) lands.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/disasters/storm_.tableComment:
NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database — one row per storm event detail record (tornadoes, floods, hurricanes, hail, winter storms, wildfires, etc.) with event magnitude, direct/indirect deaths and injuries, and property/crop damage (damage_property, damage_crops; converted from K/M/B notation to USD). Partitioned by year, streamed from the per-year NCEI gzip CSV. Joins to geo.counties and to disaster_declarations by county+date overlap.
state_fips/county_fips (D-284): NOAA's own STATE_FIPS uses 4 non-standard codes for Puerto Rico/Virgin Islands/Guam/American Samoa (99/96/98/97) instead of their real Census FIPS (72/78/66/60) — remapped so these join geo.state_ref like every other state. Confirmed live this also recovers county_fips for Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands specifically (their CZ_FIPS values are real Census municipio/district codes once paired with the corrected state code — 7,905/7,905 and 60/60 county-type rows now join geo.counties). Guam and American Samoa's CZ_FIPS values are NOT real Census codes even after the state remap (e.g. Guam's storm_events rows use "002"/"003"/"006", but geo.counties only carries a single unified "66010"; American Samoa uses "002"/"003" against geo.counties' real five-district "010"-"050") — NOAA evidently numbers these two territories' zones on its own internal scheme with no Census county-equivalent mapping. Puerto Rico has a smaller, closed variant of the same problem: 6 codes (72002/72004/72006/72008/72010/72012, 331 rows total across 2004-2008 only) are NWS PR public-zone codes NCEI stamped as CZ_TYPE='C' rather than 'Z' — interleaved with real odd-numbered municipio FIPS (72001, 72003, ...) in the same 2004-2008 window before NCEI switched to real-FIPS-only from 2009 onward. Because a zone spans multiple municipios there is no 1:1 remap that could recover a real municipio code from a zone code, so StormEventsStreamingTransformer explicitly nulls county_fips for these 6 values instead of emitting an unresolvable FIPS. A second, unrelated residual: for a small number of county-type rows in the 50 states (confirmed live: 72 in Alaska across this table's full history, 49 in Georgia isolated to Jan-2025-published rows, 1 in Louisiana), CZ_FIPS itself doesn't match any real county FIPS at all — e.g. Georgia's early-2025 batch pairs real county names like "WALKER" with CZ_FIPS values ("2", "4", "6"...) that belong to no actual Georgia county. Confirmed this is wrong in NOAA's own published file, not an artifact of this ingest. Neither residual has a crosswalk that recovers the correct FIPS from what NOAA actually published; a LEFT JOIN to geo.counties silently drops these rows, expect the gap rather than treating it as a join bug.
Zone-coded events (cz_type = 'Z', ~41% of rows and ~half of 2011-2023 property damage — mostly hurricane, wildfire, coastal flood and storm-surge events) have NULL county_fips by design: NOAA records an NWS zone number, not a county. cz_fips keeps that zone number and nws_zone_county maps it to counties: join on s.state_fips = z.state_fips AND s.cz_fips = z.zone. About 10% of zones span more than one county, so the join can fan out one event into several counties — damage summed after that join double counts unless allocated (e.g. divide by the zone's county count). Zone numbering follows the current NWS file; zones NWS retired or renumbered since the event do not match.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/federal_out.tableComment: OMB Historical Table 3.2 ("Outlays by Function and Subfunction") — federal outlays broken out by OMB's 20 canonical budget-function codes (050 National Defense, 570 Medicare, 650 Social Security, 900 Net Interest, etc.), FY1962-2031 (recent years are OMB's own budget-cycle actuals; later years are the President's Budget estimates, see is_estimate). Closes the gap left by fiscal.usaspending_by_state/county/district (place-of-performance geography, not function) and this schema's own federal_debt/ treasury_yields (debt levels and borrowing cost, not spending composition) — none of those answer "how much of federal spending is Social Security vs. defense vs. net interest." Subfunction-level detail (e.g. 051 Department of Defense-Military) is not ingested here — a follow-up sourcing task if a future question needs finer grain. Values in current-dollar millions, not inflation-adjusted. Source: OMB's Historical Tables page (whitehouse.gov/omb/historical-tables/); the download URL embeds the current budget cycle and changes annually — re-derive it from that landing page's own hist03z2 link if this table's source URL ever 404s, same caveat class as disasters.wildfire_risk_by_county's WRC download.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/soi_incom.tableComment: IRS Statistics of Income individual income tax statistics aggregated by ZIP x AGI size class (agi_stub) x tax year. The finest-grained revenue table; joins to geo ZIP crosswalks for county/CBSA rollups and to census ACS income. All dollar amounts are in THOUSANDS of dollars and may be negative. agi_stub brackets: 1=$1-25k, 2=$25-50k, 3=$50-75k, 4=$75-100k, 5=$100-200k, 6=$200k+. zip_code = 00000 rows are the state total for that state (kept; exclude in views that sum ZIPs). Source (per year): irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/{YY}zpallagi.csv.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/econ/industry_oc.tableComment: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) national employment headcount cross-tabulated by industry AND major occupation group (not seasonally adjusted) — the industry-specific cut of OEWS that state_occupation_employment cannot provide (that table is state-level and cross-industry only). Answers "within industry X, what is the occupation mix" and "has the occupation mix shifted between industry X and industry Y" questions state_occupation_employment structurally cannot: BLS publishes industry-specific OEWS estimates only at the National level, across sector/3/4/5-digit NAICS industry codes (~430 industries after excluding the cross-industry total) crossed with ~23 major SOC occupation groups (2-digit group + '0000', e.g. '150000' Computer and Mathematical Occupations) — detailed 6-digit SOC codes are not loaded here to keep row count bounded; state_occupation_employment remains the source for detailed-occupation, cross-industry headcounts. One row per (industry_code, occupation_code) per published reference year. Decode industry_code with econ_reference.oe_industries and occupation_code with econ_reference.oe_occupations. Small industry x occupation cells may be suppressed by BLS (row absent, not zero).

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/energy/eia_coal_.tableComment:
MSHA MinesProdYearly coal mine production data (pipe-delimited CSV ZIP). The transformer downloads MinesProdYearly.zip and Mines.zip, performs an inner join on mine_id, filters to coal mines (COAL_METAL_IND = 'C'), and returns one row per mine + subunit + year. Includes mine demographics, operator/controller identity, geographic location (lat/lon, county, state), mine type and status, production volume in short tons, employee count, annual hours, labor productivity, and average seam height (underground mines). The transformer filters by the requested year dimension. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
controller_name and operator_name are unstructured (no per-row id) — mine_id is per-mine, not per-company. ref.canonical_org_entity carries each as an already-resolved identity (eia_coal_controller_name, eia_coal_operator_name, each with an LEI when matched); join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/edu/ipeds_instit.tableComment:
NCES IPEDS Institutional Characteristics (HD survey) directory. One row per institution per year. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips (pad integer to 5-char string). Enrollment is NOT here (IPEDS EF survey). Tuition/fees are NOT here — see ipeds_tuition table (academic-year-tuition endpoint). college_scorecard joins via unitid = college_scorecard.id. ipeds_completions and ipeds_financials join via unitid.
To reach an institution's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on ipeds_unitid = unitid — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the institution's LEI/SEC CIK and its unitid sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching inst_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses institutions filing under a differently-worded name.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/law/bill_recorde.tableComment: Roll-call votes recorded against a bill or one of its amendments, one row per vote, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `url` is the House Clerk or Senate roll-call XML that holds the member-by-member result. A vote on an amendment has `amendment_type` and `amendment_number` set; a vote on the bill itself has them NULL. `action_date` and `action_text` are those of the bill or amendment action that recorded the vote (for example "Passed/agreed to in House: On passage Passed by the Yeas and Nays: 220 - 213"). `full_action_name` (e.g. "Passage of a Measure") appears only on votes listed directly on the bill in a few older files, which then have NULL action fields. One roll call can be cited by several actions on the same bill, so there is one row per citation and no unique key.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/health/va_medica.tableComment:
Veterans Health Administration (VHA) medical-facility roster with geocoding — station number, facility type, name, address, city, state, ZIP, and (lat, lon). Static-snapshot table: the whole layer is re-paginated and the partition overwritten each run; history lives in Iceberg snapshots. Enables drive-time / distance-to-nearest VA-medical-facility computation for a veteran-population question (e.g. joined to census.acs_veterans by state or county). Cross-checked live 2026-09-13 against the real Palo Alto VA Medical Center (STA_NO='640'): city=Palo Alto CA 94304, LAT/LON = (37.40132, -122.13911), matches the real 3801 Miranda Ave campus location.
Facility-type coverage (facility_type, 1696 rows total, confirmed live 2026-09-13): PCCBOC 414, OOS 400, VTCR 318, MSCBOC 289, VAMC 171, MVCTR 73, DRRTP 15, HCC 12, CLC 2, MCS 2 — these 10 codes are the complete set present in the layer. VTCR (Vet Center) and MVCTR (Mobile Vet Center) together are 391 rows (23% of the table) — Vet Centers ARE included here, correcting this table's earlier sourcing research, which had assumed (without checking the live facility_type distribution) that this HIFLD layer was VHA-medical-only. None of the 10 codes correspond to a National Cemetery Administration or Veterans Benefits Administration facility, so this layer does not carry cemeteries or benefits regional offices; VA's own Facilities API (developer.va.gov, self-service API key required) would be needed to add them.
Source: the HIFLD-hosted mirror of VA's VAST (VHA Site Tracking) database at services2.arcgis.com/VFLAJVozK0rtzQmT — an individually-hosted ArcGIS mirror re-verifying VA's public-domain federal data (same accepted mirror pattern as housing.opportunity_zones). Re-verify-if-404s risk: if the HIFLD mirror stops serving this layer, the fallback is VA's own developer.va.gov Facilities API, which needs an instant-issuance self-service key and would broaden coverage to Vet Centers, cemeteries, and benefits offices in return.
street_address (from ArcGIS S_ADD1) is populated almost exclusively for Vet Center/Mobile Vet Center rows (VTCR 307/318, MVCTR 73/73 — confirmed live) — every other facility_type, including VAMC itself (1/171), mostly carries city/state/ZIP without a street. Use (city, state, zip) as the mailing/routing granularity when street_address is missing; (lat, lon) remain populated for every row and are the reliable input for distance computation.

Loans report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's, which inflates obligated_amount for districts with large loan servicers; this figure is a truer measure of spending actually landing in the district. Under the Federal Credit Reform Act, a loan award's obligated amount is its estimated subsidy cost, re-estimated annually, and a downward reestimate or negative subsidy can make a district/year's net loan-type obligation negative; when that happens, this figure is arithmetically larger than obligated_amount, since excluding a negative-valued subset raises the total rather than lowering it.
"},{"id":7,"name":"obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin","required":false,"type":"double","doc":"obligated_amount_excl_loans further excluding CMS (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services) funded awards — matches usaspending_by_state/ usaspending_by_county's column of the same name; see those tables' comments for the nationwide evidence. CMS-funded awards report place of performance at the Medicare Administrative Contractor's location, not the beneficiary's, which concentrates Medicare claims spending into whichever district hosts a MAC contractor's office.
"},{"id":8,"name":"obligated_amount_contracts","required":false,"type":"double","doc":"Obligations from procurement contract/IDV award types only (codes A, B, C, D, IDV_A-E) — the actual "federal contract spending" figure (D-278). obligated_amount above is ALL award types combined (contracts + grants + loans + direct payments + other assistance) and is not a contract-spending figure by itself; a caller who specifically means contracts should use this column, not filter/derive from obligated_amount.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/fiscal/usaspendi.tableComment: Federal spending summarized by place-of-performance congressional district x fiscal year — the district-grain counterpart to usaspending_by_state and usaspending_by_county. From USAspending spending_by_geography (geo_layer=district, all award types, FY expressed as Oct-Sep); one call per fiscal year returns all 442 districts in a single unpaginated response (435 numbered districts, at-large single-district states as district "00", and non-voting delegate districts for DC/PR/GU/VI/AS/MP as district "98"). Carries obligated_amount (all award types) alongside obligated_amount_excl_loans and obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin for the same reasons as usaspending_by_state/usaspending_by_county — see those tables' comments for the nationwide evidence. obligated_amount_contracts isolates procurement contract/IDV awards specifically (D-278), since obligated_amount alone mixes contracts with grants, loans, and direct payments indistinguishably. cd_fips matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips exactly (state FIPS + district number), no crosswalk needed. Does NOT carry a recipient/contractor-name dimension — USAspending's award-level search (spending_by_award, already used by UsaSpendingAwardSearchProvider for the broadband_*_awards tables) is paginated per-award rather than pre-aggregated, so a full recipient-concentration table across all 442 districts is a materially heavier build, deliberately left as a separate follow-up rather than folded into this one. For per-capita, join census.acs_population rather than a stored figure here. Joins to geo.congressional_districts via cd_fips. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/.

","cd_name":"USAspending's own district label, e.g. "PA-04"","obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin":"obligated_amount_excl_loans further excluding CMS (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services) funded awards — matches usaspending_by_state/ usaspending_by_county's column of the same name; see those tables' comments for the nationwide evidence. CMS-funded awards report place of performance at the Medicare Administrative Contractor's location, not the beneficiary's, which concentrates Medicare claims spending into whichever district hosts a MAC contractor's office.
","state_abbr":"2-letter USPS state abbreviation, decoded from USAspending's display_name","obligated_amount":"Aggregated obligations for the fiscal year (USD), all award types","cd_fips":"4-digit congressional district code (state FIPS + district number), matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips","district_number":"District number as text (e.g. "04"); "00" means an at-large single-district state, "98" means a non-voting delegate district (DC, Puerto Rico, Guam, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands)
","obligated_amount_excl_loans":"Aggregated obligations for the fiscal year (USD), excluding loan award types '07' (direct loans) and '08' (guaranteed/insured loans). Loans report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's, which inflates obligated_amount for districts with large loan servicers; this figure is a truer measure of spending actually landing in the district. Under the Federal Credit Reform Act, a loan award's obligated amount is its estimated subsidy cost, re-estimated annually, and a downward reestimate or negative subsidy can make a district/year's net loan-type obligation negative; when that happens, this figure is arithmetically larger than obligated_amount, since excluding a negative-valued subset raises the total rather than lowering it.
"}

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/crime/cde_police.tableComment:
FBI CDE LEOKA (Law Enforcement Officers Killed and Assaulted) Police Employee data at AGENCY-year grain — one row per (ori, year) with the same total-sworn-officer and civilian counts that cde_police_employment carries at state grain, plus the county the FBI itself publishes for each ORI. Sourced to close the gap #266 identified: no table gave county-grain sworn-officer headcount over time, so a policing-intensity-vs-crime-rate analysis at county grain was structurally impossible from this schema.
Roll-up: GROUP BY county_name (or JOIN cde_agencies via ori for canonical county naming and geo.counties FK linkage) collapses this to county-year. GROUP BY state_abbr recovers cde_police_employment's totals — both are LEOKA-derived, but the state-grain table pulls the CDE API's state aggregate directly while this table sums per-agency reports, so tiny differences can appear on years with late-arriving amendments between the two API paths' snapshots.
**Source**: two live endpoints, chained in the DataProvider — api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde/agency/byStateAbbr/{state} gives each state's ORI list plus FBI's own county label per agency, then cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/pe/agency/{ori}?from=Y&to=Y returns that agency's PE record for the year. Confirmed live 2026-09-14 (Nome PD AK0010600 FY2020 = 9 male + 1 female officers, matching a real small Alaska department).
**NULL-response filtering**: the pe/agency endpoint returns a fully-null envelope for ORIs that never reported PE data in the queried year. Those rows are dropped rather than stored as all-NULL counts — a real "no data" from LEOKA is the same as "agency did not report", not a distinguishable state worth carrying. Row count per year therefore reflects only agencies that actually reported.
**County-name convention**: FBI publishes county as UPPER-CASE with hyphens ('KENAI PENINSULA'), 'NOT SPECIFIED' for state-police/university/airport/tribal agencies that don't sit in a single county, and occasional multi-county strings for agencies spanning two counties. Kept verbatim from the source; a downstream view can normalize to geo.counties.county_name (title case) via UPPER() / TRIM() plus the NOT-SPECIFIED filter.
**API key**: uses API_DATA_GOV env var (same key already used by cde_agencies). The PE endpoint itself is keyless; only the agency-list call routes through api.usa.gov.

s3://govdata-parquet-v1/weather/climate_.tableComment: NOAA CDO Monthly Climate Normals (NORMAL_MLY dataset, 1981-2010 period). One row per station per month (all 12 months per station). Each state is fetched, paged and pivoted as one unit and stored as its own partition. Values are in metric units (°C, mm). CDO's raw response is in its "standard" units (tenths of °F for temperature, hundredths of an inch for precipitation, tenths of an inch for snowfall); ClimateNormalsTransformer converts each to metric with the correct formula per field (absolute temperatures use (°F-32)×5/9; the two stddev columns are a delta and use ×5/9 with no -32 offset). county_fips is joined from ghcnd_stations_with_county. Requires NOAA_CDO_TOKEN. Static dataset — update logic is not needed until NOAA releases a new 30-year period. Cross-references ghcnd_stations_with_county via station_id.
